**Root-caused before proposing anything, per the standing verify-never-assert rule:** traced the live client code (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`'s `runIntentPipeline`) — every message first hits Marcus's `ci-routing-intent` (Skill on his `channel-intelligence` Capability, the only agent/capability pairing that uses it, confirmed via `agent_capability_assignments`). Its schema allows `qa`/`theory`/`forecast`/`correct`/`escalate`, but its `method` field (read live from Supabase, not assumed) only ever defined how to distinguish qa/theory/forecast — zero guidance for escalate, and `output_desc` was null. An open-ended catalog question falls into the undefined bucket by default. `escalate` is a hard client-side dead end (`runIntentPipeline` returns the placeholder immediately, the agent loop never starts) — upstream of `AA-182`/`AA-186`'s fix, which only ever mattered once Marcus routed a question to `qa` in the first place.

**Clarified mid-session, John's question:** confirmed this edits an *existing* Skill (`ci-routing-intent`), not a new one, and that `output_desc` is a separate field read only by Michelle's roster-broker (`lib/project-manager.js`, one call site, grep-confirmed) for her own delegation reasoning — it is never injected into `ci-routing-intent`'s own prompt, so it has zero effect on the routing bug itself. Authoring it was optional, bundled in only because `AA-194` already tracked it as a known gap on Marcus's roster row and it was cheap to include in the same edit.

**Fix approved and applied (exact wording shown to John before writing, per the mandatory stop-gate):** appended an escalate-classification paragraph to `method` — catalog-style "what data is available" questions are qa, not escalate; since escalate has no working destination today, default to qa when genuinely ambiguous. Authored `output_desc` in the same terse "Returns X — the Y" style already used by sibling Intent Skills (checked live for consistency before writing, not guessed).

**Live-verified, caught a second real bug in the process:** the original failing question now correctly returns `qa`/high confidence. A negative-control test (a genuinely escalate-worthy request) returned `{"error":"Parse failed and retry also failed","detail":"No tool_use block in response"}` — reproduced twice in a row, not a one-off. `VERCEL_TOKEN` was unset in both the Bash and PowerShell shells (checked directly per `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`'s known Windows `setx` gap, genuinely unreachable this session, documented rather than assumed unavailable) — could not pull the raw Anthropic stop_reason. Root-caused instead via config comparison: `ci-routing-intent` (`max_tokens: 300`, `temperature: null`) is the one intent in its `can_request_help`/`tool_choice:'auto'` family never migrated onto the `temperature=0`/adequate-`max_tokens` fix `AA-154`/`AA-149` already proved on 3 siblings (`ci-answer-intent` 3000/0, `qg-review-intent` 1500/0, `library-catalog-intent` 1500/0) — a `AA-192`-shaped "one site never migrated onto an already-proven fix" pattern, not a new bug class. The session's own longer `method` text gave the model more to reason about, pushing this pre-existing thin margin into visible failure (even the passing `qa` call needed the existing retry-once safety net).

**Second fix approved and applied, same proven pattern, no new numbers invented:** pinned `temperature=0`, raised `max_tokens` 300→1500 to match `qg-review-intent`/`library-catalog-intent`. Re-verified live: original question still `qa`/high confidence; the escalate negative-control now correctly returns `escalate`/high confidence — the "default to qa when ambiguous" guidance did not over-correct into swallowing genuine escalate cases. Both calls still show `retry_count: 1` on the first attempt — consistent with the platform's already-documented `AA-151`/`AA-172` retry-family behavior (seen at 10-80% rates on other `can_request_help` intents), not treated as a new regression, not chased further this session.

## S-CHI-07-design / S-CHI-07 (v6.3.34, `202827d`, 2026-07-16, worktree `continuity-ux-0716`)

**Context:** first of a 5-session Channel Intelligence UX sweep opened by John's live-screenshot walkthrough of the Chat/Evidence/Agent Routing panels (`CHI-07`→`CHI-08`→`CHI-12`→`CHI-09`→`CHI-10`). John flagged several missing/inconsistent "Full Agent Routing & Answer Given in Xm Ys" captions and Agent Routing lines that never show a duration even after "Read more." Investigated with two `Explore` sub-agent passes plus direct source reads before proposing scope — root cause was structural, not a render bug: `logEvent()` had 21 independent call sites (13 in the component body, 8 inside the module-scope `runQaWithQualityGate`/`runHypothesisTest` functions) each hand-computing or hand-nulling their own `durationMs`, each with its own justifying comment; `setMessages()` had 17 independent call sites, only 1 of which (the `qa` bubble) ever set `totalElapsedMs`, even though 7 more ack-bubble sites already carried `hopStart`/`hopEnd`. A stray bug surfaced in the same sweep: `failure_triage` (L992) logged a literal `durationMs: 0` — every sibling non-measurable event used `null`. When asked whether to just patch the render layer or instrument new timing, John redirected both answers into "this should be a central service, not something hardcoded in multiple places" — matching this repo's own "multi-site bug pattern → shared-service check" rule (`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`) almost exactly.

**Fix — 2 new helpers, `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` only (1 file):**
- `buildHopEvent(type, agentId, data, durationMs, extra)` — a single declared `NON_MEASURABLE_EVENT_TYPES` set (`agent_selection`, `delegation`, `delegation_return`, `failure_triage`, `question_boundary`) replaces 6 scattered comments; a caller-supplied real duration passes through unchanged, an omitted duration on a declared type resolves to `null`, an omitted duration on any other type logs a `console.error` dev-guard (never throws — never blocks the user) and still resolves to `null`. Migrated all 21 `logEvent`/`onEvent` call sites through it — the `failure_triage` fix falls out of this migration for free (its site simply stops passing a stale `0`).
- `buildMessage({role, kind, text, hopStart, hopEnd, totalElapsedMs, needsReview, reviewReason})` — whenever `hopStart` is present, `totalElapsedMs` is a required companion (same fail-open `console.error` pattern if a caller forgets it). Migrated all 17 `setMessages` call sites. **Deliberately conservative scope, confirmed while writing the kickoff doc:** 8 sites that carried no hop data before this session (`qa_failed`, `hyp_entry`, the generic `non_qa` fallback, every `error` kind) still carry none — the data genuinely isn't available at those call sites without adding new UI surface, which was explicitly out of scope. Of the 9 sites that already had `hopStart`/`hopEnd`, the `qa` bubble already had `totalElapsedMs` too; the other 8 (submission ack, 2×info-only ack, 4×resolution ack, ~~1 more~~) gained it — `onDiscard` needed a brand-new `turnStart` capture (had none before), `onSelectHypothesis`'s ack correctly closes over a `turnStart` declared just after it (synchronous code, safe by the time the async `.then()` fires), `onResolveConfirmation`'s 4 ack sites reuse the function's existing `t0`.

**Process note found mid-session, fixed and flagged as a follow-up (`task_3216010f`):** this worktree's shared `.git` (all worktrees share one ref store) still has a local `dev` branch belonging to the main checkout, observed 253 commits behind `origin/dev`. `git push origin dev` — the literal command in this repo's own `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`/every prior kickoff doc's COMMIT section — silently resolves "dev" to that stale local ref rather than the current branch's HEAD, and gets rejected non-fast-forward in a way indistinguishable from the real concurrent-session race `CLAUDE.md` rule #4 already handles (re-fetch/re-rebase does **not** fix it, since the problem is which local ref is being pushed, not remote staleness). Fixed by using `git push origin HEAD:dev` instead — confirmed working. This session's own kickoff doc was patched live after hitting this once. Spun off as a background task to fix the same bare-`dev` instruction everywhere else it appears in the standing docs.

**Verification:** Node test (`test-s-chi-07.mjs`) 16/16 PASS, deleted before commit. `npm run build` zero errors. Post-migration greps confirmed zero raw `durationMs:` literals outside `buildHopEvent`'s own definition, zero raw inline `setMessages` literals outside `buildMessage`'s own definition, zero `durationMs: 0` anywhere.

**Independently re-verified against the real deployed dev preview by the design session, not accepted from the coding report alone (bypassed Vercel deployment protection via `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET`, confirmed fresh from `.env.local` rather than trusted from memory):** 3 full live round trips. (1) A plain `qa` question ("Japan is Apple's fastest-growing GEO...") confirmed the pre-existing regression case unchanged — "Hops 2–3 / Full Agent Routing & Answer Given in 1m 23s". (2) A guardrail-block/escalation run (the EMEA co-op question, which happened to trip Owen's guardrail this run) confirmed live that the `failure_triage` line ("Pipeline Triage — Deciding whether more research would help — more research wouldn't help here") now renders with **no** duration suffix, directly next to its sibling "Blocking this answer — a policy issue was found · 64.8s" line which does have one — the `0`-bug fix confirmed live, not just by code read. (3) A full hypothesis flow (flagged the Japan answer for review → generated 4 theories → selected H2 → tested it → resolved Info Only) confirmed 3 previously-silent elapsed captions now render: the submission-ack bubble ("Hop 6 / Full Agent Routing & Answer Given in 2s"), the Theory Evidence card ("Hops 7–6 / Full Agent Routing & Answer Given in 1m 2s" — the `onDiscard`-adjacent `hypFlow.testElapsedMs` render fix), and the info-only-ack bubble ("Hop 9 / Full Agent Routing & Answer Given in 1s" — the brand-new `turnStart` capture in `onDiscard`). Michelle's `agent_selection` line confirmed still shows no duration (correct, unchanged). Zero console errors across all three runs, including zero firings of the new dev-guard (confirming no call site was missed). Accept/Reject resolution-ack not independently re-run live — same already-proven `t0`-reuse pattern as the verified Info Only ack, not a novel path, per the standing guidance against re-proving an already-verified mechanism (`STANDARDS.md` Category L).

**Tooling note:** the Browser pane's `computer{action:"screenshot"}` consistently timed out this session against both the landing-page overlay and the live app; worked around entirely via `read_page`/`get_page_text`/`javascript_tool` text extraction plus ref-based clicks, which worked reliably throughout. `resize_window` to the desktop preset didn't visually change the rendered layout (stayed in the mobile tabbed "Chat"/"Evidence & Interaction" view) — worked around by using the tab-switch buttons instead of relying on a 3-column desktop layout. Neither issue reflects anything in the app itself.

**Close-out:** `CHI-07` moved directly to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` (skipped the "leave in main table one more cycle" precedent some prior sessions used, since this session immediately continues into `CHI-08` and a stale main-table row would only add confusion). `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Version in dev" bumped to `v6.3.34`; "In flight now" bullet updated (not removed — 4 more sessions queued in this same design session); "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated, `CHI-04`'s entry aged out (already fully captured above). `docs/FEATURES.md`, `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`, `CLAUDE-STATE.md`, `docs/SESSIONS.md`, `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.34-CHI-07-*.md` touched, plus the one `.jsx` file. Serverless function count unaffected (no `api/` file added, `AI PATTERN CHECK` N/A — no `api/` route touched).

## S-AI-53-design / S-AI-53 (v6.3.33, `e15586b`, 2026-07-16, worktree `log-19-teach-metadata-fix-0716`)

**Context:** `AI-53` (`docs/FEATURES.md`) found `SERVICE_CATALOG`'s `document-extraction` entry describing two operationally distinct things under one feature string — a real Claude Sonnet 4.5 call in `api/brief.js` generating structured training-doc metadata, and `api/extract.js`'s deterministic zero-cost PDF/DOCX/TXT parser — plus `api/extract.js`'s own two actions (parse vs. CSV upload) both hardcoding `ai_type: 'deterministic'`, indistinguishable from each other in By-Service. Root cause traced deeper than a naming fix during design: `api/extract.js`/`api/brief.js` (Vercel backend) had no shared source to pull a real service slug from — `SERVICE_CATALOG` lived only in `useAIActivity.js` (Vite frontend, which the backend cannot import), so each route hardcoded its own literal. Second, related finding: `knowledge-reinforcement`'s catalog entry claimed `['Embeddings','Structured Output']` but its real call site (`lib/knowledge-write.js`'s `embedAndUpsertEntry()`) only ever logs `patternsUsed: ['embeddings']` — a stale hand-maintained claim. Third, surfaced by a mid-design rebase: `src/aiPatterns.js`'s `AI_PAT.KNOWLEDGE_REINFORCEMENT` (used by 8 screens for step/task badges) hardcoded the identical stale claim — a concurrent session (`LOG-20`, already in `dev`) had changed this file's sourcing but explicitly preserved the content byte-identical, since correcting it wasn't `LOG-20`'s scope. Folded in as Task 5 (John's explicit call, a file-count exception to the normal 3-file cap) to avoid leaving a new Category M cross-reference contradiction between the two files.

**Fix — 5 files:** moved `SERVICE_CATALOG` into `shared/ai-patterns.js` (same treatment `AA-190b` already gave `PATTERN_CATALOG`), with the `document-extraction` entry removed and replaced by three: `document-metadata-generation` (the real AI call), `document-parsing`, `csv-upload` (both deterministic, `serviceType: 'logic'`) — 35 entries total (33 − 1 + 3). Added a derived `SERVICE_SLUG` export (`Object.fromEntries` over the catalog's own slugs) so `api/extract.js`/`api/brief.js` import their slugs instead of hardcoding literals — structurally prevents a future collision rather than just detecting one after the fact. `knowledge-reinforcement`'s patterns corrected to `['Embeddings']` only. `useAIActivity.js`: now imports `SERVICE_CATALOG` from the shared file (local 33-entry array deleted); `AI_TYPE_TO_SERVICE.extraction` repointed to `document-metadata-generation`; `byService`'s `patterns` field now self-derives from each service's real logged `patternsUsed` (via a new `PATTERN_NAME_BY_SLUG` lookup), falling back to the static catalog hint only when a service has zero real calls yet — closes this staleness bug class for all ~35 services, not just these two instances. `api/extract.js`/`api/brief.js` import `SERVICE_SLUG` and use it at both `logActivity()` call sites instead of string literals. `src/aiPatterns.js`'s `AI_PAT.KNOWLEDGE_REINFORCEMENT` corrected to `names('embeddings')` only.

**Mid-session rebase:** after this session's own push (`e15586b`), a concurrent session (`LOG-21`) landed on top of it (`01184f6`, moving `classifyRow()`/`buildActivitySummary()`/`percentile()` into `useAIActivity.js` from `useAgents.js`). A `git fetch` + `git rebase origin/dev` immediately before close-out found `e15586b` already an ancestor of `origin/dev`'s tip — the rebase fast-forwarded with nothing to replay, and a full re-read of `useAIActivity.js` post-rebase confirmed this session's `byService`/`PATTERN_NAME_BY_SLUG`/`SERVICE_CATALOG` changes were layered correctly under `LOG-21`'s restructuring, no duplication or conflict. `npm run build` re-run clean after the rebase to confirm.

**Verification:** Node test (`test-ai-53.mjs`) 9/9 PASS, deleted before commit. `npm run build` zero errors (both before and after the mid-session rebase). `node scripts/check-ai-logging-coverage.js` — 3 CRITICAL findings, all pre-existing and unrelated to this session's slugs (`lib/agent-run.js`, `lib/vector-search.js`, `AIReviewTab.jsx` — none of `document-parsing`/`csv-upload`/`document-metadata-generation` appear in any finding, confirming a clean result as the kickoff predicted).

## S-AUDITLOG-design / S-LOG-19 / S-LOG-20 / S-LOG-21 (v6.3.35/v6.3.36/v6.3.37, `ee0bc18`/`fa20694`/`01184f6`, 2026-07-16, worktree `design-auditlog-0716`)

**Context:** John asked for direct confirmation on 7 points about the AI Audit screen (global "AI Transparency" panel) vs. the MI screen's Agent Routing/Agents panel, prompted by two screenshots — same display service? same record service? real industry pattern names, not invented? same central storage, do totals reconcile? patterns discovered in real-time or hardcoded? any other architecture rules to check? and a fix list.

**Investigation (no code written this phase, per the design-sessions-produce-docs-only rule):** read `ARCHITECTURE.md §19i` (Four-Source Trust Model, LOCKED) in full; read `src/hooks/useAIActivity.js`, `src/hooks/useAgents.js`, `src/components/AIActivityPanel.jsx`, `src/screens/MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` (`MI_LOOP_SCOPE`/`PROPOSED_MI_AGENT_IDS` only), `lib/activity-log.js`, `shared/ai-patterns.js`, `src/aiPatterns.js`; grepped every `ai_activity_log` write call site across `api/`/`lib/` to confirm no stray direct-insert bypassed the shared `logActivity()`/`logAICall()` writers. **Findings reported to John, verbatim per question:** (1) different hooks/components (`useAIActivity()` vs. `useAgentActivitySummary()`) — not the same display service. (2) same central table (`ai_activity_log`), exactly two canonical writers (`logAICall()` client-side, `logActivity()` server-side, `AA-190`), every server call site confirmed compliant. (3) real published pattern names confirmed (`AA-190b`'s Orchestrator-Workers/Prompt Compression/Case Retention renames, each citing a real source in code comments). (4) same table, but two independently-scoped queries — totals converge today by coincidence of current usage, not design. (5) display-side self-maintaining (`LOG-14`'s auto-bucket fallback), but pattern *detection* itself still requires a hand-written detector per pattern (`§19i`'s 4-bucket model) — not automatic. (6) found two unprompted gaps: a stale comment in `useAgents.js` (claimed a 500-row cap `AI-184` already removed) and a second, independent hardcoded pattern-label module (`src/aiPatterns.js`, used by 8 other screens' badges) with no structural link to the canonical catalog. (7) 3-item fix list logged as `LOG-19`/`LOG-20`/`LOG-21`.

## S-CHI-12-design / S-CHI-12 (v6.3.39, `861e299`, 2026-07-16, worktree `continuity-ux-0716`)

**Context:** third of the 5-session Channel Intelligence UX sweep (`CHI-07`→`CHI-08`→`CHI-12`→`CHI-09`→`CHI-10`), continuing directly from `CHI-08`'s close-out. `QaEvidenceCard` had no height/overflow control — headline/body/table/byline/elapsed-line/flagged-line/CTA were flat siblings in one unbounded div, so the "Needs your input" CTA rendered wherever the accumulated content pushed it; John had to scroll Column 2 to find it on a real long answer. Depended on `CHI-08` shipping first so the flagged-narrative line landed in the Chat bubble before being deleted here — confirmed live before scoping (the string still existed in `QaEvidenceCard` post-`CHI-08`, correctly left out of that session's scope).

**Mock — took two iterations before it actually demonstrated the bug:** the first attempt (an interactive HTML widget with height/toggle sliders) used sample content short enough that it never overflowed even without a fix, so both states looked identical to the card already live in the app — John: "all I saw was a mock evidence section, we already have this in the UI." A second attempt (a JS-driven before/after comparison) failed to render at all — the injected `innerHTML` never populated, leaving two empty boxes. Root-caused both failures as the JS/HTML approach being too fragile in this sandbox for a reliable design review artifact; switched to a static SVG wireframe (no script, no external font dependency) with genuinely long sample content that visibly overflowed a simulated column. First SVG draft still put the CTA hard against the bottom edge of the frame; John's explicit correction — CTA should always sit above the fold with margin to spare, and the scrollable content should read as its own bordered box that ends cleanly above it — was implemented and approved.

**Technical correction found during scoping, before the kickoff doc was written:** the `FEATURES.md` placeholder row's original plan was to reuse `MI-54`'s `flex:1`/`minHeight:0`/`overflow:"hidden"` pattern "one level deeper." Tracing the actual ancestor chain live found `QaEvidenceCard` sits inside `EvidenceColumn`'s own already-scrolling region (`overflowY:"auto"`, itself flex-column) as a plain stacked child, not a flex child being handed available height by its parent — `flex:1`/`minHeight:0` on `QaEvidenceCard` itself would have been inert. Corrected mechanism: a fixed `maxHeight:320` (px, not `vh`) directly on the content sub-region, which needs no bounded-height context from its parent at all.

**Fix — 1 file, `src/screens/MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`:**
- Deleted the "Full Agent Routing & Answer Given in Xm Ys" and "⚑ Marcus flagged this —" lines from `QaEvidenceCard` — both duplicated in the Chat bubble by `CHI-08`. The "Formatted by {agent} · {role}" byline is not a duplicate, kept as the last line of content.
- Wrapped headline/body/tables/byline in a new div: `borderTop`/`borderBottom` (`1px solid T.line`, reusing the card's own outer border for the left/right edges rather than adding a full box border), `maxHeight:320`, `overflowY:"auto"`. The review-choice ack / "Needs your input" CTA footer is untouched, rendering below that box, unbounded, always fully visible.

**Verification:** Node test (`test-chi-12.mjs`) 10/10 PASS, deleted before commit — source-level checks confirmed both duplicate lines gone, the bounded box present with the exact `maxHeight`/`overflowY`/border values, the byline and CTA/ack copy unchanged, and correct source ordering (bounded box after the header, before the CTA footer). `npm run build` zero errors.

**Independently re-verified against the real deployed dev preview by the design session, not accepted from the coding report alone:** a real live Q&A (Japan GEO growth question, genuinely long — 5 body sections + an 8-row data table) produced `qaEvidence` substantial enough to trigger real overflow. Direct DOM/computed-style inspection (not just visual read) confirmed: the bounded box's `scrollHeight` (1485px) genuinely exceeds its `clientHeight` (318px) — real internal scrolling firing, not just a theoretical cap; the CTA element's bounding rect sits fully inside its scroll-ancestor's (`EvidenceColumn`'s own scrolling region) visible bounds with zero further scrolling needed; "Full Agent Routing & Answer Given" appears exactly once across the entire page (the Chat bubble only — zero leakage into Evidence, confirmed by a page-wide text-match count). Clicking "Good, thanks" correctly swapped the CTA for the ack line. Repeated the same flow on a real mobile viewport (375×812) — the original tab's `resize_window` call silently failed to propagate to the page (`window.innerWidth` stayed at the desktop value despite the tool reporting success), worked around by opening a fresh tab and resizing before navigation, which took correctly; confirmed identically bounded/scrolling content box, zero horizontal overflow (`document.body.scrollWidth === window.innerWidth`), and zero duplicate-line leakage in the mobile Evidence tab's own render path. Zero console errors on both desktop and mobile runs. Not independently re-triggered live this session: the flagged-line removal (the live answer wasn't flagged) and the "Have Priya… generate theories" click (reuses `CHI-05`'s already-proven `onReview` path) — both accepted via the Node test's source-level check plus direct code read, per the standing guidance against re-proving an already-verified mechanism.

**Close-out:** `CHI-12` moved directly to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`. `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Version in dev" bumped to `v6.3.39`; "In flight now" bullet updated (not removed — `CHI-09`/`CHI-10` still queued in this same design session); "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated, `S-AI-53`'s entry aged out (already fully captured in its own `docs/SESSIONS.md` entry above). `docs/FEATURES.md`, `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`, `CLAUDE-STATE.md`, `docs/SESSIONS.md` touched, plus the 1 file the coding session changed. Node test 4/4 PASS (static source-shape check, since the bug class isn't reproducible in a pure-Node reimplementation — the actual gap that let it ship), build clean.

## S-LOO-006-design/S-LOO-006 (v6.3.43, 2026-07-16, worktree `continuity-regression-0716`)

**`LOO-006` ✅ Done, archived — Owen's `qg-review-intent`: schema-agnostic triage synthesis + mandatory Library verification before any `synthesized_as_fact` block. Closes `CHI-06`, also archived.**

**Context:** John reported a Channel Intelligence Q&A dead-end that looked like a regression of `AA-194` (confirmed still intact, not the cause). Root-caused live against real Supabase traces to two distinct defects, both in Owen's Skill Profile content (`method`/`traits.schema`), zero code files:
1. **Schema-fragile triage (closes `CHI-06`'s null-`triage` crash).** Owen's `method` instructed him to escalate an unfixable guardrail block via `request_help`, then copy the delegate's `recommend_escalate`/`suggested_research_request` fields verbatim into his own `triage`. That only holds when Michelle routes to Sam Reyes (`intake-failure-intent`) — her routing is genuine agent-reasoned judgment (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §19d/§19e), and on a live-traced run she legitimately picked Nadia Farouk (`data-escalate-intent`) instead, whose schema has no such fields. `triage` came back `null`, crashing `buildFailureText()` (`CHI-06`).
2. **Inconsistent `synthesized_as_fact` firing on Library-backed content (~1 in 5, John's own live repro).** A real Data Room record (`the_library.id = 1c7104c5-...`, `data_type: synthesized`, the Nordholm co-op scenario) was being blocked inconsistently — Owen's own guardrail reasoning reversed itself on identical text within one run, with no independently-checkable fact grounding the call.

**Alternatives considered and rejected (John, this session):** hardcoding Sam as the escalation target (banned by `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19d's Correction note), removing Nadia's `data-escalate-intent` candidacy (same anti-pattern via subtraction), and removing `synthesized_as_fact` from the rule set entirely (rejected — it also catches a separate fake-hand-off-narration failure mode, still wanted).

**Fix (Task 1, one Supabase `UPDATE`, `skill_profiles` where `slug='qg-review-intent'`):** rewrote `method` (5736→7782 chars) so (a) escalation triage is synthesized in Owen's own words from whatever the delegate actually returned, schema-agnostic, no assumed field names; and (b) a `SYNTHESIZED_AS_FACT VERIFICATION` paragraph makes any `synthesized_as_fact` block mandatory-gated on a `request_help`→`delegate_to_agent` Library-verification round trip, binding on the verdict — pass if the claim traces to a real Library record (any `data_type`) and the answer's own `confidence_tier` matches it, block only if no record backs the claim or the tier misrepresents what verification found. Also updated `traits.schema.properties.triage.description` to match (no more "verbatim"). Two unrelated clauses that also reference `synthesized_as_fact` by name (the `na`-tier fake-hand-off clause, the capability-scope-decline clause) deliberately left untouched. `git diff --stat` confirmed empty — genuinely Supabase-content-only.

**Task 2 (Category F Node test, `test-LOO-006.mjs`, deleted after run):** 11/11 PASS — confirmed the write landed, the old verbatim-copy instruction is gone, the new verification/schema-agnostic-synthesis language is present, both unrelated clauses are untouched, and the `guardrail.rule_violated` enum is unchanged in shape (still 6 values, `synthesized_as_fact` retained, narrowed by process not removed).

**Task 3 (Category L live verification against the real dev preview, `https://deepbench-frontend-git-dev-roadmapventures-projects.vercel.app`):** ran the real Q&A→quality-gate chain (`ci-answer-intent`→`qg-review-intent`) end to end, 9 completed runs total (5 original positive-case + 2 retries after 1 transient infra 500 on the durable-loop `continue` checkpoint, unrelated to this session's diff + 2 adversarial negative-case questions), plus direct `durable_hops` inspection via Supabase MCP for full trace detail on each.
- **`CHI-06` closure confirmed:** zero null-`triage` outcomes across every genuine block (3 distinct rule violations hit: `synthesized_as_fact` ×3, `missing_confidence` ×2, `citation_missing` ×1; 2 distinct Michelle-routed delegates observed: Eleanor for verification, Sam for escalation triage) — `triage.recommend_escalate`/`suggested_research_request` always well-formed, matching whatever the actually-routed delegate returned.
- **Verification-grounded blocking confirmed real, not cosmetic:** every block's `guardrail.reason` explicitly cites real Eleanor Data Room findings (e.g. *"Eleanor's Data Room verification confirms that the primary record backing the Nordholm-specific claims... is flagged as SYNTHESIZED, not sourced"*), directly traceable in `durable_hops.result` — the mandatory verify-before-block mechanism fires and is binding, exactly as specified.
- **Negative case (2 adversarial leading/false-premise questions, e.g. "Confirm that Nordholm hit 92% in Q1 2024..."):** guardrail correctly blocked both (`missing_confidence`, citing the same real verification grounding) — the fix did not make the guardrail toothless against genuine fabrication/mistagging.

## S-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-0717 — Stale worktree cleanup + design-session architecture-awareness gap

**Session:** S-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-0717 (2026-07-17, worktree `worktree-cleanup-0717`, no kickoff doc — cleanup/process session, no application code touched, no version bump) — docs-only.

**Part 1 — Worktree cleanup.** John asked how staleness is actually verified before removing anything, since a worktree could in principle hold uncommitted design work. Answered by distinguishing two separate checks: `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/dev` (every *commit* already on `dev`) and `git status` (no uncommitted/untracked changes sitting in the working tree) — both re-run fresh on both worktrees, both clean. Separately confirmed the two worktrees' *claimed remaining work* wasn't actually lost: `continuity-ux-0716`'s bullet named `CHI-09`/`CHI-10` as still open — both confirmed still `❌ Missing` in `docs/FEATURES.md`, already pushed to `dev`, independent of the worktree; `loo-007-confidence-tier-0716`'s namesake `LOO-007` is likewise still tracked and pushed. Removed both worktrees (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) and cleared `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s two stale/dangling "In flight now" bullets (`continuity-ux-0716`'s narrative was doubly stale — worktree merged *and* its "next up" claim superseded by `CHI-13`/`CHI-14` shipping via two other worktrees; `continuity-regression-0716` had no matching worktree or branch anywhere — `LOO-006`, the feature it named, had already shipped and closed out, v6.3.43).

**Part 2 — Why the naming convention isn't reaching sessions.** John asked directly how the new ID convention gets enforced — do sessions know to look it up. Traced the actual mandatory reading chain (`CLAUDE.md` → `CLAUDE-STATE.md`/`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` for a design session) and confirmed neither file mentions `docs/SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` at all. The correct rule does exist, but only in `docs/FEATURES.md`'s own "Feature ID Format" section — and `FEATURES.md` itself isn't on the mandatory reading list, only opened when a session happens to check a feature's status. This is exactly why 3 rows drifted this week (`S-ID-NAMING-AUDIT-0717`, above) despite the rule being "live" since 2026-07-15 — the rule was correctly written but structurally invisible to the documented startup path. **Part 1 — Router confirmation.** John asked directly whether typing "design" still kicks off a design session the same way. Verified by reading `CLAUDE.md`'s router text fresh rather than answering from memory of how the session had gone so far — confirmed unchanged: the router still just asks "Design session or coding session?", and "design" answers that directly. While verifying, caught a real instance of exactly the kind of drift today's own work was about preventing: `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`'s Step 1/2 text (rewritten earlier the same day, before "Product Focus Area" was agreed) still said "Product Area" in two spots. Fixed both, committed and pushed separately (`03098f8..f5643e9`) before this session's own scope began.

**Part 2 — Decision-autonomy calibration.** John raised a direct concern: design sessions have been checking in on too many small decisions lately, and he's unsure whether that reflects genuine stakes or whether he should extend more autonomy instead of gating on his approval by default. Answered using today's own conversation as evidence rather than an abstract framework pulled from nowhere: reviewed the actual check-ins made this session and separated the ones with real justification (`AA-194`'s rename — already flagged as ambiguous by `SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` itself; the `PRO`/`SES` naming collision — an active conflict, not hypothetical; the architecture-model terminology — John had explicitly asked to be involved in that one) from at least one that wasn't (whether `SES-005` needed its own item vs. folding into `SES-002` — a low-stakes, easily-reversible call that could have just been made and reported).

**Proposed and John confirmed a 3-tier default**, written directly into `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` as a new standing rule ("Decision Autonomy Tiers," placed right after "No Coding in Design Sessions" — a foundational operating-mode rule, not something narrow enough to bury in the Backlog Capture section):
- **Tier 1 (decide and report, no check-in):** backlog file/tier placement when the criterion clearly applies; fold-into-existing-row vs. new-ID calls when scope reasoning is clear-cut; non-canonical wording/phrasing; anything cheap to revise later with zero downstream cost if wrong.
- **Tier 2 (decide, flag clearly in the close-out report):** judgment calls that could reasonably go either way with low cost either way — John sees the call made and can redirect after the fact rather than gating the work on approval beforehand.
- **Tier 3 (ask first, always):** canonical terminology/naming that future sessions will reference (the specific "talking past each other" risk); anything touching shared state other sessions or people depend on (pushing to `dev`, deleting a worktree, renaming a heavily cross-referenced ID); reversing a decision John already made; anything John's told this session directly he wants to be involved in, for that topic.
- **Default to Tier 2 when genuinely unsure** which tier applies — the asymmetry is deliberate: a wrong Tier-2 call costs a correction after the fact, while defaulting everything to Tier 3 recreates the exact fatigue this rule exists to fix.

Cross-referenced from `SES-003`'s row in `docs/FEATURES.md` (the "How to Work With John" reference item) so that future item folds this rule in by reference when built, rather than re-deriving the same content twice.

## S-RULES-CHECK-0717 — Sub-agent/coding-session awareness gaps, checked before writing anything

**Session:** S-RULES-CHECK-0717 (2026-07-17, worktree `rules-check-0717`, no kickoff doc, no application code touched, no version bump) — docs-only.

**Part 1 — Are "sub-session," "sub-agent," and "worktree session" the same thing?** John asked directly. Answered precisely rather than treating them as synonyms: a **session** is a full independent conversation that always sets up its own worktree by hard rule ("worktree session" isn't a fourth category, just naming the mechanism); a **sub-agent** (the `Agent`/Task tool) is an ephemeral, prompt-scoped helper spawned from within a session that does *not* get its own worktree and starts with zero memory of the parent conversation; "sub-session" isn't formally distinct in this repo's docs, loosely covering either the spawned coding session or a versioned split (`72a`/`72b`/`72c`), both of which are actually full sessions.

**Part 2 — Coverage check, not assumption.** Full design/coding sessions are already covered by today's fixes (`CLAUDE.md`'s router is mandatory for every session, routes design sessions straight to `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`). Coding sessions deliberately don't read `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` at all — by design, they execute kickoff docs rather than making architectural calls themselves — so that's not a gap. The real gap: ad-hoc research/sweep sub-agents (like today's `FEATURES-LATER.md` 225-row sweep) get a hand-written prompt with no automatic path to `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`/`SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` — the exact same failure shape `CLAUDE.md` rule #3 already fixed for worktree paths (2026-07-16), just not yet generalized past "tell it where to work" to "tell it what's currently true."

**Part 3 — Does this also help a coding session avoid writing rogue/duplicate code?** John's follow-up. Honest answer, not a reflexive yes: no, not directly — coding sessions don't read `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md` at all, so this specific fix (sub-agent bootstrapping) doesn't reach them. The actual mechanism for catching duplication has to be the design session, upstream, before the kickoff doc exists — coding sessions only have a weaker downstream backstop via `CLAUDE-RULES.md` (the one file they read "if they hit a pattern question mid-session").

Also fixed a stale `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19e doc note. 3 files. Independently re-verified from scratch by a second coding-session pass (unexplained sequencing oddity: the fix was already live on `dev` before that verification pass started — flagged to John, no clean explanation found, but every claim was independently re-checked against real Supabase/code state regardless, including catching a typo in the kickoff's own live-test instructions and self-correcting against real data).

## S-CHI-09-design/S-CHI-09 — Agent Routing drawer: within-hop chronological event order (v6.3.48)

**Session:** S-CHI-09-design (worktree `chi-tickets-0717`, 2026-07-17), coding session `S-CHI-09` spawned automatically per the Design→Code→Verify Loop. v6.3.48.

John asked to continue the open `CHI` backlog. Presented the 5 open tickets (`CHI-09`, `CHI-10`, `CHI-11`, `CHI-15`, `CHI-16`); John chose to split `CHI-09` (which had bundled two unrelated fixes) into two issues and work only the first.

**Split:** `CHI-09` kept the within-hop event order bug; the second fix (Michelle's unsummarized `agent_selection` raw-reasoning line) became `CHI-17` (next free ID — `CHI-16` was the highest in use across all 4 backlog files), filed `❌ Missing`, deferred.

**Root cause (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`'s `groupEventsIntoHops()`, L796-817):** fed `ordered = [...events].reverse()` (newest-first, correct for hop-card stacking), but when merging consecutive same-agent events into one hop it just `push`ed each event onto that hop's own `events` array in iteration order — so *within* a hop, events inherited the same newest-first order the outer list uses, when a human reading one hop's own activity expects chronological (oldest-first) order. One shared function, called from both the desktop drawer and the mobile pinned feed — fixing it here fixes both call sites, no per-site patch (the repo's own "multi-site bug pattern → shared-service check" applied correctly from the start, since it was already one shared function, not duplicated).

**Fix:** one line added to the function's closing `hops.map` — `events: [...h.events].reverse()` on the non-boundary branch.

**Two side effects found while tracing this, confirmed in scope with John before writing the kickoff doc (not separate work):**
1. `RoutingHopCard`'s left-border color reads `hop.events[hop.events.length - 1]` (`lastColor`) — under the bug that was actually the *oldest* event; after the fix it's the true last/most-recent event, matching what the variable name implied was always intended.
2. `RoutingHopCard`'s React `key` is `hop.events[0].id` — under the bug that changed every time a new event streamed into a growing hop (forcing an unneeded remount); after the fix it's the oldest/first event, stable for the hop's whole lifetime.

**Coding session:** single file (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`), single task, exactly as specced. Node test (`test-CHI-09.mjs`, Category B) — the coding session found and fixed two pre-existing defects in the kickoff doc's own T2 test fixture (a miscounted hop-collapse total, and Owen's two sub-events listed in the wrong relative order) — confirmed these were fixture-only errors, not touching the actual shipped diff, before accepting the fix. 14/14 tests passed after correction. `npm run build` succeeded. `git diff --stat` — exactly 1 file, 6 insertions/1 deletion. Committed `416d173`, pushed via `git push origin HEAD:dev`.

**Design session's own independent live verification against the real dev preview** (Vercel deployment-protection bypass header appended as a query param to get past the SSO interstitial — see `docs/ENV-VARS.md`/memory `reference-vercel-bypass`): ran the live EMEA co-op-budget question end to end (6 hops, 1m 30s). Confirmed via direct `getComputedStyle` border-left-color reads, not just a visual glance — Marcus's hop 1 (`intent_routing` 3.6s → `qa_answer` 12.4s, `needs_review: true`) showed border color `rgb(182,135,58)` (`T.brass`, the `qa_answer`/needs_review color) rather than `T.navyMid` (`intent_routing`'s color) — proof the border now reads the *last* event in the hop, not the first, confirming side effect 1 live. Within-hop order for Marcus's 2-event hop displayed intent-routing before answer-generation — the only order that makes causal sense, and the order the pre-fix code could not have produced (it would have shown the answer before the routing decision). Owen's hop 4 (`delegation` "routing this to Eleanor" → `proofreader` "reviewing... 45.9s") showed border color `rgb(90,117,56)` (`T.moss`, matching `proofreader`'s pass-result color) — also consistent with the fix reading the true last event. Repeated the same check after resizing to a 375×812 mobile viewport — identical hop content and ordering from the shared function's second call site. Zero console errors on both. Side effect 2 (React key stability) not independently re-proven live — already deterministically covered by the Node test's T-side-effect-2 case (simulating a hop's growth step by step), per the standing guidance against re-proving an already-verified mechanism live when a pure-logic unit test already covers it.

Kickoff: `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.48-CHI-09-agent-routing-within-hop-chronological-order.md`.

**Close-out:** `CHI-09` moved to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` as ✅ Done. `CHI-17` stays in `docs/FEATURES.md` as ❌ Missing, unaffected. `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Version in dev" bumped to v6.3.48, "In flight now" bullet removed, "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated (`S-STEP3-FIX-0717` aged out, already fully captured in its own `docs/SESSIONS.md` entry, confirmed before dropping). Worktree `chi-tickets-0717` and branch `session/chi-tickets-0717` removed per `CLAUDE.md` rule #7 after this close-out commit is pushed.

## S-CHI-19-design / S-CHI-19 (v6.3.53, Supabase-only, no code commit, 2026-07-17, worktree `design-chi-tickets-review-0717`)

**John's ask:** work `CHI-19` from the open backlog list this session surfaced (Marcus's Q&A answers dive into partner specifics without ever naming which real-world entity a generic question reference resolved to — e.g. "our EMEA retail partner" never gets connected to "Nordholm").

**Target correction, before the kickoff doc was written:** `CHI-19`'s own row named `qa-answer-format` (`method`/`output_desc`) as the fix location. Live Supabase check (per the row's own "verify live against Supabase first" instruction) showed this was wrong on two counts: `qa-answer-format` belongs to `screen-controls`/Alex Reeves, not Marcus's `channel-intelligence`, and its own `method` text explicitly forbids content judgment ("never invent, add, or omit facts... never content judgment") — it only reformats whatever raw answer text it's handed. The real content-generation Skill is `ci-answer-intent`, confirmed genuinely attached to `channel-intelligence` and assigned to Marcus alone. Also confirmed `output_desc` is never read into the model prompt at all for Intent-type Skills (`db-assembly.js`'s `typeSlug === "intent"` branch reads only `objective`/`method`/`traits.analysis_instructions`) — same shape as the unrelated `AA-167` finding, one Skill type over. `method` was the only viable target.

**Iteration on the fix itself, driven by John's own follow-up questions during the design walkthrough — not a single-shot design:**
1. First draft ("Our EMEA retail partner is Nordholm Retail Group, which is using 55%...") named the entity but John caught that it didn't establish the actual relationship — a bare name swap. Checked the real Data Room record (`the_library`, id `1c7104c5-9bc1-4ee7-9b61-d6070dc5aba8`, `data_type: synthesized`): Nordholm is described as "one of Apple's larger EMEA authorized resellers operating in Germany and the Netherlands." Revised the instruction to require pulling the entity's relationship/role from whatever the retrieved record actually says each time, not a hardcoded fact (a future partner will have a different relationship).
2. John then asked what "EMEA" itself is — confirmed it's a standard geographic/business-region abbreviation (Europe, the Middle East, and Africa), verified against `the_library`'s own `geo` column values (`Americas`, `Brazil`, `EMEA`, `EMEA Emerging`, `Europe`, `Greater China`, `India`, `Japan`, `Latin America`, `Southeast Asia` — a region list, not an organization list). John's resulting ask: spell out any abbreviation on first use per chat, abbreviate after — confirmed this is genuinely checkable, not just aspirational: `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`'s `conversationContext()` really does join every prior chat message into a `PRIOR CONVERSATION` section injected before `CURRENT TASK` (`db-assembly.js` lines 509-527) on every call.

**Coding session:** spawned via `Agent` tool into this same worktree. Ran the kickoff's dollar-quoted Supabase `UPDATE` (append-only, `ci-answer-intent.method`) via MCP `execute_sql`, then the Category F Node test (`test-CHI-19.mjs`, live REST fetch against the real row) — 10/10 PASS, confirming `output_desc`/`objective`/`traits.schema.required`/`guardrails` byte-identical pre/post. Deleted before commit. `git status` empty — zero `src`/`api` diffs, confirmed Supabase-content-only as scoped.

**Design session's own independent live verification against the real deployed dev preview, not accepted from the Node test alone — a Category L check, since the coding session's own test never exercised the real pipeline end to end:** the real EMEA/Nordholm co-op question, run fresh each time. Run 1 (original append): entity resolution fired correctly ("Nordholm Retail Group, one of Apple's larger EMEA authorized resellers operating in Germany and the Netherlands, is using 55%...") — but the abbreviation was never spelled out, even on a brand-new chat with no `PRIOR CONVERSATION` section to justify skipping it. Root-caused: the instruction only said what to do when `PRIOR CONVERSATION` shows a prior definition, never what to do when there's no `PRIOR CONVERSATION` section at all (the first-ever question) — confirmed the instruction really was present, correctly worded, in the assembled prompt via a local `assemblePrompt()` reconstruction (no live LLM call needed for that check), ruling out a wiring bug.

**Run 2** (tightened wording — added "regardless of whether the question itself already used that abbreviation" + explicit no-`PRIOR CONVERSATION` handling): same failure, "EMEA" still not expanded. **Run 3** (escalated to "you MUST... unconditionally... even though EMEA is common terminology"): same failure. Entity resolution held correctly across all three runs. Three different wordings failing identically ruled out simple phrasing ambiguity as the cause.

**Diagnostic run 4 (John's own hypothesis — tested, not assumed):** rather than a fourth prose rewrite, tested whether Marcus was anchoring on the retrieved chunk's own unexpanded "EMEA" phrasing. Temporarily edited the live `the_library` record to pre-expand it ("...one of Apple's larger Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) authorized resellers...") and re-ran the same question fresh. Result: Marcus's answer still compressed it back to bare "EMEA," even with the full expansion sitting directly in his retrieved context — ruling out source-anchoring as the mechanism. Reverted the diagnostic edit immediately after (`the_library` row confirmed byte-identical to its original via a `NOT LIKE`/`LIKE` round-trip check).

**Conclusion:** entity resolution is a genuine, reliable fix (4/4 live runs). Abbreviation-expansion-on-first-use is a real, repeatable model-default problem (0/4 across 3 prose wordings + 1 source-data test) that prose instructions — in either the Skill's `method` or the source data itself — don't reliably override. Also confirmed `guardrails.must`/`must_not` would not have helped even as an alternative lever: `request-receivable.js` shows those fields only drive a separate post-hoc Haiku validator that flags pass/fail after generation, never shaping what Marcus actually writes.

**Scope decision at close-out:** rather than ship a `method` field describing a capability that doesn't reliably work, trimmed the live text back to the entity-resolution instruction only (renamed "ENTITY RESOLUTION," dropped "& TERMINOLOGY"), with an inline note pointing to `CHI-22`. ## S-DAT-6-design / S-DAT-6 (v6.3.94, `addb9a2`, 2026-07-21, worktree `design-confirmation-uuid-0721`)

Found live during `CHI-42`'s own verification session (logged independently there as `AA-199`/`task_469f3123`, reconciled/superseded by this session's `DAT-6`/`LOO-17` before close-out — see `AA-199`'s row in `docs/FEATURES.md`). Traced end-to-end, not assumed: `writeLibrary()`'s `insert` operation (`lib/librarian.js`) ran a raw Postgres `the_library?id=eq.<supersedes_id>` lookup with zero UUID-format validation whenever `params.supersedes_id` was set. Live-reproduced twice against the real dev preview: a "Store as Forecast" commit on a hypothesis-test result populates `supersedes_id` with the new entry's own human-readable `chunk_id` slug (e.g. `geo-revenue-analysis-fy2025`), not a real row id, throwing Postgres `22P02`.

**Identified as the same bug shape `AA-189` (✅ Done) already fixed at a sibling call site** — `AA-189`'s own kickoff doc explicitly named `supersedes_id` as "the same category" as the `source_chunk_ids` guard it added to `writeTheReasoning()`, but didn't touch it, leaving this site unguarded. Fix mirrors `AA-189` exactly: a `UUID_RE` format check before the lookup, reusing the existing `denied-supersedes-cross-room` tier on a malformed id — no new response shape, no schema change, 1 file.

Node test 6/6 PASS, deleted before commit. `npm run build` clean. Version header updated on `lib/librarian.js`.

**Live QA completed in a follow-up verification pass (`verify-dat6-0721`, same day):** the first live click-through reached a new `ConfirmationCard` with the identical bug-shape `chunk_id`, confirming the repro path was real and current — but the follow-up write call hit real, live `Anthropic 529 overloaded` errors on 3 consecutive attempts (confirmed via raw network response bodies), external and unrelated to this fix, before ever reaching `writeLibrary()`. A dedicated follow-up session re-attempted the live UI flow and repeatedly landed on non-deterministic action types (`opinion`, a proofreader-rejected answer) that never reach `writeLibrary()` at all — traced the real delegation chain via direct Supabase schema reads (`data-patch-intent`'s `on_accept_intent_slug` → `data-patch-execute-intent`'s `analysis_instructions`: only `action:"promote"` triggers the `request_help`→`library-write-intent` chain that actually calls `writeLibrary()`). Constructed a `pending_confirmations` row directly, matching the exact original bug shape (`action:"promote"`, slug `chunk_id`, supersede `version_note`), and resolved it via the real deployed API (no UI, same production code path) — got the clean `{"error":"library-write handler: writeLibrary failed -- denied-supersedes-cross-room"}` (HTTP 500), not the raw `22P02` Postgres string, reproduced identically on a second attempt. Confirmation stayed `status:'pending'` throughout (this failure path throws synchronously, before any `durable_hops` checkpoint, so it never triggers `LOO-17`) — cleaned up via a normal Reject call, zero residue.

**Also found and logged, not fixed this session (deliberately split, one-feature-per-session discipline):** `LOO-17` — `resolveAccept()`/`markAcceptedDelegated()` flips a `pending_confirmations` row to `status:'accepted'` on a mere `durable_hops` checkpoint return (`{status:'in_progress', job_id}`), not only on a genuinely completed write. Confirmed live via direct Supabase query on 2 separate stuck rows (including one produced by this session's own Anthropic-overload hit) — `resolution` shows a stale in-progress checkpoint pointer while `status` already reads `accepted`, permanently blocking Edit/Reject (409) and turning further Accept clicks into retries of the same dead job. Generic to every `requires_human_confirmation` capability that can checkpoint, not specific to `DAT-6`. Needs its own design session — open question flagged to John: on a failed resume, revert the confirmation to `pending` (John's stated preference, matches `AA-189`'s existing "leave card open" precedent, zero new UI work) or a new distinct `accept_failed` status (more semantically precise, needs new UI treatment/approval). Logged as `LOO-17` in `docs/FEATURES.md`.

**Close-out:** `DAT-6` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` (code shipped + unit-tested + deployed + live-verified). `LOO-17` stays `❌ Missing`, queued as next design session on this track. `AA-199` marked superseded, pointing to both.

## S-LOO-17-design / S-LOO-17 (v6.3.102, `5ae8c2a`, 2026-07-21, worktree `design-loo-17-0721`)

Fixes the bug `DAT-6`'s own investigation surfaced and logged separately: `resolveAccept()` (`api/capabilities/execute.js`) treated any return from a delegated `on_accept_intent_slug` capability call as a completed accept — including a `durable_hops` checkpoint placeholder (`{status:'in_progress', job_id}`), not only a genuine result. Live Supabase rows confirmed this precisely: `status:'accepted'` with a stale in-progress checkpoint pointer stored as `resolution`, from calls whose actual resumed writes later failed. Once flipped, the confirmation was permanently stuck — Accept retries re-hit the same dead job, Edit/Reject both hard-failed 409. Generic to any `requires_human_confirmation` capability that can checkpoint, not `DAT-6`-specific.

**Design decision walked through live with John, not assumed:** on a failed resume, revert to `pending` (invisible, relies on a scrolling chat-error line) vs. a new `accept_failed` status (visible, needs new UI work later). John's explicit call: `accept_failed` — "give feedback to the user, and let them decide what to do next" needs an actually visible state, not a silent revert. Also confirmed live (`onResolveConfirmation`'s catch, `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`) exactly what revert-to-pending would have looked like before deciding, so the choice was grounded in the real current behavior, not a guess.

**Fix, 2 files, no schema change:**
- New transitional `accepting` status — set when the delegated call checkpoints, reusing the existing `resolution` jsonb column to hold the `job_id`. Blocks concurrent Edit/Reject exactly like `accepted` does today, so the fix doesn't introduce a new race during the wait.
- New terminal `accept_failed` status — closed out via a reverse `job_id` lookup (`getConfirmationByCheckpointJobId()`) added to the `continue` route handler: `markAcceptedDelegated()` on a genuine terminal success, `markAcceptFailed()` on a genuine terminal failure, no-op if it checkpoints again.
- **Same bug shape found at 2 more sites during Architect Review (multi-site check), fixed identically, not left as separate future bugs:** `resolveAccept()`'s own fast/synchronous failure path (a `runCapability()` throw that never even reaches a checkpoint — `HAR-8`'s 3 attempts already happened inside that one call), and `resolvePendingConfirmation()`'s plain accept path (used by any confirmed intent with no `on_accept_intent_slug` — this path can never checkpoint at all, `sendRequest()` has no loop).
- **Necessary completion, not optional:** the eligibility guard (`status !== 'pending'`) widened at all 3 check sites (`resolveAccept()`, `resolvePendingConfirmation()`, the `edit` route branch) to `['pending','accept_failed'].includes(status)` — without this, `accept_failed` would have been just as dead-ended as today's bug, defeating the entire point of adding it.

Entirely inside the confirmation layer — confirmed unnecessary to touch `runCapability()`/`runLoop()`/`checkpointAndReturn()`/`resumeCapability()`'s own internals or the `durable_hops` schema; the reverse lookup on the existing `resolution` column is sufficient. `accept_failed`'s own visual/UI treatment deliberately deferred — real UI work needing a mock + John's sign-off, not blocking this backend fix.

**Coding session note, found live during setup:** a local `PreToolUse` hook (`block-design-session-code.js`, `SES-010`) correctly blocked code edits from the `session/design-loo-17-0721` branch — the coding session resolved it exactly as intended (a fresh `session/coding-loo-17-0721` worktree/branch, removed after push), the same resolution pattern `S-CHI-43` already established.

Node test 11/11 PASS, deleted before commit. `npm run build` clean.

**Live QA in two passes, gap found and closed within this same session, not left open.** Coding session's own Category L proved the fast/synchronous-failure site directly: a real `pending_confirmations` row with a deliberately-broken `proposed_action` landed cleanly on `accept_failed` with a real error captured; a second Accept call against that same row retried (500) instead of 409ing; Reject on a separate `accept_failed` row resolved cleanly (200). Honestly flagged as *not* proving the checkpoint-then-resume site (Task 4's `continue`-branch close-out) — unit-test-only, not live-forceable on demand through the normal UI flow.
