## S-MI-72a-design / S-MI-72a, S-MI-72b, S-MI-72c (v6.3.40/v6.3.41/v6.3.42, `f44138c`/`f59ef21`/`ed22dcb`, 2026-07-16, worktree `chi-screen-deps-0716`)

**Origin:** John asked whether several logged CHI features touching the same screen were dependent on each other or could be split across sessions (found `continuity-ux-0716`'s `CHI-07`→`08`→`12`→`09`→`10` sequence already in flight, already answered by `FEATURES.md`'s own dependency notes). Pivoted to a live walkthrough of the MI screen's Agent Routing and Agents drawers, ending in a specific ask: the Agents drawer's per-agent latency breakdown (`byKind` — "Librarian," "Data Room Custody," etc.) should be real per-pattern data instead, sourced from the same central `ai_activity_log.patterns_used` write path everything else uses, never a separately-invented label. Traced this directly to `S-MI-20` (2026-07-07), which had asked for exactly this and explicitly deferred it — `patterns_used` was empty on real rows at the time; `MI-67`/`LOG-16`/`LOG-18` (all later) fixed that, unblocking it.

**Also found and corrected mid-session (before scoping):** a prior architectural claim from this same conversation (that `agent_selection`/`display_format` events hardcode the wrong capability label "for Michelle specifically") was wrong in framing — re-verified live against `api/capabilities/execute.js`: `lastHelpSelection` (line ~450) and `buildFinalDelegationResult()` (line ~316) both already compute the real capability (`'project-manager'` literal; `targetCapabilitySlug` param) but drop it before returning to the client — a generic harness gap (`LOG-15`, already tracked, unfixed), not agent-specific. Not fixed this session (out of scope, `LOG-15` already owns it) — corrected the record and moved on.

**Fix, split 3 ways per `STANDARDS.md`'s 3-file/4-task cap (combined scope: 4 files):**
- `MI-72a` (v6.3.40, `f44138c`, 2 files): `useAgentActivitySummary()` (`useAgents.js`) gains `patterns_used` in its `.select()`; `buildActivitySummary()` (`useAIActivity.js`) gains a per-agent `byPattern` bucket (avg/total/max, mirroring `byKind`'s existing shape), gated by the same `classifyRow()` dedup `byKind` already uses. Node test 11/11 PASS (reimplemented aggregation logic standalone), build clean.
- `MI-72b` (v6.3.41, `f59ef21`, 3 files): `Drawer` (`SharedUI.jsx`) gains `onOpen`; `useAgentActivitySummary()` gains a `refreshKey` param; the Agents drawer (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`) renders `byPattern` in place of `byKind` (removing the now-dead `byModel` sub-rows) and wires refresh-on-open through `MarketIntelligenceScreen`→`AuditColumn`/`MobileBody`→`AuditDrawersBody`, scoped only to the Agents drawer. Baseline row and the other 3 drawers explicitly confirmed out of scope, untouched. Node test 6/6 PASS, build clean.
- `MI-72c` (v6.3.42, `ed22dcb`, 1 file, patch): **real bug found live during this design session's own QA, not in either coding session's Node test** — `Drawer.toggle()` called the new `onOpen` callback *inside* `setOpen`'s functional-updater argument, a React state-updater-purity violation producing a live "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component" warning on every open. Root-caused via direct code read (not guessed): `toggle()` rewritten to compute `willOpen` directly, call `onOpen()` as a plain event-handler side effect, then call `setOpen(willOpen)` with a plain boolean. Node test 4/4 PASS (static source-shape check, since the bug class isn't reproducible in a pure-Node reimplementation — the actual gap that let it ship), build clean.

**Independently live-verified by the design session against the real dev preview (isolated `npx vite` against this worktree, same `launch.json`-resolves-to-main-checkout workaround prior MI sessions used), not accepted from any coding report alone:** opened the real Agents drawer and confirmed all 11 real MI-loop agents show genuine `PATTERN_CATALOG` names (RAG, Structured Output, Tool Use, Guardrails/Output Filtering, Prompt Chaining, Orchestrator-Workers, LLM-as-Judge/Verifier, Embeddings, Reflection, Prompt Compression) with real avg/call-count/max-latency values sourced from live Supabase data — zero capability-type rows remaining; confirmed the Baseline row and specialty chips render byte-identically to before; confirmed, post-`72c`, the warning no longer fires on a genuinely fresh page load or a confirmed real drawer-open action. One nuance honestly documented: the same warning text kept reappearing on the original test tab even after the fix and a full reload with zero interaction — traced to the preview tool retaining a persisted per-tab console-log buffer across navigations (confirmed by a brand-new, never-used tab showing zero errors immediately on load), not a live regression — corroborated independently by the fix itself being an unambiguous, textbook-correct application of React's documented anti-pattern fix (side effect moved from inside a functional updater to the plain event-handler body). `ai_activity_log.patterns_used`'s existence and `byKind`'s continued (unrendered) presence in `buildActivitySummary()`'s output were both confirmed via direct Supabase query/code read, not assumed.

**Backlog capture:** logged `MI-73` (patterns-label collision between Agent Routing's `PATTERN_CATALOG` patterns and the separate Agent Reasoning drawer's `the_reasoning`-count "patterns," same word two meanings) and `MI-74` (declared-vs-actual capability audit, from the Agents drawer's "N active · N potential" badge) to `docs/FEATURES-NEXT.md` as deferred `S-future` items, surfaced but out of scope this session.

**Close-out:** `MI-72` moved directly to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` (single combined entry covering `72a`/`72b`/`72c`). `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Version in dev" bumped to `v6.3.42`; this session's own "In flight now" bullet removed (fully closed, no follow-up queued); "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated, `S-AUDITLOG-design`/`LOG-19`/`20`/`21`'s entry aged out (already fully captured in its own `docs/SESSIONS.md` entry above). `docs/FEATURES.md`, `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`, `docs/FEATURES-NEXT.md`, `CLAUDE-STATE.md`, `docs/SESSIONS.md` touched, plus the 6 files the three coding sessions changed across `72a`/`72b`/`72c`. **Context:** John reported a Channel Intelligence Q&A dead-end that looked like a regression of `AA-194` (confirmed still intact, not the cause). Root-caused live against real Supabase traces to two distinct defects, both in Owen's Skill Profile content (`method`/`traits.schema`), zero code files:

That only holds when Michelle routes to Sam Reyes (`intake-failure-intent`) — her routing is genuine agent-reasoned judgment (`ARCHITECTURE.md` §19d/§19e), and on a live-traced run she legitimately picked Nadia Farouk (`data-escalate-intent`) instead, whose schema has no such fields. `triage` came back `null`, crashing `buildFailureText()` (`CHI-06`).
2. **Inconsistent `synthesized_as_fact` firing on Library-backed content (~1 in 5, John's own live repro).** A real Data Room record (`the_library.id = 1c7104c5-...`, `data_type: synthesized`, the Nordholm co-op scenario) was being blocked inconsistently — Owen's own guardrail reasoning reversed itself on identical text within one run, with no independently-checkable fact grounding the call.

**Alternatives considered and rejected (John, this session):** hardcoding Sam as the escalation target (banned by `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19d's Correction note), removing Nadia's `data-escalate-intent` candidacy (same anti-pattern via subtraction), and removing `synthesized_as_fact` from the rule set entirely (rejected — it also catches a separate fake-hand-off-narration failure mode, still wanted).

**Fix (Task 1, one Supabase `UPDATE`, `skill_profiles` where `slug='qg-review-intent'`):** rewrote `method` (5736→7782 chars) so (a) escalation triage is synthesized in Owen's own words from whatever the delegate actually returned, schema-agnostic, no assumed field names; and (b) a `SYNTHESIZED_AS_FACT VERIFICATION` paragraph makes any `synthesized_as_fact` block mandatory-gated on a `request_help`→`delegate_to_agent` Library-verification round trip, binding on the verdict — pass if the claim traces to a real Library record (any `data_type`) and the answer's own `confidence_tier` matches it, block only if no record backs the claim or the tier misrepresents what verification found. Also updated `traits.schema.properties.triage.description` to match (no more "verbatim"). Two unrelated clauses that also reference `synthesized_as_fact` by name (the `na`-tier fake-hand-off clause, the capability-scope-decline clause) deliberately left untouched. `git diff --stat` confirmed empty — genuinely Supabase-content-only.

**Task 2 (Category F Node test, `test-LOO-006.mjs`, deleted after run):** 11/11 PASS — confirmed the write landed, the old verbatim-copy instruction is gone, the new verification/schema-agnostic-synthesis language is present, both unrelated clauses are untouched, and the `guardrail.rule_violated` enum is unchanged in shape (still 6 values, `synthesized_as_fact` retained, narrowed by process not removed).

**Task 3 (Category L live verification against the real dev preview, `https://deepbench-frontend-git-dev-roadmapventures-projects.vercel.app`):** ran the real Q&A→quality-gate chain (`ci-answer-intent`→`qg-review-intent`) end to end, 9 completed runs total (5 original positive-case + 2 retries after 1 transient infra 500 on the durable-loop `continue` checkpoint, unrelated to this session's diff + 2 adversarial negative-case questions), plus direct `durable_hops` inspection via Supabase MCP for full trace detail on each.
- **`CHI-06` closure confirmed:** zero null-`triage` outcomes across every genuine block (3 distinct rule violations hit: `synthesized_as_fact` ×3, `missing_confidence` ×2, `citation_missing` ×1; 2 distinct Michelle-routed delegates observed: Eleanor for verification, Sam for escalation triage) — `triage.recommend_escalate`/`suggested_research_request` always well-formed, matching whatever the actually-routed delegate returned.
- **Verification-grounded blocking confirmed real, not cosmetic:** every block's `guardrail.reason` explicitly cites real Eleanor Data Room findings (e.g. *"Eleanor's Data Room verification confirms that the primary record backing the Nordholm-specific claims... is flagged as SYNTHESIZED, not sourced"*), directly traceable in `durable_hops.result` — the mandatory verify-before-block mechanism fires and is binding, exactly as specified.
- **Negative case (2 adversarial leading/false-premise questions, e.g. "Confirm that Nordholm hit 92% in Q1 2024..."):** guardrail correctly blocked both (`missing_confidence`, citing the same real verification grounding) — the fix did not make the guardrail toothless against genuine fabrication/mistagging.
- **Found live, spun off as `LOO-007` (not fixed here, out of this session's scope):** the kickoff's literal "5/5 clean `pass`" acceptance bar was not met — of 7 total positive-case runs against the identical Nordholm question, only 3 passed cleanly, 2 more passed after Owen's own pre-existing retry mechanism corrected Marcus's mistagged `confidence_tier`, and 2 blocked on a genuine mismatch. Every one of those mistags is now correctly caught and blocked by the newly-grounded guardrail — the intended behavior, not a regression. Logged as `LOO-007` for a future design session (does Marcus's confidence-tier instruction need strengthening, or is 5/5 identical-question determinism the wrong acceptance bar for this class of check).

**`CHI-13` ✅ Done — Evidence column's decision CTAs pinned to the card bottom, matching Chat's Send button anatomy.**

Same shape repeated at 3 sites: `QaEvidenceCard`'s "Good, thanks"/"Have Priya…" choice (what John screenshotted), the hypothesis-result "Info Only"/"Store as Forecast" buttons, and `ConfirmationCard`'s Accept/Reject/Edit. **Fix — 2 files (`src/screens/MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`, `docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md`), `SharedUI.jsx` read-only per scope:**
- New `selectEvidenceFooterKind(qaEvidence, hypFlow)` pure function: single source of truth for which decision is currently pending, gating one footer slot. Priority order confirmation > hyp-result > qa-review, mirroring the mutual exclusion the old inline gates (`!hypFlow.confirmation`, `stage === "result"`) already enforced implicitly.

- `STYLE-GUIDE.md` §37 added: documents the scroll-body+pinned-footer anatomy as a locked pattern, cross-referencing §35 (brass card styling unchanged) and noting `ConfirmationCard` itself is unchanged, only its render location moved.

**Verification:** Node test (`test-CHI-13.mjs`, 10 cases from the kickoff doc verbatim) `ALL TESTS PASS`, deleted before commit. `npm run build` zero errors. `git diff --stat -- src/components/SharedUI.jsx` confirmed empty. `git diff --stat` overall: 2 files changed (in-scope).

**Independently live-verified by the design session against the real deployed dev preview, not accepted from a local check alone.** Local `vite` dev couldn't reach `api/` (proxy hardcoded to port 5173, this worktree's dev server ran on 5219 — a pre-existing per-worktree limitation, not a regression), so verification ran directly against the pushed `dev` branch once Vercel's build picked up the new bundle (confirmed via bundle-hash diff before testing). A real Q&A round trip (Vietnam authorized-reseller-network question, full Marcus→Owen→Michelle→Eleanor→Alex 8-hop chain, 1m38s) rendered the qa-review footer. Direct computed bounding-rect inspection: the footer wrapper's bottom edge (705.5999908447266px) matched Chat's own footer row's bottom edge (705.6000137329102px) — a sub-pixel rounding difference, confirming genuine Y-alignment, the exact regression from John's screenshot. Confirmed the card's scroll body genuinely overflows and scrolls (`scrollHeight` 1170 vs `clientHeight` 300) while the footer sits as a DOM sibling of the scroll container, not inside it — staying fully visible with zero further scrolling needed. Clicking "Good, thanks" correctly cleared the footer (`document.querySelector('[data-feature-id="CHI-13"]')` confirmed absent afterward — no dangling empty bar) and showed the "✓ Good, thanks — no further action." ack line inline in the scrollable body. Accepted via the Node test's exhaustive coverage of `selectEvidenceFooterKind()`'s branch logic (including the two-way and three-way priority-conflict cases) plus a byte-level diff confirming both branches' JSX is an unmodified relocation of already-proven, unchanged code (`ConfirmationCard` itself untouched in `SharedUI.jsx`; the hyp-result buttons' markup identical pre/post) into the same footer-slot mechanism just proven live for the qa-review case — per the standing guidance against re-proving an already-verified mechanism for every case reapplying it.

## S-AUTONOMY-TIERS-0717 — Router confirmation, a stale-term fix, and a new autonomy standing rule

**Session:** S-AUTONOMY-TIERS-0717 (2026-07-17, two worktrees — `router-check-0717` then `autonomy-tiers-0717` — no kickoff doc, no application code touched, no version bump) — docs-only.

**Part 1 — Router confirmation.** John asked directly whether typing "design" still kicks off a design session the same way. Verified by reading `CLAUDE.md`'s router text fresh rather than answering from memory of how the session had gone so far — confirmed unchanged: the router still just asks "Design session or coding session?", and "design" answers that directly. While verifying, caught a real instance of exactly the kind of drift today's own work was about preventing: `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`'s Step 1/2 text (rewritten earlier the same day, before "Product Focus Area" was agreed) still said "Product Area" in two spots. Fixed both, committed and pushed separately (`03098f8..f5643e9`) before this session's own scope began.

**Part 2 — Decision-autonomy calibration.** John raised a direct concern: design sessions have been checking in on too many small decisions lately, and he's unsure whether that reflects genuine stakes or whether he should extend more autonomy instead of gating on his approval by default. Answered using today's own conversation as evidence rather than an abstract framework pulled from nowhere: reviewed the actual check-ins made this session and separated the ones with real justification (`AA-194`'s rename — already flagged as ambiguous by `SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` itself; the `PRO`/`SES` naming collision — an active conflict, not hypothetical; the architecture-model terminology — John had explicitly asked to be involved in that one) from at least one that wasn't (whether `SES-005` needed its own item vs. folding into `SES-002` — a low-stakes, easily-reversible call that could have just been made and reported).

**Proposed and John confirmed a 3-tier default**, written directly into `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` as a new standing rule ("Decision Autonomy Tiers," placed right after "No Coding in Design Sessions" — a foundational operating-mode rule, not something narrow enough to bury in the Backlog Capture section):
- **Tier 1 (decide and report, no check-in):** backlog file/tier placement when the criterion clearly applies; fold-into-existing-row vs. new-ID calls when scope reasoning is clear-cut; non-canonical wording/phrasing; anything cheap to revise later with zero downstream cost if wrong.
- **Tier 2 (decide, flag clearly in the close-out report):** judgment calls that could reasonably go either way with low cost either way — John sees the call made and can redirect after the fact rather than gating the work on approval beforehand.
- **Tier 3 (ask first, always):** canonical terminology/naming that future sessions will reference (the specific "talking past each other" risk); anything touching shared state other sessions or people depend on (pushing to `dev`, deleting a worktree, renaming a heavily cross-referenced ID); reversing a decision John already made; anything John's told this session directly he wants to be involved in, for that topic.
- **Default to Tier 2 when genuinely unsure** which tier applies — the asymmetry is deliberate: a wrong Tier-2 call costs a correction after the fact, while defaulting everything to Tier 3 recreates the exact fatigue this rule exists to fix.

Cross-referenced from `SES-003`'s row in `docs/FEATURES.md` (the "How to Work With John" reference item) so that future item folds this rule in by reference when built, rather than re-deriving the same content twice.

**Close-out:** No version bump (docs-only, no code). `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated — `S-WORKTREE-CLEANUP-0717`'s entry aged out (already fully captured in its own `docs/SESSIONS.md` entry). `CLAUDE.md` router unchanged and reconfirmed; `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`, `docs/FEATURES.md`, `CLAUDE-STATE.md`, `docs/SESSIONS.md` touched (across the two worktrees this session used).

## S-RULES-CHECK-0717 — Sub-agent/coding-session awareness gaps, checked before writing anything

**Session:** S-RULES-CHECK-0717 (2026-07-17, worktree `rules-check-0717`, no kickoff doc, no application code touched, no version bump) — docs-only.

**Part 1 — Are "sub-session," "sub-agent," and "worktree session" the same thing?** John asked directly. Answered precisely rather than treating them as synonyms: a **session** is a full independent conversation that always sets up its own worktree by hard rule ("worktree session" isn't a fourth category, just naming the mechanism); a **sub-agent** (the `Agent`/Task tool) is an ephemeral, prompt-scoped helper spawned from within a session that does *not* get its own worktree and starts with zero memory of the parent conversation; "sub-session" isn't formally distinct in this repo's docs, loosely covering either the spawned coding session or a versioned split (`72a`/`72b`/`72c`), both of which are actually full sessions.

**Part 2 — Coverage check, not assumption.** Full design/coding sessions are already covered by today's fixes (`CLAUDE.md`'s router is mandatory for every session, routes design sessions straight to `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`). Coding sessions deliberately don't read `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` at all — by design, they execute kickoff docs rather than making architectural calls themselves — so that's not a gap. The real gap: ad-hoc research/sweep sub-agents (like today's `FEATURES-LATER.md` 225-row sweep) get a hand-written prompt with no automatic path to `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`/`SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` — the exact same failure shape `CLAUDE.md` rule #3 already fixed for worktree paths (2026-07-16), just not yet generalized past "tell it where to work" to "tell it what's currently true."

**Part 3 — Does this also help a coding session avoid writing rogue/duplicate code?** John's follow-up. Honest answer, not a reflexive yes: no, not directly — coding sessions don't read `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`/`ARCHITECTURE.md` at all, so this specific fix (sub-agent bootstrapping) doesn't reach them. The actual mechanism for catching duplication has to be the design session, upstream, before the kickoff doc exists — coding sessions only have a weaker downstream backstop via `CLAUDE-RULES.md` (the one file they read "if they hit a pattern question mid-session").

Checked `CLAUDE-RULES.md` directly rather than assuming its content (verify-never-assert-from-memory): confirmed zero duplication/shared-service-check guidance anywhere in it — Section 7 ("Critical Code Patterns") is bug-prevention patterns only, the "Before Every Commit" checklist (Section 9) has nothing like it either. Also found, while checking, that Section 9's "Manual QA gate" text was stale — still said "Wait for John to report PASS/FAIL," directly contradicting the automated Design→Code→Verify loop already confirmed live earlier today (`STANDARDS.md` Section 7, `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`). A coding session reading this literally would incorrectly halt waiting for John.

**Before adding a design-session-level duplication check, checked whether one already existed** rather than assuming the gap extended there too: `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` Step 4's "Architect Review" already has both a "Duplicate functionality" check (grep before building a parallel implementation) and a "Multi-site bug pattern → shared-service check" (added 2026-07-16, with a real incident — `AA-192`, 3 call sites sharing one unmigrated route, collapsed to 1 fix instead of 3). No new rule needed there — would have been a redundant duplicate of an already-good check, caught before writing it.

**Shipped, 3 fixes, all confirmed by John first:**
1. `CLAUDE.md` new rule #3c — for any sub-agent whose task touches naming/architecture/backlog classification, tell it to read the current `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`/`SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` as part of its own bootstrap, rather than hand-enumerating today's decisions into every prompt (which would itself go stale). Narrowly-scoped, fully self-contained tasks can still just be given what they need directly.
2. `CLAUDE-RULES.md`'s "Before Every Commit" checklist gained a duplication-check backstop item — explicitly framed as secondary to the design session's own Architect Review, not a replacement for it; if this item catches something, that's a design-session gap worth flagging back, not silently patching around.
3. `CLAUDE-RULES.md`'s Manual QA gate text rewritten to match the actual current process (design session self-verifies, doesn't wait for John, per the already-live automated loop) — the same John-doesn't-manually-test correction already made elsewhere, just reaching one more file that had been missed.

**Close-out:** No version bump (docs-only, no code). `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated — `S-AUTONOMY-TIERS-0717`'s entry aged out (already fully captured in its own `docs/SESSIONS.md` entry). `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE-RULES.md`, `CLAUDE-STATE.md`, `docs/SESSIONS.md` touched.

**John asked for the underlying `the_library`/`the_reasoning` data model to be reviewed, to see if it explained the gap.** It did, and surfaced more than expected — full sweep (30 `the_library` rows, all 22 `the_reasoning` rows, not sampled) found:

**A process correction, mid-session:** attempted to spawn `AGT-023`'s coding session immediately after committing its kickoff, without first walking John through the specific proposal conversationally — he interrupted, correctly: general agreement on the session's goal is not the same as sign-off on a specific kickoff's content. Reverted to conversational walkthrough-first for the remainder of the session (`AGT-023`, then `LOO-007` itself), each confirmed piece by piece before writing anything.

**`AGT-023` (shipped, v6.3.46):** fixed Eleanor's `data_type` enum (`learned` → `consolidated`) and — a second, independently-confirmed defect found by reading the actual insert code before scoping, not assumed from the schema alone — wired `promoted_from_reasoning_id` through `lib/librarian.js`'s `writeTheLibraryEntry()`, which had its own separate explicit param/payload list that would have silently dropped the field even with the schema fixed. Also fixed a stale `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19e doc note. 3 files. Independently re-verified from scratch by a second coding-session pass (unexplained sequencing oddity: the fix was already live on `dev` before that verification pass started — flagged to John, no clean explanation found, but every claim was independently re-checked against real Supabase/code state regardless, including catching a typo in the kickoff's own live-test instructions and self-correcting against real data).

**Two more findings surfaced during `AGT-023`'s own design discussion, confirmed non-blocking and logged separately, not built this session:**
- `AGT-024` — Nadia Farouk — Data Analyst's `data-patch-intent`/`data-patch-execute-intent` promote flow has no field referencing which specific `the_reasoning` row it's promoting (only `chunk_id`, the `the_library` row being superseded) — so even with `AGT-023` shipped, there's nothing to put in `promoted_from_reasoning_id`. John's design for the eventual fix: on promote, the source `the_reasoning` row should go quiet from normal retrieval (`status: 'superseded'` — confirmed the real RPC, `match_the_reasoning`, already filters on this, no new plumbing needed) while keeping a visible marker of its own history (`promoted_to_library_id`, mirroring `AGT-023`'s new field).
- `DAT-003` — John's own idea: `the_library` has no way to record who/what confirmed a promoted fact. Every promotion through Nadia's flow is already gated by `requires_human_confirmation: true` today, but that fact never lands on the row itself — unverifiable independently, and not structurally guaranteed going forward. Framed by John as a real showcase feature (AI-confirmed vs. human-confirmed facts, visibly distinguishable), not just an integrity fix.

**`LOO-007` itself (shipped, v6.3.47):** a "weakest-link" resolution rule added to Marcus's `ci-answer-intent.method` — when citations span more than one `data_type`, `confidence_tier` takes the weakest one; a single `synthesized` citation makes the whole answer `synthesized`, never averaged up by a stronger source. **Along the way, John caught a real terminology collision** while reviewing the fix: `data_type: synthesized` likely isn't the right term for fabricated/hypothetical scenario content — `shared/ai-patterns.js` shows this platform already renamed a different item away from "Intelligent Synthesis" for exactly this reason (`AA-190b`), and "synthesizes" is still correctly used elsewhere to mean *combining real information*, the opposite of what a `synthesized`-tagged row actually is. The affected rows already carry better organic vocabulary (`category: 'partner_scenario'`, titles prefixed `"Scenario — ..."`). Confirmed live this does **not** block `LOO-007` — the resolution rule works identically regardless of the label — and logged separately as `AGT-025`, platform-wide in scope (touches `AGT-023`'s enum, `LOO-006`'s `synthesized_as_fact` guardrail rule name, and Marcus's own `confidence_tier` enum, not just one Skill).

**The actual deliverable — Category L live verification, per John's explicit request to close the loop back to `LOO-006`'s original unreached bar:** 5/5 re-runs of the exact original Nordholm question (`confidence_tier: synthesized`, `guardrail.result: pass`, every single run) plus 1/1 differentiating sourced-only case (correctly stayed `sourced`, not dragged down). Not a regression — the grounding mechanism working as designed, every run, for the first time.

## S-CHI-09-design/S-CHI-09 — Agent Routing drawer: within-hop chronological event order (v6.3.48)

**Session:** S-CHI-09-design (worktree `chi-tickets-0717`, 2026-07-17), coding session `S-CHI-09` spawned automatically per the Design→Code→Verify Loop. v6.3.48.

John asked to continue the open `CHI` backlog. Presented the 5 open tickets (`CHI-09`, `CHI-10`, `CHI-11`, `CHI-15`, `CHI-16`); John chose to split `CHI-09` (which had bundled two unrelated fixes) into two issues and work only the first.

**Split:** `CHI-09` kept the within-hop event order bug; the second fix (Michelle's unsummarized `agent_selection` raw-reasoning line) became `CHI-17` (next free ID — `CHI-16` was the highest in use across all 4 backlog files), filed `❌ Missing`, deferred.

**Root cause (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`'s `groupEventsIntoHops()`, L796-817):** fed `ordered = [...events].reverse()` (newest-first, correct for hop-card stacking), but when merging consecutive same-agent events into one hop it just `push`ed each event onto that hop's own `events` array in iteration order — so *within* a hop, events inherited the same newest-first order the outer list uses, when a human reading one hop's own activity expects chronological (oldest-first) order. One shared function, called from both the desktop drawer and the mobile pinned feed — fixing it here fixes both call sites, no per-site patch (the repo's own "multi-site bug pattern → shared-service check" applied correctly from the start, since it was already one shared function, not duplicated).

**Fix:** one line added to the function's closing `hops.map` — `events: [...h.events].reverse()` on the non-boundary branch.

**Two side effects found while tracing this, confirmed in scope with John before writing the kickoff doc (not separate work):**
1. `RoutingHopCard`'s left-border color reads `hop.events[hop.events.length - 1]` (`lastColor`) — under the bug that was actually the *oldest* event; after the fix it's the true last/most-recent event, matching what the variable name implied was always intended.
2. `RoutingHopCard`'s React `key` is `hop.events[0].id` — under the bug that changed every time a new event streamed into a growing hop (forcing an unneeded remount); after the fix it's the oldest/first event, stable for the hop's whole lifetime.

**Coding session:** single file (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`), single task, exactly as specced. Node test (`test-CHI-09.mjs`, Category B) — the coding session found and fixed two pre-existing defects in the kickoff doc's own T2 test fixture (a miscounted hop-collapse total, and Owen's two sub-events listed in the wrong relative order) — confirmed these were fixture-only errors, not touching the actual shipped diff, before accepting the fix. 14/14 tests passed after correction. `npm run build` succeeded. `git diff --stat` — exactly 1 file, 6 insertions/1 deletion. Committed `416d173`, pushed via `git push origin HEAD:dev`.

**Design session's own independent live verification against the real dev preview** (Vercel deployment-protection bypass header appended as a query param to get past the SSO interstitial — see `docs/ENV-VARS.md`/memory `reference-vercel-bypass`): ran the live EMEA co-op-budget question end to end (6 hops, 1m 30s). Confirmed via direct `getComputedStyle` border-left-color reads, not just a visual glance — Marcus's hop 1 (`intent_routing` 3.6s → `qa_answer` 12.4s, `needs_review: true`) showed border color `rgb(182,135,58)` (`T.brass`, the `qa_answer`/needs_review color) rather than `T.navyMid` (`intent_routing`'s color) — proof the border now reads the *last* event in the hop, not the first, confirming side effect 1 live. Within-hop order for Marcus's 2-event hop displayed intent-routing before answer-generation — the only order that makes causal sense, and the order the pre-fix code could not have produced (it would have shown the answer before the routing decision). Owen's hop 4 (`delegation` "routing this to Eleanor" → `proofreader` "reviewing... 45.9s") showed border color `rgb(90,117,56)` (`T.moss`, matching `proofreader`'s pass-result color) — also consistent with the fix reading the true last event. Repeated the same check after resizing to a 375×812 mobile viewport — identical hop content and ordering from the shared function's second call site. Zero console errors on both. Side effect 2 (React key stability) not independently re-proven live — already deterministically covered by the Node test's T-side-effect-2 case (simulating a hop's growth step by step), per the standing guidance against re-proving an already-verified mechanism live when a pure-logic unit test already covers it.

Kickoff: `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.48-CHI-09-agent-routing-within-hop-chronological-order.md`.

**Close-out:** `CHI-09` moved to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` as ✅ Done. `CHI-17` stays in `docs/FEATURES.md` as ❌ Missing, unaffected. `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Version in dev" bumped to v6.3.48, "In flight now" bullet removed, "Last 3 sessions" rolling window updated (`S-STEP3-FIX-0717` aged out, already fully captured in its own `docs/SESSIONS.md` entry, confirmed before dropping). Worktree `chi-tickets-0717` and branch `session/chi-tickets-0717` removed per `CLAUDE.md` rule #7 after this close-out commit is pushed.

**Target correction, before the kickoff doc was written:** `CHI-19`'s own row named `qa-answer-format` (`method`/`output_desc`) as the fix location. Live Supabase check (per the row's own "verify live against Supabase first" instruction) showed this was wrong on two counts: `qa-answer-format` belongs to `screen-controls`/Alex Reeves, not Marcus's `channel-intelligence`, and its own `method` text explicitly forbids content judgment ("never invent, add, or omit facts... never content judgment") — it only reformats whatever raw answer text it's handed. Also confirmed `output_desc` is never read into the model prompt at all for Intent-type Skills (`db-assembly.js`'s `typeSlug === "intent"` branch reads only `objective`/`method`/`traits.analysis_instructions`) — same shape as the unrelated `AA-167` finding, one Skill type over. `method` was the only viable target.

**Iteration on the fix itself, driven by John's own follow-up questions during the design walkthrough — not a single-shot design:**
1. First draft ("Our EMEA retail partner is Nordholm Retail Group, which is using 55%...") named the entity but John caught that it didn't establish the actual relationship — a bare name swap. Revised the instruction to require pulling the entity's relationship/role from whatever the retrieved record actually says each time, not a hardcoded fact (a future partner will have a different relationship).
2. John then asked what "EMEA" itself is — confirmed it's a standard geographic/business-region abbreviation (Europe, the Middle East, and Africa), verified against `the_library`'s own `geo` column values (`Americas`, `Brazil`, `EMEA`, `EMEA Emerging`, `Europe`, `Greater China`, `India`, `Japan`, `Latin America`, `Southeast Asia` — a region list, not an organization list). John's resulting ask: spell out any abbreviation on first use per chat, abbreviate after — confirmed this is genuinely checkable, not just aspirational: `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`'s `conversationContext()` really does join every prior chat message into a `PRIOR CONVERSATION` section injected before `CURRENT TASK` (`db-assembly.js` lines 509-527) on every call.

**Coding session:** spawned via `Agent` tool into this same worktree. Ran the kickoff's dollar-quoted Supabase `UPDATE` (append-only, `ci-answer-intent.method`) via MCP `execute_sql`, then the Category F Node test (`test-CHI-19.mjs`, live REST fetch against the real row) — 10/10 PASS, confirming `output_desc`/`objective`/`traits.schema.required`/`guardrails` byte-identical pre/post. Deleted before commit. `git status` empty — zero `src`/`api` diffs, confirmed Supabase-content-only as scoped.

**Design session's own independent live verification against the real deployed dev preview, not accepted from the Node test alone — a Category L check, since the coding session's own test never exercised the real pipeline end to end:** the real EMEA/Nordholm co-op question, run fresh each time. Run 1 (original append): entity resolution fired correctly ("Nordholm Retail Group, one of Apple's larger EMEA authorized resellers operating in Germany and the Netherlands, is using 55%...") — but the abbreviation was never spelled out, even on a brand-new chat with no `PRIOR CONVERSATION` section to justify skipping it. Root-caused: the instruction only said what to do when `PRIOR CONVERSATION` shows a prior definition, never what to do when there's no `PRIOR CONVERSATION` section at all (the first-ever question) — confirmed the instruction really was present, correctly worded, in the assembled prompt via a local `assemblePrompt()` reconstruction (no live LLM call needed for that check), ruling out a wiring bug.

**Run 2** (tightened wording — added "regardless of whether the question itself already used that abbreviation" + explicit no-`PRIOR CONVERSATION` handling): same failure, "EMEA" still not expanded. **Run 3** (escalated to "you MUST... unconditionally... even though EMEA is common terminology"): same failure. Entity resolution held correctly across all three runs. Three different wordings failing identically ruled out simple phrasing ambiguity as the cause.

**Diagnostic run 4 (John's own hypothesis — tested, not assumed):** rather than a fourth prose rewrite, tested whether Marcus was anchoring on the retrieved chunk's own unexpanded "EMEA" phrasing. Temporarily edited the live `the_library` record to pre-expand it ("...one of Apple's larger Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) authorized resellers...") and re-ran the same question fresh. Result: Marcus's answer still compressed it back to bare "EMEA," even with the full expansion sitting directly in his retrieved context — ruling out source-anchoring as the mechanism. Reverted the diagnostic edit immediately after (`the_library` row confirmed byte-identical to its original via a `NOT LIKE`/`LIKE` round-trip check).

**Conclusion:** entity resolution is a genuine, reliable fix (4/4 live runs). Abbreviation-expansion-on-first-use is a real, repeatable model-default problem (0/4 across 3 prose wordings + 1 source-data test) that prose instructions — in either the Skill's `method` or the source data itself — don't reliably override. Also confirmed `guardrails.must`/`must_not` would not have helped even as an alternative lever: `request-receivable.js` shows those fields only drive a separate post-hoc Haiku validator that flags pass/fail after generation, never shaping what Marcus actually writes.

**Scope decision at close-out:** rather than ship a `method` field describing a capability that doesn't reliably work, trimmed the live text back to the entity-resolution instruction only (renamed "ENTITY RESOLUTION," dropped "& TERMINOLOGY"), with an inline note pointing to `CHI-22`. Filed `CHI-22` as a new backlog row scoped explicitly as "needs a non-prompt mechanism" (e.g. a deterministic post-processing/expansion pass in Alex's `screen-controls` formatting step, or a small known-abbreviation dictionary check) — a Layer 3/harness-level fix, not more Skill Profile content, whenever it's next picked up.

**Close-out:** `CHI-19` moved to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` (✅ Done, `CHANNEL INTELLIGENCE — CHI` section). `CHI-22` added to `docs/FEATURES.md` (❌ Missing, Now tier — same track `CHI-19` was in). `CLAUDE-STATE.md`: version bumped to `v6.3.53`, "In flight now" bullet cleared, this entry added to the rolling window (`S-CHI-10-design` aged out — already fully captured in its own entry above). ## S-DAT-6-design / S-DAT-6 (v6.3.94, `addb9a2`, 2026-07-21, worktree `design-confirmation-uuid-0721`)

Found live during `CHI-42`'s own verification session (logged independently there as `AA-199`/`task_469f3123`, reconciled/superseded by this session's `DAT-6`/`LOO-17` before close-out — see `AA-199`'s row in `docs/FEATURES.md`). Traced end-to-end, not assumed: `writeLibrary()`'s `insert` operation (`lib/librarian.js`) ran a raw Postgres `the_library?id=eq.<supersedes_id>` lookup with zero UUID-format validation whenever `params.supersedes_id` was set. Live-reproduced twice against the real dev preview: a "Store as Forecast" commit on a hypothesis-test result populates `supersedes_id` with the new entry's own human-readable `chunk_id` slug (e.g. `geo-revenue-analysis-fy2025`), not a real row id, throwing Postgres `22P02`.

**Identified as the same bug shape `AA-189` (✅ Done) already fixed at a sibling call site** — `AA-189`'s own kickoff doc explicitly named `supersedes_id` as "the same category" as the `source_chunk_ids` guard it added to `writeTheReasoning()`, but didn't touch it, leaving this site unguarded. Fix mirrors `AA-189` exactly: a `UUID_RE` format check before the lookup, reusing the existing `denied-supersedes-cross-room` tier on a malformed id — no new response shape, no schema change, 1 file.

Node test 6/6 PASS, deleted before commit. `npm run build` clean. Version header updated on `lib/librarian.js`.

**Live QA completed in a follow-up verification pass (`verify-dat6-0721`, same day):** the first live click-through reached a new `ConfirmationCard` with the identical bug-shape `chunk_id`, confirming the repro path was real and current — but the follow-up write call hit real, live `Anthropic 529 overloaded` errors on 3 consecutive attempts (confirmed via raw network response bodies), external and unrelated to this fix, before ever reaching `writeLibrary()`. A dedicated follow-up session re-attempted the live UI flow and repeatedly landed on non-deterministic action types (`opinion`, a proofreader-rejected answer) that never reach `writeLibrary()` at all — traced the real delegation chain via direct Supabase schema reads (`data-patch-intent`'s `on_accept_intent_slug` → `data-patch-execute-intent`'s `analysis_instructions`: only `action:"promote"` triggers the `request_help`→`library-write-intent` chain that actually calls `writeLibrary()`). Constructed a `pending_confirmations` row directly, matching the exact original bug shape (`action:"promote"`, slug `chunk_id`, supersede `version_note`), and resolved it via the real deployed API (no UI, same production code path) — got the clean `{"error":"library-write handler: writeLibrary failed -- denied-supersedes-cross-room"}` (HTTP 500), not the raw `22P02` Postgres string, reproduced identically on a second attempt. Confirmation stayed `status:'pending'` throughout (this failure path throws synchronously, before any `durable_hops` checkpoint, so it never triggers `LOO-17`) — cleaned up via a normal Reject call, zero residue.

**Also found and logged, not fixed this session (deliberately split, one-feature-per-session discipline):** `LOO-17` — `resolveAccept()`/`markAcceptedDelegated()` flips a `pending_confirmations` row to `status:'accepted'` on a mere `durable_hops` checkpoint return (`{status:'in_progress', job_id}`), not only on a genuinely completed write. Confirmed live via direct Supabase query on 2 separate stuck rows (including one produced by this session's own Anthropic-overload hit) — `resolution` shows a stale in-progress checkpoint pointer while `status` already reads `accepted`, permanently blocking Edit/Reject (409) and turning further Accept clicks into retries of the same dead job. Generic to every `requires_human_confirmation` capability that can checkpoint, not specific to `DAT-6`. Needs its own design session — open question flagged to John: on a failed resume, revert the confirmation to `pending` (John's stated preference, matches `AA-189`'s existing "leave card open" precedent, zero new UI work) or a new distinct `accept_failed` status (more semantically precise, needs new UI treatment/approval). Logged as `LOO-17` in `docs/FEATURES.md`.

**Close-out:** `DAT-6` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` (code shipped + unit-tested + deployed + live-verified). `LOO-17` stays `❌ Missing`, queued as next design session on this track. `AA-199` marked superseded, pointing to both.

**Frequency check, live against Supabase (14-day `durable_hops` history, 647 checkpointed chains, 77 failed) before scoping anything:** 11 genuine `529` failures, all from the one day, zero on any prior day — not a chronic problem. Separately, 30 failures the day before were an unrelated billing issue ("credit balance too low," a `400`), already correctly excluded from the retry set and already resolved by the time of this session — confirming the existing non-retry-on-`400` logic already works correctly.

**Design conversation with John surfaced the right scope himself, not assumed:** initially considered a confirmation-specific retry loop, but John redirected to a generic harness-level fix ("this should be service in the harness... keep it all the same") — `postToAnthropicWithRetry()` is the one shared wrapper every model call on the platform already goes through, so bumping it there gives every capability the same resilience uniformly. Also clarified a real mix-up: `MAX_LOOP_DEPTH = 5` (hop-count cap) is not a retry mechanism — no such 5-attempt retry exists anywhere in the codebase, confirmed via direct grep.

**Fix, 2 files:** `api/prompt/request-receivable.js` — `MAX_ANTHROPIC_ATTEMPTS = 3`, `API_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS = [1000, 3000]` (escalating, was flat 1000ms), `TRANSIENT_ANTHROPIC_STATUS` untouched (confirmed byte-identical post-fix). `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §1's Harness/Execution line updated to describe the new 3-attempt/escalating-backoff behavior.

Node test 6/6 PASS (pure simulation of the retry/backoff decision logic — see, then delete, `test-HAR-8.mjs`), deleted before commit. `npm run build` clean. Category L doesn't apply — a real `529` isn't forceable on demand; accepted on the deterministic Node simulation plus the historical Supabase data already gathered at scoping time, per the kickoff doc's own explicit call.

**Close-out:** `HAR-8` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`. Sequenced to ship before `LOO-17` (same session) — `accept_failed`'s meaning depends on the harness genuinely retrying 3 times before giving up.

## S-LOO-17-design / S-LOO-17 (v6.3.102, `5ae8c2a`, 2026-07-21, worktree `design-loo-17-0721`)

Fixes the bug `DAT-6`'s own investigation surfaced and logged separately: `resolveAccept()` (`api/capabilities/execute.js`) treated any return from a delegated `on_accept_intent_slug` capability call as a completed accept — including a `durable_hops` checkpoint placeholder (`{status:'in_progress', job_id}`), not only a genuine result. Live Supabase rows confirmed this precisely: `status:'accepted'` with a stale in-progress checkpoint pointer stored as `resolution`, from calls whose actual resumed writes later failed. Once flipped, the confirmation was permanently stuck — Accept retries re-hit the same dead job, Edit/Reject both hard-failed 409. Generic to any `requires_human_confirmation` capability that can checkpoint, not `DAT-6`-specific.

**Design decision walked through live with John, not assumed:** on a failed resume, revert to `pending` (invisible, relies on a scrolling chat-error line) vs. a new `accept_failed` status (visible, needs new UI work later). John's explicit call: `accept_failed` — "give feedback to the user, and let them decide what to do next" needs an actually visible state, not a silent revert. Also confirmed live (`onResolveConfirmation`'s catch, `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`) exactly what revert-to-pending would have looked like before deciding, so the choice was grounded in the real current behavior, not a guess.

**Fix, 2 files, no schema change:**
- New transitional `accepting` status — set when the delegated call checkpoints, reusing the existing `resolution` jsonb column to hold the `job_id`. Blocks concurrent Edit/Reject exactly like `accepted` does today, so the fix doesn't introduce a new race during the wait.
- New terminal `accept_failed` status — closed out via a reverse `job_id` lookup (`getConfirmationByCheckpointJobId()`) added to the `continue` route handler: `markAcceptedDelegated()` on a genuine terminal success, `markAcceptFailed()` on a genuine terminal failure, no-op if it checkpoints again.
- **Same bug shape found at 2 more sites during Architect Review (multi-site check), fixed identically, not left as separate future bugs:** `resolveAccept()`'s own fast/synchronous failure path (a `runCapability()` throw that never even reaches a checkpoint — `HAR-8`'s 3 attempts already happened inside that one call), and `resolvePendingConfirmation()`'s plain accept path (used by any confirmed intent with no `on_accept_intent_slug` — this path can never checkpoint at all, `sendRequest()` has no loop).
- **Necessary completion, not optional:** the eligibility guard (`status !== 'pending'`) widened at all 3 check sites (`resolveAccept()`, `resolvePendingConfirmation()`, the `edit` route branch) to `['pending','accept_failed'].includes(status)` — without this, `accept_failed` would have been just as dead-ended as today's bug, defeating the entire point of adding it.

Entirely inside the confirmation layer — confirmed unnecessary to touch `runCapability()`/`runLoop()`/`checkpointAndReturn()`/`resumeCapability()`'s own internals or the `durable_hops` schema; the reverse lookup on the existing `resolution` column is sufficient. `accept_failed`'s own visual/UI treatment deliberately deferred — real UI work needing a mock + John's sign-off, not blocking this backend fix.

**Coding session note, found live during setup:** a local `PreToolUse` hook (`block-design-session-code.js`, `SES-010`) correctly blocked code edits from the `session/design-loo-17-0721` branch — the coding session resolved it exactly as intended (a fresh `session/coding-loo-17-0721` worktree/branch, removed after push), the same resolution pattern `S-CHI-43` already established.

Node test 11/11 PASS, deleted before commit. `npm run build` clean.

**Live QA in two passes, gap found and closed within this same session, not left open.** Coding session's own Category L proved the fast/synchronous-failure site directly: a real `pending_confirmations` row with a deliberately-broken `proposed_action` landed cleanly on `accept_failed` with a real error captured; a second Accept call against that same row retried (500) instead of 409ing; Reject on a separate `accept_failed` row resolved cleanly (200). Honestly flagged as *not* proving the checkpoint-then-resume site (Task 4's `continue`-branch close-out) — unit-test-only, not live-forceable on demand through the normal UI flow.

## design-ai35-registry-0721 (docs-only, no version bump, 2026-07-21, worktree `design-ai35-registry-0721`)

Live design conversation with John, redefining `AI-35`/AI pattern tracking from first principles rather than patching the existing model. No code touched.

**Why this happened now:** while scoping `LOG-33` (found already-resolved by `AA-181`, closed same session, no code needed — see that row in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`), the conversation surfaced John's own framing of *why* pattern tracking exists: the platform's primary showcase that real AI reasoning, not deterministic code, drives every agent-loop hop, at a scale where cost/frequency/behavior are measurable per pattern. Testing the existing model (`ARCHITECTURE.md §19i`'s Four-Source Trust Model) against that purpose surfaced 5 governance questions it never answered: (1) how do we know we're missing a pattern a model now exhibits, (2) how do we know our names/definitions are industry-standard, (3) how do we know we're not inventing patterns even when detection is honest, (4) how do we handle an industry rename, (5) how do we handle a model doing something genuinely new.

**Grounded in real external research before answering, not reasoned in isolation:** WebSearch confirmed (a) LLM/agent observability is a real, well-funded industry category (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize, Datadog, W&B Weave); (b) OpenTelemetry's GenAI Semantic Conventions is a real, versioned, cross-vendor standard for the actual call/span schema, in active development since April 2024 — the real reference point for "is our schema standard," which this platform doesn't currently align to; (c) Anthropic's own "Building Effective Agents" paper is the real published source for 5 of this platform's pattern names (prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer); (d) 2026 academic literature (e.g. "VeryTrace") independently validates the self-report-then-verify idea already used for this platform's Case-Based-Reasoning design — not invented in isolation.

**The core diagnosis:** the existing model tangled three separate concerns into one flat catalog + one hardcoded write-time function — *what really happened* (a fact, changes only when model behavior changes), *how we prove it* (a detection method, changes as detection quality improves), and *what we call it* (a name from the literature, changes as industry terminology shifts). Tangling them is exactly why a rename or a newly-observed behavior felt expensive.

**Redefinition — three separated layers, replacing the tangled model:**
- **Layer A (Call Facts)** — generic, structural, checkable facts captured at write time regardless of pattern names: real tool-call records, real retrieved-chunk ids, call-chaining links, which internal gates fired, the model's self-reported structured claims. Nothing here knows what a "pattern" is.
- **Layer B (Classification Rules)** — pattern names as *derived labels* over Layer A facts, versioned, evaluated at read time (mirrors how `cost_usd` already works via `AA-181`) — so a rename or new pattern is a rule edit/addition, never a backfill or new per-call-site instrumentation. The prior 4-bucket evidence model survives here, reframed as "what kind of proof a rule may use," not a fixed list of 24 patterns each needing bespoke code.
- **Layer C (Pattern Vocabulary)** — citation-governed: every entry requires a real published source, a maturity status, a review date, and a `superseded_by` forward-pointer so renames never silently erase historical meaning.

**Schema decision made this session:** `PATTERN_CATALOG`'s governance fields move out of the static `shared/ai-patterns.js` file into a real Supabase table — this metadata is operational (needs editing without a code deploy), same reasoning already applied to `dev_version_counter`/`feature_id_counter` in this codebase. `ai_activity_log` stays the one central table, gaining new fields for Layer A. Whether individual Layer B rules are data-driven or code is left to whichever session builds Layer B.

**`ARCHITECTURE.md §19i` rewritten wholesale** (not patched) — the prior Four-Source Trust Model is preserved in a collapsed `<details>` block in the same section for history, explicitly marked superseded, not deleted.

**`AI-35` fully re-scoped in `docs/FEATURES.md`** with the ordered build sequence: (1) this doc rewrite, done; (2) Layer C vocabulary schema + a mandatory re-verification/reclassification audit of all 24 existing catalog entries against real sources (existing entries were never uniformly checked against this discipline — folds in `LOG-23`'s missing "Routing" pattern and `LOG-28`'s open Memory Consolidation question, the first concrete case the audit resolves); (3) Layer A generic fact capture; (4) Layer B read-time classifier (folds in `LOG-17`'s `llm-as-judge`/Case-Based-Reasoning/`streaming` detection, substantially answers `LOG-26`); (5) migration/cutover decision (historical rows keep frozen old-style classification, never retroactively rewritten — same precedent already established elsewhere); (6) rollup views (platform-wide/by-hop/by-agent), computed queries, same shape as today's `byService`/`byPattern`.

**Backlog reconciliation, same session:** `LOG-24` (persistent anti-hardcoding rule) marked 🔶 Partial — the rule is now written and LOCKED (`§19i` itself), but `SERVICE_LABEL`'s own cleanup is still open, small. `LOG-25`/`HAR-01` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` — both were open questions this redefinition directly answers, no further code needed for the questions themselves. `LOG-17`/`24`/`26`/`28` marked merged into `AI-35`, not independently actionable. `LOG-27` (cosmetic labeling gap) unaffected, stays open separately.

No kickoff doc — this is architecture/backlog restructuring, not a coding task. Steps 2-6 above each need their own design session (Architect Review, kickoff doc) before any code is touched, per the standing one-feature-per-session discipline.

**Design session closed that gap directly rather than accepting it as a permanent limitation:** constructed a real `durable_hops` row (`status:'in_progress'`, deliberately-malformed `format_contract` so the resume would genuinely fail) linked to a `pending_confirmations` row (`status:'accepting'`, `resolution:{job_id,...}`) via Supabase, then called `action:'continue'` against the real deployed API. The resume genuinely failed (`"reasoning-write handler: action required in structured output"`), and the linked confirmation correctly closed out to `accept_failed` with that real error captured in `resolution.error` — confirming Task 4's reverse-lookup-and-close-out logic works live, not just in the Node simulation. Reject on that same row then resolved cleanly (200), proving the widened guard holds for the checkpoint-derived case too, not just the fast-failure one. Both synthetic rows (`durable_hops` + `pending_confirmations`) cleaned up via Reject, zero residue left in Supabase.

**Close-out:** `LOO-17` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`. `AA-199`'s original two-part finding (`DAT-6` + `LOO-17`) is now fully closed on both halves.

## S-SES-011-design / S-SES-011 / S-SES-011a (v6.3.105 → v6.3.107, `a5d6bea` / `e78423a`, 2026-07-21, worktree `ses-11`)

Found 2026-07-21, same session as `SES-010` — two related frictions bundled under one backlog row: (1) the full 8-step worktree-isolation ceremony was run in full for several single-line, additive-only bookkeeping edits, and (2) `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s shared "In flight now"/bullet-list block caused real merge conflicts purely from bookkeeping, not from actual feature-work collisions (3 hit in one afternoon).

Decompose the shared "In flight now" block into one file per session (`.claude/inflight/<session-name>.md`) — structurally can't collide since no two sessions ever touch the same file — and define the lightweight bookkeeping path as "pure append (zero deletions) to a file only this session touches," which the per-file decomposition makes safe by construction. `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Last 3 sessions" section deliberately left alone (lower contention, edited only at individual close-out) — a scoped, flagged Tier-2 call, not asked.

**S-SES-011 (v6.3.105, `a5d6bea`):** 3 files, 4 tasks. `CLAUDE.md` gained the Lightweight Bookkeeping Path hard rule (skip `.env.local` copy + immediate worktree removal for qualifying pure-append edits, `git diff --stat` verified before push) and retargeted rules 6/6c/8 from shared bullets to per-session files. `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`'s two "In flight now" references retargeted to match. `scripts/check-session-docs.js` gained `freshDevDirEntries()` (directory counterpart to the existing `freshDevText()`) so `extractInFlightBullets()` reads `.claude/inflight/*.md` instead of parsing `CLAUDE-STATE.md` text; "Last 3 sessions" checks untouched. Node test 5/5 PASS, build clean.

**Design session's own close-out migration:** the ~7 real "In flight now" bullets existing at the time were moved verbatim into their own `.claude/inflight/<name>.md` files (11 total, including this session's own and one late addition), and `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s section collapsed to a two-line pointer. Hit one real merge conflict during this exact push — `design-chi-49-0721` updated its own bullet on `dev` between this session's read and push — resolved by taking the newer content into that session's migrated file, a live, first-hand demonstration of the exact friction `SES-011` exists to eliminate going forward.

**S-SES-011a (v6.3.107, `e78423a`) — real QA FAIL found during this design session's own self-verification, not hypothetical:** `freshDevDirEntries()`'s `git ls-tree --name-only origin/dev -- .claude/inflight` was missing `-r` (recursive) — a non-recursive `ls-tree` on a directory pathspec returns only that directory's own tree entry, not the files inside it, so the function silently returned zero entries regardless of how many real inflight files existed. Confirmed live (`git ls-tree` with vs. without `-r` against the real repo) before writing the patch. Root cause, not symptom: `SES-011`'s own Node test only exercised the pre-migration empty-directory case, never a populated one, so both states produced the same (wrong) zero-entries result and the bug shipped clean. 1 file, 1 task, Node test 2/2 PASS (including a live Category L check against the real, already-pushed inflight files), build clean.

**Verified directly, not accepted from the coding reports alone:** re-ran `node scripts/check-session-docs.js` against the real worktree after each push. Post-`SES-011a`, check 5 correctly stopped flagging all 11 migrated sessions and correctly kept flagging the 2 genuinely-untracked worktrees (`design-ai-35-0721`, `design-owen-news-provenance-0721`) — confirming the fix is precise, not overbroad. Checks 5c/5d, previously unable to fire at all (empty array), now correctly surface real pre-existing content-staleness findings in several migrated bullets (not this session's bug to fix, left for a future hygiene pass).

## S-DAT-7-design (v6.3.112, worktree `design-dat-7-0721`, 2026-07-21)

`DAT-7` was found live by `design-chi-50-0721` as an Accept-time HTTP 500 on Nadia — Data Analyst's Draft Forecast proposal (`"reasoning-write handler: writeContent failed -- denied-source-chunk-cross-room-or-missing"`), filed with the working hypothesis that it was a `§19f` `the_reasoning` write-path credential/room-boundary bug. This session root-caused it directly against live Supabase data and found that hypothesis wrong.

**Root cause 1 (the actual bug):** pulled the real failed `pending_confirmations` row (`id: 1f9ad39e-b7bb-40fd-83f5-8f850aa92a16`, `status: accept_failed`, `2026-07-21T20:53:16Z`) — its `proposed_action.chunk_id` is `"JPN-GROWTH-STRUCTURAL-HYP-001"`, a human-readable label Nadia invented, not a real `the_library` id. A second live "opinion" proposal from the same day (`2c10b0ef-...`, `chunk_id: "JPN-STRUCTURAL-CYCLE-001"`) shows the identical shape — 2/2 real organic samples. Traced why: `data-patch-intent`'s Supabase `skill_profiles` trait schema gives its `chunk_id` output field zero instruction (`{"type":["string","null"]}`, no `description`, and this intent has no `analysis_instructions` at all, unlike its sibling `data-patch-execute-intent`) — nothing tells the model to echo `task_context.disputed_chunk_id` verbatim, so it invents a descriptive slug instead. That bad value flows unchanged through `data-patch-execute-intent` (working as designed) into `reasoning-write.js` → `lib/search-harness.js`'s `writeTheReasoning()`, whose `AA-189` UUID-format guard correctly denies it. **The guard is not the bug; confirmed and left untouched.**

**Root cause 2 (why it surfaced as a crash, not a graceful message):** `reasoning-write.js`'s `handle()` bare-throws a statusless `Error` on any denial, which `execute.js`'s single outer catch maps to a raw HTTP 500. Checked the sibling `library-write.js` (Eleanor — Librarian's equivalent handler) — identical bare-throw shape, same bug pattern at 2 call sites dispatched through the same `format_contract.handler` registry (`request-receivable.js`). Per the multi-site-bug-pattern check, scoped as one fix covering both files rather than two independent patches. `request-receivable.js` already has the target idiom in the same file for its own "unknown handler" 501 case — `execute.js`'s outer catch already forwards `e.status`/`e.detail`, so no `execute.js` change is needed.

**Design walkthrough with John (one issue at a time, per `WORKING-WITH-JOHN.md`):** presented root cause 1 alone first, confirmed (including folding in a `temperature: 0` pin on `data-patch-intent`, matching `AA-154`'s existing precedent). Root cause 2 initially unclear to John on first pass — re-explained without HTTP-status-code framing, grounded in what "try again" actually does today (nothing, since the bad `chunk_id` is permanently baked into the stored proposal — only Edit/Reject work) — then merged what had been proposed as two separate tasks (server-side status/detail; client-side recovery copy) into one, since the first has no purpose without the second. Final scope, and the exact user-facing copy line, both explicitly confirmed before the kickoff doc was written.

**Kickoff written:** `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.112-DAT-7-nadia-chunk-id-echo-and-graceful-denial.md` — 2 tasks, 3 code files (`reasoning-write.js`, `library-write.js`, `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`) + 1 Supabase trait edit. Includes a Category L live test using a real `the_library` id (`0d09ac6e-baca-4471-a3f5-c0a63007882d`, `apple-cso-data-room`) confirmed live this session, for a loop-closure check uniquely traceable to the new write.

Coding session spawned next via the Automated Design→Code→Verify Loop; outcome to be appended here at close-out.

Close-out: `SES-011` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`.

## S-CHI-55-design/S-CHI-55 (v6.3.118, worktree `investigate-news-fetch-0721`, 2026-07-21)

Started as a live bug investigation: John reported dev's news fetch spinning ~1 min then showing nothing, his first test in 10 hours during which several concurrent sessions shipped (`SES-020`, `S-AI-35-2a`, `SES-019`, `DAT-7`, `CHI-49`–`53`). Live re-test reproduced the full Jordan→Alex news-fetch pipeline succeeding end to end; no commit in the intervening window touched `fetchNewsCards()`. Root cause not confirmed as a regression — most likely a slow-but-successful run (`ws-news-search-intent` latencies run 13s–43s against `execute.js`'s 60s Vercel `maxDuration`) combined with `fetchNewsCards()`'s deliberate silent fail-open (no visible error, by original `CHI-33` design). Logged as `CHI-54`, a UX gap (should a timeout ever surface visibly), not a blind fix.

**Pivoted into a UI cleanup walkthrough** once John confirmed the news issue resolved via refresh and brought 29 numbered items from a live screenshot review. Organized into themes rather than fixing 29 discrete items — many were the same root cause recurring: drawer content "accumulation" (4 mentions), Agent Routing "new question" divider consistency (4 mentions), chat bubble/status placement (8 mentions). Each theme confirmed with John before any scope was finalized (`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` Step 8b's stop-gate, applied per-theme given the volume). Claimed `CHI-55`–`CHI-60` from the atomic feature-ID counter, logged all 6 with full context to `docs/FEATURES.md`.

**`CHI-55` root-caused in 2 passes, live with John.** First hypothesis: `useDrawerStack`'s `manualOverride` (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` ~L1694-1717) only tracks a single `{key,open}` pair, so 2 manually-opened drawers can be simultaneously expanded — confirmed as intentional, not the bug (John's explicit call: keep multi-open, preserves the "papers on a desk" persistence intent `CHI-43`/`CHI-49` were built around). John re-tested live and found the real cause himself: comparing Column 2 (`EvidenceColumn`) against Column 3 (`AuditColumn`), Column 2's outer wrapper sets `background:T.cardAlt` + a border — identical to every individual `Drawer` inside it — while Column 3's equivalent wrapper sets no background at all, sitting directly on the app's real page background (`T.paperDeep`, confirmed at `AppShell.jsx:345`). Two open drawers in a same-colored parent box read as one merged block; Column 3's sections don't have this problem because there's real contrast between drawer and backdrop.

**Fix:** removed `background`/`border` from `EvidenceColumn`'s outer wrapper (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` ~L1855), and updated `ScrollFadeHint`'s `bg` prop (~L2090) from `T.cardAlt` to `T.paperDeep` to match. Visual-only, zero state/architecture change, 1 file. Explicitly scoped out `InteractColumn` (Column 1/chat) even though it shares the same wrapper pattern by an existing code comment — chat bubbles already have strong color/alignment-based distinction regardless of container background, so this specific problem (same-color content blending into same-color container) doesn't apply there.

**Kickoff written:** `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.118-CHI-55-evidence-column-background-removal.md` — 1 file, 2 tasks. Coding session spawned via the Automated Design→Code→Verify Loop: Node test 6/6 PASS, `npm run build` clean, committed (`03ba83e`) and pushed to `dev`.

**Self-verified QA live** (Manual QA Checklist, Section 11) — not just accepting the coding report: opened the dev preview, ran a real Q&A question end to end (9 hops), then opened both the News and Analysis & Narrative drawers simultaneously. Used direct computed-style inspection via the browser's JS console rather than a screenshot read (a screenshot-based visual check would have been weaker evidence here): confirmed the wrapper's `background-color` is `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (transparent), each `Drawer`'s own background is unchanged (`rgb(242,234,212)` = `T.cardAlt`), and the real background showing through is `rgb(221,213,190)` = `T.paperDeep` — exact match to Column 3. `ScrollFadeHint`'s gradient confirmed reading `T.paperDeep` too. Zero console errors. `git diff` confirmed `InteractColumn`/footer/`Drawer` component/`useDrawerStack` all byte-unaffected.

`CHI-55` archived ✅ Done in `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`. `CHI-54`, `CHI-56`–`CHI-60` remain open in `docs/FEATURES.md`, queued in `CLAUDE-STATE.md` for a future session — this worktree (`investigate-news-fetch-0721`) stays open in case they're picked up next.

## S-CHI-56-design/S-CHI-56 + patch (v6.3.120/v6.3.121, worktree `investigate-news-fetch-0721`, 2026-07-22)

Continuation of the same investigation session, picking up `CHI-56` next. What started as a one-paragraph "status placement" finding turned into several rounds of live architecture conversation with John before any kickoff was written — worth recording the actual back-and-forth, not just the final shape, since the early framing was materially wrong and only corrected through direct questioning.

**Round 1 — terminology alignment.** John described 4 "chat feedback items" (user prompt, Marcus prompt, live status, end status) and asked directly whether the code used different names — mapped cleanly onto `MessageBubble`(`role:"user"`/`user_action`), `MessageBubble`(`kind:"qa"`/`"non_qa"`), `AgentWorkingIndicator`, `HopSummaryLine` respectively.

**Round 2 — layout invariant, initially framed wrong.** An earlier, casual observation in this same conversation had suggested end status should move to sit under the *user's* bubble (right-aligned). John's careful requirements pass reversed this: Marcus is "the closer," so end status stays with Marcus, left-justified — the earlier note was superseded, not a contradiction to reconcile. Also new: end status should show the original time estimate alongside real elapsed, so John can judge whether the system's own estimates are accurate.

**Round 3 — root-caused the Agent Routing "some hops have a time, some don't" complaint before touching any code.** Found `NON_MEASURABLE_EVENT_TYPES` (`MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx`) declared 6 event types permanently duration-less by design, not by bug. Traced each: `agent_selection`/`failure_triage` are sub-fields embedded inside a single already-timed response (confirmed by reading the exact construction sites, `~L1252`/`~L1397`); `delegation`-family arrive as live SSE ticks with a real, uncaptured client-side arrival moment; `question_boundary` is a pure marker. Presented this and asked which way John wanted it resolved (keep the exception list vs. measure everything) — **John: measure everything, "a hop is an instance that has work and time, no matter how brief."**

**Round 4 — "turn" vs. "transaction."** Proposed extending the existing `question_boundary` divider to fire on every user action. John corrected this: a single investigation (question → deeper theories → pick a theory → commit as forecast → accept) is *one* transaction with several turns inside it, not several transactions — firing a divider on every turn would fragment one real investigation into false "new questions." Re-checked the code: the one existing `question_boundary` call site already only fires on a genuinely new typed/example question, so it was already behaving correctly as a transaction-start marker without anyone having framed it that way — no change needed there, only a symmetric "transaction complete" closing marker needed adding.

**Architect Review — no prior shared implementation existed** (grepped for any "turn"/"duration"/"elapsed" abstraction; every flow hand-rolled its own `Date.now()`/`buildHopEvent` pattern independently — confirmed, not assumed). Decided against lifting the deeply-entangled `workingStatus`/`messages`/`pipelineEvents` state into a new stateful hook in this first session — too large a rewrite for the scope at hand — and instead built `src/lib/turnTracking.js` as a pure-function module (duration resolution + transaction-boundary event builders) that the screen's existing state calls through. Session 2 migrates the remaining flows onto the same module; if a genuine stateful hook turns out to be warranted once more flows are migrated, that's Session 2's call.

**Kickoff written and shipped:** `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.120-CHI-56-turn-tracking-service.md` — 2 files, 4 tasks. Node test 18/18 PASS, `npm run build` clean, committed/pushed (`f89f503`).

**Found a real bug during this session's own mandatory live Category L verification, not hypothetical.** Asked a real question (succeeded, 7 hops, every hop showed a time — confirmed the core fix worked immediately, including previously-blank `agent_selection`/`delegation_complete` hops). Asked a second, different real question immediately after — it hit an unrelated, pre-existing backend flake (`request-receivable.js`'s "Parse failed and retry also failed," confirmed by grep to predate this session by many prior retry-hardening sessions) — but also threw 4 real `CHI-07` console errors on `delegation_complete`. Root-caused before patching: `lastEventAtRef` (this session's own new ref) was never seeded at turn start, so a turn's first delegation-family event could legitimately have no prior tick to diff against; `resolveDelegationDuration`'s own correct `null` return for that case then tripped `buildHopEvent`'s **pre-existing** guard (predates `CHI-56`, never previously applicable to these 5 types since they used to be declared non-measurable). **Wrote and shipped a proper patch kickoff rather than editing code directly in this design session** — briefly drafted the fix inline to confirm it, then reverted it and went through the same design→kickoff→coding-agent loop as everything else in this session, keeping the established discipline consistent even for a same-session bug found by the design session itself. `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.121-CHI-56-patch-turn-start-seed.md` — 1 file, 1 line + comment. Node test 4/4 PASS, `npm run build` clean, committed/pushed (`c6ccdf7`).

**Re-verified live after the patch, thoroughly — 4 consecutive real questions in one continuous session, 31 total hops** spanning a plain success, a legitimate Owen guardrail block that escalated through Sam and Eleanor, and 2 more successes. Every single hop showed a real, non-zero duration. On the console-error question specifically: initial re-checks kept showing the same 4 old errors, which was concerning until direct instrumentation (overriding `console.error` to tally only occurrences from that point forward, rather than trusting the browser tool's own buffered/replayed console history) proved a full subsequent turn — including its own delegation-family events within a legitimate guardrail-block-and-escalate chain — produced zero new errors. The earlier repeated sightings were stale history, not a live recurrence; worth noting as a real gotcha in this testing setup for future sessions doing repeated console checks in the same tab.
