## S-SES-32 (v6.3.206, 2026-07-28 night, worktree `design-log-60`, docs-only) — secondary backlog IDs need a closure gate

**How it started.** John opened a design session on `LOG-60` (Observability). Orientation found `LOG-60` had no design work left in it: a 2026-07-28 sweep had marked its original dropped-rows mechanism stale (it predates the Layer B rearchitecture), and the `design-log-81` conversation had already settled the live question — every AI Audit count is real model calls only. `LOG-60`'s row ends with "Close this row when `LOG-81`'s QA passes."

**The coordination call (John's, option 3 of 3 offered).** `LOG-81`'s coding commit `5c69eb0` was already on `origin/dev` and its session was live (last activity minutes earlier, `CLAUDE-STATE.md` still at v6.3.200, close-out not yet run). Rather than verify and close `LOG-60` in parallel — which would have run this session's edits into `docs/FEATURES.md` underneath an active close-out — the row was handed to the `Design log-81` session via `send_message`, tied to its own **QA checklist item 4** ("classified distinct + not yet classified = header Total Calls exactly"), which is `LOG-60`'s reconciliation question restated. Pass → close and archive `LOG-60`; fail → leave open with the measured delta. This session wrote nothing to `docs/FEATURES.md`'s `LOG-60` row.

**The process gap this exposed (the actual deliverable).** `LOG-81`'s kickoff named `LOG-60` exactly once — in its Section 1 Feature line, "also settles `LOG-60` (Observability)'s denominator question" — and nowhere in Sections 9–12. No gate, no close-out step. `LOG-60`'s row pointed at `LOG-81`; `LOG-81`'s kickoff pointed at `LOG-60`; neither pointed at an action. Nothing in `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` required the kickoff to discharge an ID it adopted, and Step 5c's All-PASS branch archives only "the feature ID's row," singular. The miss was caught by luck — John opened a session on the orphaned row itself.

**Rule shipped** (`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`, 2 insertions):
- **Step 4 Architect Review, new bullet "Secondary backlog IDs need a closure gate"** — naming another ID as settled/folded-in/superseded obliges the kickoff to (a) name the QA item that gates it and (b) list it in the close-out step. If no gate can be named that would prove it resolved, don't claim it settled; leave it open and say what it waits on.
- **Step 5c All-PASS branch** — discharge every secondary ID the kickoff named, each against its stated gate; passed → close and archive in the same commit, failed → stays open with the measured reason on its row. Never inherit the primary's ✅ by adjacency, never silently stay open; state which happened.

**Back-check (partial, and logged as partial).** Swept `docs/kickoffs/` for adoption language. `AA-83` and `AA-135` were verified correctly archived. **One live pre-existing instance found: `MI-41` (UI)**, still `❌ Missing`, while kickoff `v6.2.18-MI-51` states `MI-42` (archived ✅) "supersedes/folds in the standalone `MI-41` idea." The descriptions don't match — the kickoff describes a chat-timer/Agent-Routing-drawer idea, `MI-41`'s row is Column 3's `flex`/`minHeight`/`overflowY` chain — so it's either a mis-cited ID or two items sharing one number (`SES-30`'s collision family). ~15 other matching kickoffs were **not** individually confirmed. Tracked on `SES-32`'s row as 🔶 Partial rather than claimed as a completed sweep.

**Relationship to `SES-27`.** Same close-out-leak family, different mechanism: `SES-27` is one row's own scope outrunning its checkmark; `SES-32` is a second row that no session's close-out owns. Both left open work wearing a resolved label.

**Not done here, deliberately:** `LOG-60` itself was not closed (belongs to `design-log-81`), and `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s "Version in dev" line was not touched — v6.3.203 (`LOG-81`) is the real pending app version and rewriting that header mid-close-out would have clobbered a live session's work. This session is docs-only; no code, no app behavior change.

## S-LOG-71-design / S-LOG-71 (v6.3.205, `eab4b46`, 2026-07-28 night, worktree `design-log-71`, 1 code file + 1 migration) — a resumed hop now logs the same frozen signature its first hop did

**The defect, in one sentence.** `LOG-67` froze the §19k config-half onto every agent-turn row at write time, but only `runCapability()` ever supplied it — so any hop that resumed after a checkpoint logged a fact-half-only row that no config-half criterion could ever match.

**Root cause, read fresh.** `resumeCapability()` re-enters `runLoop()` at **three** sites (`execute.js` 1289 / 1326 / 1343). The `LOG-71` row and `BETA-TRIAGE.md` §3 bucket 5 both said "both resume re-entries" — that was wrong, and fixing only two would have left the post-dispatch continuation broken. `durable_hops` had no `signature_config` column (verified against `information_schema`, 29 columns), so `resumeCapability()` — which rebuilds its entire world from that one row — had nothing to pass.

**Quantified before deciding anything.** Of 1,979 `agent-turn` rows written on/after 2026-07-26 (fully post-`LOG-67`-deploy), **221 (11.2%) carried a fact-half with no config-half, and 214 of those (97%) had a `span_id` matching a `durable_hops` row.** The control is what makes it causal rather than correlated: among the *healthy* config-bearing rows, only **17%** span-match a durable row. Seven rows were left unexplained and stated as such.

**John's decision — persist, don't recompute.** Three options were weighed and two rejected on stated grounds:
- **Recompute on resume** via `buildSignatureConfig()` — rejected: it re-reads *today's* skill profiles, so a resumed hop's signature would reflect resume-time config. That is precisely the drift `LOG-67` shipped to eliminate.
- **Read the config-half back from the sibling `ai_activity_log` row** — genuinely tempting (115 of 125 affected spans have one), and it was John's own instinct: *"Its persisted in the database already isn't it?"* Half-true, and the half that isn't decides it. `logAgentTurn()` at `execute.js:855` is **fire-and-forget (no `await`)**, which is exactly why 8% of affected spans have no sibling at all; and it would make the audit log a runtime read-dependency of the executor, inverting the layering.
- **Persist on `durable_hops`** ← chosen. The fifth instance of one pattern: `task_context` (`AA-145`), `delegation_required` (`AA-148`), `requires_human_confirmation` (`LOO-20`), `enable_web_search` (`HAR-17`) each closed this same gap the same way.

**What shipped.** Migration `log71_durable_hops_signature_config` (`jsonb`, nullable, no backfill). `checkpointAndReturn()` gained a `signatureConfig` param written into its **always-run patch** — `LOG-49`'s `span_id` precedent, which is why `durable-loop.js` needed **zero** changes (`loadDurableHopRow()` already selects `*`). The write is **conditional** (`...(signatureConfig ? {…} : {})`) so a snapshot-less checkpoint can never erase one the row already carries. All six `checkpointAndReturn()` call sites pass it; all three resume re-entries recover `row.signature_config ?? null`. No `buildSignatureConfig()` call anywhere on the resume path.

**Category L, run live against real Supabase + real Anthropic** (in-process via `__setTestBudgetMs(0)` to force the checkpoint branch deterministically, then cleared for the resume — the override is a module export, not reachable over HTTP): forced checkpoint on `quality-gate`/`qg-content-context-intent`/owen → `durable_hops.signature_config` persisted with all four config keys and an ordered `assembled_skill_slugs` → resumed row `#24861` carries the config-half **byte-identical to the frozen original** → value still present after completion → fresh non-checkpointing call `#24863` unregressed (0 durable rows for its span). Node suite 21/21; `npm run build` clean (re-run independently — the worktree's `node_modules` was absent at QA time and had to be installed).

**Two QA items that did not pass as written, both stated rather than quietly dropped:**
1. **Item 7 was a bad assertion, not a bug.** "`ai_call_patterns` names the resumed row" returns **0** — but so does every *fresh* row of the same capability+intent (six checked). The resumed row is now exactly as classifiable as a fresh one, which is all `LOG-71` can deliver; the 0 belongs to `LOG-72`'s criteria gap (27 vocabulary entries, 9 with criteria). The checklist item should have been written as a parity test against a fresh control from the start.
2. **Item 1 (deployed build) could not be satisfied.** The newest git-triggered Vercel `dev` deployment is `b309da8` (21:55 CST); `origin/dev` had advanced 9 commits past it with no build. Filed as **`SES-33`**. The verification above therefore ran against the *exact committed bytes* (worktree HEAD `eab4b46`, diff-verified identical to `dev`) but not against a deployed function — documented as such, not accepted as equivalent.

**Two coding-session test corrections, both verified legitimate before acceptance.** The kickoff's own Section 8 shipped two bad assertions: `checkpointAndReturn` call-site count `=== 6` also matched the function *declaration* (the untouched `origin/dev` baseline already read 7), and "resume never recomputes" grepped raw source for `buildSignatureConfig` when all four occurrences are comments — three of them the kickoff's own mandated Task 3 comment text, making the doc's test and its own spec mutually exclusive. Both corrected in the test, neither masked a code defect.

**Spun off:**
- **`LOG-111`** (Architecture) — the historical backfill. `LOG-69`-done backfilled 13,841 rows whose `call_facts` **IS NULL**; rows carrying a fact-half but no config-half fell outside that `WHERE` clause entirely — **2,738 all-time**, never touched. 657 recover from a same-`span_id` sibling holding the genuine frozen original, a *stronger* source than `LOG-69`'s recompute-from-current-config route. Sanctioned by §19i's intent-provability extension (ARCHITECTURE.md:1418) — the no-backfill rule governs the contingent fact-half only, never the config-half. Sequenced **after** `LOG-71` or it just refills.
- **`SES-33`** (Tooling) — the Vercel `dev` build outage above. Not new: `8fbfdd4`'s commit message shows another session already hit it and worked around it with a manual poke, which produced a deployment carrying **no git metadata at all**. Needs the integration re-checked, not another poke.
- **`LOG-103`** closed as merged into `LOG-71`, John's approval, confirmed a duplicate two independent ways.

**Process note.** The rebase before the kickoff push hit a real conflict in `docs/FEATURES.md` — a concurrent session had rewritten the adjacent `LOG-72` row (8,999 → 8,656 chars) after this worktree branched. Resolved per `CLAUDE.md`'s adjacency-collision rule: kept this session's `LOG-71` edit and the other session's `LOG-72` verbatim, then diffed the result byte-for-byte against `origin/dev` to confirm nothing of theirs was lost.

## S-LOG-81-design / S-LOG-81 (v6.3.203, 2026-07-28 night, worktree `design-log-81`) — every AI Audit count means real model calls only; `LOG-60` closed on the same gate

**The question John settled.** The AI Audit header said "Total Calls: 24,819," and a CTO reading that as "the AI made 24,819 model calls" would be wrong twice: **4,247 rows are deterministic operations** (Eleanor Voss — The Librarian's library reads 2,409, agent-directory lookups 1,745, library writes 85 — logged by design per §12, but no model, no tokens, no cost), and **~5,175 rows are duplicate halves** of the still-active `LOG-91` double-write. Real unique model calls: ~15,400. John chose **Option A — "Total Calls" counts real model calls only** — then confirmed the same criterion for **By Agent** and for **By Pattern's denominator**, one decision at a time. He explicitly kept the **2,571 model rows with empty `call_facts`** inside "not yet classified": that population is his signature-backfill to-do list (`LOG-42`'s thread), not noise to hide.

**Definition shipped.** A countable call = the row **names a model** AND **is not the duplicate `agent-turn` half** of an `AI-51` pair. One exported predicate, `isCountableCall(e) => !!e.model && !e.isPairedDup`, defined once in `useAIActivity.js` and reused by Total Calls, By Agent, By LLM, and both By Pattern numbers. `hydrateFromSupabase()` stamps `isPairedDup` from the already-computed `pairedAgentTurnIds()` set, so the predicate stays a pure per-entry test. By Pattern's counts moved client-side via the rollup view's `log_ids` — the exact mechanism `LOG-97` already proved for cost — with per-source fallback to the view's own numbers when the log isn't hydrated. **Zero migrations; the Supabase views were not touched.**

**Two asymmetries John approved, both deliberate.** (1) **By Service keeps operations semantics** — §12 (LOCKED) tracks deterministic services as productized usage, so zeroing the Librarian's service row would be wrong; at QA, Library Custodian shows 3,698 and Roster Broker 1,745, fully intact. (2) **Total Cost is not gated** — `AI-51` already zeroes the duplicate half's cost at hydrate and deterministic rows cost nothing, so gating would be a no-op; measured $156.75 before and after.

**Live QA — 12/12 PASS, every number reconciled to SQL at QA time, not asserted.** Header **15,405 === SQL countable 15,405** (of 24,830 raw rows — an exact match, better than the ~1% tolerance the kickoff allowed for concurrent writes). By Pattern **2,110 classified distinct + 13,295 unclassified = 15,405 exactly**; the distinct-vs-sum distinction matters — per-pattern totals sum to 2,622 because multi-pattern rows are unioned, never added. By Agent sums to 15,373 across 19 agents, and the 26-row gap to the header is **exactly** the null-`agent_id` count SQL reports (measured, per the kickoff's own "don't assume" instruction). Michelle Manning — Project Manager 7,613 → **4,506** (SQL-exact); Eleanor Voss — The Librarian 4,853 → **2,356** (SQL 2,357, one live write apart). Hydration fallback verified by sampling every 200 ms through a cold panel open: the reclassification figure shows the view's own **20,734** pre-hydrate, flips to the derived **13,295** at ~1 s, never NaN, never a false zero. Mobile 375×812 renders with no horizontal overflow; console clean.

**Two of this design session's own estimates were wrong, and the shipped code was right.** Eleanor Voss — The Librarian was predicted to drop to ~1.1k and is **2,357** — the estimate had used only the `librarian` *feature*'s model rows rather than her whole `agent_id` row set (she also does data-room-custody work); SQL confirms 4,854 − 2,497 no-model = 2,357, exactly what shipped. Unclassified was predicted at ~12.8k and is **13,295**. Both were recorded as predictions in the kickoff's QA checklist, so the discrepancy surfaced immediately at verification rather than silently becoming the new "expected."

**`LOG-60` closed here, not separately.** The `design-log-60` session handed it over live (John's call), gated on this session's QA item 4 — and item 4 is precisely `LOG-60`'s question restated: it was opened because By Pattern didn't reconcile to the raw log. The answer turned out to be a decision, not a hunt for dropped rows — the header and By Pattern were counting two different populations; now they count the same one, so they reconcile by construction. Discharged per `SES-32`'s new secondary-ID rule, which that session wrote after noticing this very kickoff had adopted `LOG-60` with no closure gate.

**Infrastructure finding — folded into `SES-33`, 🔴 live, affects other sessions right now.** (This session independently hit the symptom and had claimed `SES-35` for it before finding that `design-log-71` had already filed `SES-33` minutes earlier; `SES-35` is retired unused rather than renamed, and this session's narrowing evidence was added to `SES-33` instead of filing a duplicate.) Vercel's git integration has stopped producing deployments for `dev` pushes. The dev preview URL still serves `index-CQJJJvbU.js`, which carries `CHI-88`'s v6.3.200 markers but not `LOG-81`'s code — stale for at least `HAR-20` (v6.3.201) and `LOG-81` (v6.3.203). An empty poke commit (`8fbfdd4`) produced no build at all, ruling out a slow queue; a `vercel deploy` from the same worktree at the dev tip built cleanly in 35 s and produced `index-B723nKf9.js` **containing** the new code, ruling out a build failure. **This session's QA therefore ran against that CLI preview, and says so.** Any session QA'ing against the dev URL right now is testing v6.3.200 — the second occurrence today of the "grep the served bundle before believing a live-QA result" rule.

**Concurrency note (no data lost).** A concurrent session's commit (`fd8c79e`, `S-LOG-91-design`) rewrote the `LOG-81` and `LOG-60` rows in `docs/FEATURES.md` from a stale copy, dropping this session's decision notes on both; `CHI-90`, `LOG-110`, and — usefully — this session's own measurement inside the `LOG-91` row all survived. Caught at close-out by grepping for the text rather than assuming the rebase preserved it. Both affected rows were being archived in this same commit anyway, so the authoritative record is the `FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md` entry.

**Close-out correction (same session, after John asked whether everything was finished).** Two items were reported complete when they were not, and both are now done: **QA item 12** — the note that `LOG-92`-done/`LOG-93`-done's "Total Calls === count(*)" reconciliation target is superseded — had never been written, and is now on the `LOG-81` archive row; and **`docs/BETA.md`** still carried `LOG-81` as confirmed queue item #2 and `LOG-60` as an open re-scoped question, with the bucket-3 "counting conversation" listed as an unresolved denominator decision. All three BETA.md entries now reflect the shipped state, including the measured floor drop (20,729 → 13,295 needing reclassification). The QA result stands at 12/12 only with item 12 counted as of this correction — as originally reported it was 11/12.

**Also filed.** `CHI-90` (Observability) — the CHI screen's per-agent drawer still counts every row via the shared `LOG-21` core, so it now disagrees with AI Audit; needs John's call on whether it adopts the same predicate or keeps operations semantics. `LOG-110` (Observability, `FEATURES-LATER.md`) — if John ever wants an "operations by agent" surface for the deterministic workload this change removes from the call counts.

## design-ses-18 — SES-18 root cause + bypass closure (2026-07-28 night, docs-only, no version bump)

John's call: fix the *cause*, not add a detector ("b"). `SES-18`'s reseed half had shipped the night before (`beta-doc-0728f`); this session took the open half.

**State on arrival.** Audited all 15 `feature_id_counter` prefixes against the real doc maxima across all four FEATURES files — **every prefix in sync**, so nothing was on fire and the work was purely preventive.

**Root cause (three legs, one story: the correct path was harder than the wrong one, and nothing at filing time said which was which).**
1. **The rule wasn't where the work happens.** The claim step was documented only in `.claude/skills/session-setup/SKILL.md` — a "make your worktree, copy your .env" document read once at session start. Rows get filed mid-session and at close-out, hours later. `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` — which owns the Backlog Capture rule and close-out steps 8c/9/10, and is the doc actually in front of a session when it types an ID — **never mentioned `feature_id_counter` at all** (grep-confirmed across every doc). What it *did* say was "before assigning a new item's ID, check `SCREEN-INVENTORY.md` for the correct prefix": the letters were governed, the number was not.
2. **One claim gave one ID, but multi-row filing is the normal case.** Scanned all 340 IDs ever introduced across the four FEATURES files by their introducing commit: **51 commits filed 2+ IDs of the same prefix at once** (`S-CHI-34-design` filed eight; 7 such commits in the two days before this session). Each was either N deliberate round-trips or one claim plus a hand-count.
3. **The column name asserted the opposite of its contents.** `next_number` held the *last issued* number (`CHI` = 89 with `CHI-89` live). A session reading the table instead of claiming would read "89 is next" and file on top of an existing row.

**Evidence the legs are real, not theoretical.** The 2026-07-21 block (`CHI-46`…`CHI-51`) traces to four commits between 10:34 and 13:38 CST — all *after* `SES-006` landed the counter at 10:01 that morning, i.e. sessions already in flight that had read a `CLAUDE.md` without the rule. `845b19f` alone introduced `CHI-49/50/51` in one commit; `9ffc1ed` introduced `ABT-1`+`ABT-2` in one commit. The two `CHI-48` rows (`0d5c877` 12:13, `46fd698` 13:18) are an hour apart from different sessions, both hand-picking 48. `CHI-76` is the sharpest: `b9945be` minted it at 12:41 on 2026-07-27 without claiming, and `9e38d1e` at 12:58 **claimed correctly** and got 76 anyway.

**Fix shipped (three changes, all docs + one Supabase DDL — no `src/`/`api/` files).**
- **Block claim.** `session-setup` step 3b's SQL now takes an `<N>`: `VALUES ('<PREFIX>', <N>, …) … SET last_issued_number = last_issued_number + <N> RETURNING last_issued_number`, block = `returned − N + 1` … `returned`. Filing eight rows is one call. **Verified live both paths** — new prefix with N=5 returned 5 (block 1–5), existing prefix with N=3 returned 8 (block 6–8), throwaway `ZZTEST` row deleted after.
- **Rule moved to the point of use.** `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`: a new paragraph directly under the prefix rule ("the rule above governs the letters; the number is claimed atomically…"), and a paragraph in close-out step 8c, which is the repo's single biggest producer of multi-row filings — you finish that sweep holding N missing items and need N IDs at once. `CLAUDE.md`'s atomic-counters hard rule gained the never-hand-count clause.
- **Column renamed** `next_number` → `last_issued_number`. Safe: grep-confirmed **no code reads it** (nothing in `src/`, `api/`, `scripts/`, `lib/`, `tests/`, `package.json`); only `session-setup/SKILL.md` (updated) plus historical records left as-is. A stale in-flight session's old SQL now fails loudly with "column does not exist" — the intended failure mode, versus silently minting a duplicate.

**Deliberately not done.** Drift *detection* — John scoped this session to the cause. Filed as **`SES-38`** (Tooling, post-beta), which also absorbs a side finding: `scripts/check-new-id-prefixes.js` already diffs newly-added rows and checks their prefix, but is **wired to nothing** — absent from `package.json` and from every hook in `C:/Projects/.claude/settings.json`. Its open design question is that the check needs a Supabase read from a Node script, which `check-session-docs.js` deliberately avoids (pure `fs` + `git`, always exits 0).

**Cross-references swept.** `SES-30`'s "dent `SES-18` by reseeding the `CHI` counter" is now moot (`CHI` verified in sync) — row narrowed to the rename-one-row work only. `docs/BETA.md` §2b item 3 updated from "reseed half done" to done-both-halves, pointing at `SES-38` for the remainder.

**Close-out.** `SES-18` → ✅ Done, archived. Docs touched: `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`, `.claude/skills/session-setup/SKILL.md`, `docs/FEATURES.md`, `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`, `docs/BETA.md`, `docs/SESSIONS.md`, `CLAUDE-STATE.md`. One Supabase DDL (column rename) + one real `SES` claim (`SES-38`). No version bump, no kickoff doc, no coding session — the deliverable was process, not code.

## S-LOG-91-design / S-LOG-91 (v6.3.204) — one `ai_activity_log` row per model call
**2026-07-28, worktree `log-91-design`. `LOG-91` ✅ Done, live-QA PASS 8/8. Commit `ec9d29c`.**

**Problem.** Every terminal agent turn logged one model call as two rows: `runLoop()` wrote the `agent-turn` row, then handed the same already-made call to `sendRequest()` as `precomputed_turn`, whose STEP 4 wrote a second `request-receivable` row with byte-identical `usage`. Measured at design time: 1,154 span-provable pairs, 100% identical tokens, 1,004 in the prior 24 h — active, not historical.

**John's three decisions** (one at a time, each confirmed): fix at the write path, not display; the **agent-turn row survives** (it is the only shape carrying the `capability:intent:depthN` composite the Displayer parses `intent` from — keeping the wrapper instead would have made every terminal call *less* classifiable); historical provable pairs get **merge-then-remove**, not deletion. The merge framing was John's correction to Claude's own proposal — plain deletion would have dropped the wrapper's task link, retrieval facts, and guardrails outcome on ~3.5k calls.

**The session's one real defect, caught in QA review before it shipped.** The kickoff specced `call_facts.dispatch_latency_ms` to preserve the wrapper's second duration. That is wrong, and measurably so: `call_facts` is the base of the §19k signature, and the Displayer's speed depends on `SELECT DISTINCT signature` collapsing the table before `pattern_criteria_matches()` runs. Measured live: **24,826 rows → 720 distinct signatures; with a per-call millisecond value, 24,826** — a 34× blow-up on a query with a 3 s `anon` timeout that `LOG-99` had just brought to ~289 ms. Fix: a real `dispatch_latency_ms` integer column (migration `log_91_dispatch_latency_ms`), threaded through a new optional `logActivity()` param. John approved **4 files** — one over the cap — rather than drop the measurement or split the display task. *Generalizable rule: never put a per-call numeric into `call_facts`; the signature is a grouping key, not a record.* The same trap was avoided a second time in the data pass — the provenance marker deliberately records `{basis, provenance}` only, no source row id.

**Shape of the fix.** `sendRequest()` writes its own row only when `precomputed_turn` is null (`api/plan.js`, `confirmation.js` byte-identical); on the loop path it returns `_terminal_log` instead. `runLoop()` holds the turn payload and writes it **exactly once** across all four terminal branches — the `AA-142` retry, the `AA-142` throw, the `requiresHumanConfirmation` gate, and the `sendRequest()` path (try/catch: plain on throw, merged on success, `_terminal_log` stripped before the result reaches a client). Delegating turns are untouched. `AI-51`'s timestamp heuristic is scoped to the pre-trace window so it can never mis-pair a fresh single-record wrapper.

**Process notes.** The first coding agent died mid-task on a credit exhaustion; its on-disk work was reviewed, kept, and finished by a second agent on Opus 5 — the review is what caught the `call_facts` defect, which the kickoff's own Section 8 test would *not* have caught (that test recreated the merge rules in pure JS rather than exercising `logAgentTurn()`; the second agent added a real-write-path test that does). A `SES-28`-class trap also held: only `run-all.js` proves a regression file.

**Data pass (MCP, §19i per-anomaly authorization).** Ambiguity audited first: **zero** ambiguous matches across 3,560 mergeable wrappers (span-match first, then trace + identical tokens + <60 s). Merged, verified, then deleted; plus the 2 residue rows the interrupted first attempt wrote with latency inside `call_facts`. Result: **zero provable pairs remain**, 24,990 → 21,450 rows, distinct signatures 834 → **678**, rollup 726 ms → **413 ms** (the pass made the view *faster*). The ~2,121 pre-trace unprovable pairs stay frozen behind the legacy-scoped heuristic, by John's decision — merging on a timestamp guess could glue facts onto the wrong call.

**Verification.** Deployment confirmed by grepping the served dev bundle for `LOG-91`'s cutoff constant, never by deploy status; the `api/` half confirmed independently by the cutover in the data itself (last pair 03:42:51Z, first merged write 03:43:31Z — the two "new pairs after deploy" were old lambdas serving during the alias switch, both with `dispatch_latency_ms` null). Screen totals reconciled to SQL within 10 rows of live traffic. Post-pass on-screen totals are **computed, not observed** — the Browser pane's click handling degraded mid-session (no console or network errors; the panel had rendered correctly earlier in the same session).

**Residue.** `SES-33`'s "dev is undeployed" premise re-measured and currently false — noted on that row and in `CLAUDE-STATE.md`, root cause still unproven, sequenced with `SES-015`. `LOG-81` (counting) and `LOG-60` (reconciliation) remain their own conversations; this session removed the duplicate class from both but decided nothing about deterministic ops.

## S-SES-015-design / S-SES-015 (v6.3.209, `ba3232a`, 2026-07-28, worktree `design-ses-015`, 3 files)

**`SES-015` (Tooling) — the deploy-current gate. "Pushed" is not "deployed." Self-verified QA 10/10 PASS.** Beta pre-regression prep, `docs/BETA.md` §2b item 2.

**Why it matters, stated once:** a live-QA run against a stale preview is not a weaker result — it is a result about a *different build*, and it is indistinguishable from a real one **in either direction**. `LOG-105` already produced one false "the fix didn't work." The same mechanism can just as easily produce a false green, and bucket 1 (the 24-case CHI regression) is the beta ship gate.

**Measured rather than asserted.** All 156 commits on `origin/dev` since 2026-07-28 12:00 CST, compared against every `dev` deployment Vercel actually produced (`meta.githubCommitRef === "dev"`), scoring each commit by the lag to the first build *containing* it:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Median lag | 37 s |
| p90 | 852 s (14 min) |
| Max | 2,973 s (49.5 min) |
| Waited > 5 min | 44 / 156 (28%) |
| Waited > 10 min | 31 / 156 (20%) |

The first naive cut of this number was **59/156 "never built,"** which is wrong and worth recording as a trap: a build of a *later* commit still contains yours, so per-commit build coverage is the wrong unit. The right question is whether any built commit is a *descendant*. Nearly shipped a scarier and less true number.

**This reconciles the `SES-33` dispute rather than adding a third opinion.** `SES-33` recorded "no build since `b309da8`"; `S-LOG-91-design` re-measured and called that premise false. **Both were right** — a median of 37 s with a 46-minute tail produces exactly that pattern of contradictory spot-checks. Re-measuring by hand keeps producing whichever answer the moment happens to hold, which is the argument for an on-demand instrument rather than per-session re-litigation.

**Root cause, found concurrently by `ses29-fix-kickoffs` and folded in here rather than left as this session's "unproven":** Vercel's **free-tier cap of 100 deployments/day is exhausted** (`vercel deploy` → `Resource is limited - try again in 24 hours (api-deployments-free-per-day)`). That is a better explanation than the "intermittent" reading this session reached on its own, and the two corroborate: a spent quota is not random — builds fire until the cap and then stop until the window rolls, which is precisely a fast median with a long evening tail, and it explains why a poke commit sometimes works and sometimes cures nothing. **Consequence for reading the numbers above: the 20%-over-10-min figure is "the share of the day's commits pushed after the quota ran out," not a fixed failure rate** — it moves with how many deploys the day's concurrent sessions have already spent. The gate detects the condition; it does not buy deploys back, so `SES-33` stays open.

**Two findings reshaped the scope before any code was spec'd.**

1. **The guidance already existed, in a file nobody reads.** Commit `eece74f` had already documented the bundle-grep, the Vercel API check, and the 402 limitation — into `docs/SESSIONS.md`, which is 1.67 MB and which `CLAUDE-STATE.md` explicitly instructs every session never to read by default. So the item was never "write this down"; it was **relocate it to a read-by-default home and make it a gate rather than a note.**
2. **`BETA.md` §2b's prescribed fix could not cover the run it was listed to protect.** It specified "fetch the served bundle, grep for a string unique to the build." The regression driver posts to `/api/capabilities/execute` — a serverless function with no static asset to grep. The item that existed to protect bucket 1 would have left bucket 1 exposed. **Superseded by this session**; `BETA.md` itself deliberately not edited (it belongs to the beta-doc sessions).

**The mechanism, and the one line it turns on.** `scripts/check-deploy-current.js` asks Vercel which commit `dev` is actually serving (newest `READY` **and** `aliasAssigned` — a READY deployment that never took the alias is not what the URL serves) and passes only if the tested SHA is an **ancestor** of it. Not equality. With 5–7 concurrent sessions the deployed tip is normally *ahead* of yours; an equality check would fail almost always and the gate would be ignored within a day. Verified live: `bc60735` correctly PASSED while the preview served a later commit.

The failure path is split on evidence, not on a timeout guess. If Vercel has a build in flight, poll (measured build duration ~25 s). If nothing is pending, wait one 90 s webhook grace and then **stop** — that is the proven-futile case, and burning a five-minute budget on it teaches sessions to skip the gate. It prints the remedy rather than just the problem: `POST /v13/deployments` is 402 on this plan, so an empty poke commit is the working trigger. Exit `2` (cannot run) is deliberately distinct from `1` (stale) — an unrunnable check must never read as a pass.

**A counter-example check changed the design mid-session.** The first pitch to John claimed one SHA check covers frontend and `api/` alike. Measured, that is true of the *build* but not the whole path: the dev preview's HTML is edge-cached (`X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, `Age: 298`, and `Cache-Control: no-cache` / `Pragma: no-cache` both fail to bust it), while a POST to the `api/` route is never cached (`MISS`). So the gate is **sufficient alone for the regression run**, and **necessary-but-not-sufficient for frontend visual QA**, which still needs the bundle-grep second layer. `STANDARDS.md` §6 states both paths as a table rather than one rule.

**Windows detail worth keeping:** the script's direct-invocation guard uses `pathToFileURL(process.argv[1])`, not a hand-built `file://${path}`. The hand-built form parses the drive letter as a URL *host*, so the comparison never matches and the gate silently no-ops when run directly — a guard that fails open is worse than no guard.

**QA (10/10, run by the design session, not the coding agent).** Serving commit named; the serving commit itself → exit 0; a genuine ancestor → exit 0 (the concurrent-session case the gate lives or dies on); current `dev` tip while undeployed → exit 1 `no-build-fired` with the remedy printed; a synthetic never-pushed commit → exit 1; `VERCEL_TOKEN` unset → exit 2 with the `ENV-VARS.md` pointer. `STANDARDS.md` §6 no longer opens with the "After every Vercel deploy:" assumption (the section's single deleted line) and carries both the measured table and the two-path table; runbook Step 0 precedes the endpoint/auth step with **8 insertions, 0 deletions**, so `SES-28`'s concurrent edit to the same file rebases cleanly. Exactly 3 files. `test-ses-015.mjs` (12 assertions) deleted before commit.

**One honest gap:** the *pending-build → poll → pass* path was never exercised live — every run during QA found either coverage or nothing queued. The polling branch is covered by unit assertions only. Not a blocker; recorded so a future session doesn't assume it was observed.

**Residue.** `SES-39` (Tooling) — the row's third proposal, "prefer local dev QA when the change doesn't need `api/`," deliberately scoped out: it does nothing for bucket 1 (that driver needs the serverless route, which local dev 404s on, per `SES-014`) and converts a hard gate into a per-session judgment call. `SES-40` (Tech Debt) — found live when the documented SQL failed: `session-setup`'s step 3b tells every session to claim an ID via `next_number`, but the column is `last_issued_number`; it errors loudly rather than corrupting anything, but the improvised recovery is exactly how `SES-18`'s desync started.

## S-CHI-90-design / S-CHI-90 (v6.3.211, `a184efe`, 2026-07-28 night, worktree `design-chi-90`, 3 files) — one definition of "a call", on both screens

**The question John settled.** The CHI Agents drawer said Eleanor Voss — The Librarian had made **4,291 calls**; AI Audit, for the same agent, would say ~**1,801**. Both labelled "Calls", both in the same product. Cause: `LOG-81` (v6.3.203) redefined a call for AI Audit and deliberately left the shared `LOG-21` core alone, so `buildActivitySummary()` kept incrementing `d.calls` for every logged row. AI Audit never felt it — its `byAgent.calls` comes from `countableCallsByAgent`, computed outside the core, which **discards** the core's `.calls` entirely and uses only `d.totalCost`. The CHI drawer renders the core's `.calls` directly, so it alone kept operations semantics. John chose **AI Audit's definition**: the drawer is keyed by *agent*, which structurally makes it the same surface as By Agent; §12 (LOCKED) keeps operations semantics with By *Service*, and service ≠ agent.

**What shipped.** `calls` is now gated by `LOG-81`'s existing `isCountableCall` — no second predicate, the anti-drift point of the session. The raw every-row count moved to a new `operations` field, which drives **only** the drawer's active/potential split. That second half was not in the one-line fix as first described and was added during Architect Review: `activeIds` filtered on the same `.calls` field, so gating it would let an agent whose screen contribution is entirely deterministic be relabelled **"not yet used on this screen"** while doing thousands of real library reads. `LOG-81` had accepted `calls: 0` for that case because AI Audit still renders the agent; the CHI drawer has a consumer AI Audit does not.

**QA 10/10, and every agent reconciled to SQL exactly** — not within tolerance, exactly, on all 11: Michelle Manning — Project Manager 4,843 → **2,784**, Eleanor Voss — The Librarian 4,291 → **1,801**, Marcus Webb — GEO CSO Expert 2,803 → **2,357**, Dan Bingham — AI Prompt Strategist **28 unchanged** (no deterministic rows, no dup halves — proof the gate is selective, not a blanket reduction). Header stayed "11 active · 0 potential"; desktop and mobile 375×812 both rendered all 11 with identical numbers. AI Audit was verified *correct*, not merely unchanged: By Agent and Total Calls matched fresh SQL exactly (Eleanor 2,014 / Michelle 4,510 / Marcus 2,979 / total 15,127).

**Avg Cost — proven unchanged rather than eyeballed.** The two changed hunks are the initializer literal and the increment; the `rowCost`/`totalCost`/`costCount`/`avgCost` lines are byte-identical, so the value is mathematically the same. A SQL cross-check was attempted and produced a *useful negative*: **zero** rows in the drawer's scope carry `cost_usd`, so every displayed cost is `computeCallCost()`-derived client-side and cannot be reproduced in SQL at all — worth knowing before a future session tries to reconcile cost the way this one reconciled counts.

**QA ran against a local dev server, not the dev URL.** Frontend-only change, so localhost exercises the identical code path against the identical Supabase — and it sidesteps `SES-33` entirely rather than reasoning about whether deploys were firing. This is exactly `SES-39`'s proposal (scoped out of `S-SES-015` the same day) being used in practice; the one cost is that `api/` routes 500 under `vite dev`, which is why the console shows `fetchNewsCards ... failed: 500` and nothing else.

**Two live-QA mechanics worth reusing.** (1) The Agents drawer would not open via `.click()` on an ancestor — React maps the event by target, so the click has to be dispatched on a **leaf inside** the `onClick` div and read in a **separate** tool call, because the state update has not flushed within the same synchronous block. (2) A first mobile read appeared to contradict desktop (Marcus 2,497 vs 2,357). It was a bad DOM walk, not a bug: re-parsing by explicit StatCell structure returned numbers identical to desktop and to SQL. Re-measuring the database before believing the screen is what settled it.

**Residue.** `LOG-112` (Observability) — the drawer's per-agent `byPattern` block reads `row.patterns_used`, frozen legacy per `.claude/rules/ai-pattern-signature.md` (§19k/§19l). 1,925 of Eleanor Voss — The Librarian's 2,411 deterministic `librarian` rows carry it, so her card now reads `1801 CALLS` above a `Rag — (3450 calls)` row. The sub-rows were never a decomposition of the headline (a row counts in every pattern it carries; pattern-less rows never appear), and pre-`CHI-90` they always sat below it, so nothing looked wrong. That is no longer self-evident to a reader — flagged to John at close-out, because fixing it also needs his call on whether deterministic latency stays visible in the drawer at all.

**`HAR-20` post-deploy verification (2026-07-29, worktree `ses29-status`) — closes the one item the design session left owed.** Vercel's git integration resumed; serving commit `e89d698` was confirmed by ancestry to contain `94acad9`/`525c394`/`fefbe79`, so all three fixes are live on the dev preview. Six live `qg-content-context-intent` judge calls through the **deployed** function: 6/6 terminal verdicts, **zero** `Parse failed and retry also failed`, and the judge discriminated correctly (3 rich artifacts passed, 3 hollow failed) rather than merely not crashing. `durable_hops` still holds exactly 7 failed judge hops — all pre-fix, latest 01:18:46Z — alongside the intent's first-ever `complete` hop. `HAR-20` archived. Note for future gate use: `scripts/check-deploy-current.js` answers *"is the preview current with HEAD"*, which fails whenever any unrelated commit lands after the last build; when the question is *"does the preview contain my commit,"* test ancestry against the serving SHA instead. Also observed: importing that script rather than invoking it exits 0 silently — the `SES-28` vacuous-pass shape, worth a look if it is ever wrapped by another tool.

**`DAT-11` repair half applied (2026-07-29, John approved, worktree `dat11-repair`) — and it surfaced the defect's mirror image.** Both wrongly-retired baseline rows are back to `active`: `59eede59` (Signal Mobile — a true orphan, nothing ever superseded it, and its absence is what broke case 8's designed Horizon-vs-Signal comparison) and `35f01679` (Nippo Carrier — retired *mid-run* by agent-authored `b1daf789`). Nothing was deleted: `b1daf789` keeps its content and stays active, its `supersedes_id` was cleared so it no longer claims to retire a baseline row. **All 20 `is_baseline` rows are now active and the runbook §1 gate passes.**

**Correction worth recording, because this session had it wrong first.** The root-cause findings called `b88cf8cd`/`629f2184`/`85fa8d76` "orphan/duplicate residue rows" to clean up. Reading them before touching them showed otherwise: they are real, substantive agent-authored content (1,032–1,205 chars of specific Nordholm and Elevate Mobility analysis). The actual defect is the **opposite** of deletion — the promote chain leaves the OLD row `active` when its status flip is denied, so **both copies stay retrievable**. A repo-wide check found **5** such incomplete flips, and **3 of the 5 stale rows are `is_baseline=true`** — including `0d09ac6e` (Upgrade Cycles) sitting behind a row literally titled *"DAT-7 End-to-End Live Test"*. So the fix is completing the interrupted flip, never removing content, and the enforcement half is more load-bearing than first scoped: agent output is retiring seed corpus rows in both directions. Left unrepaired deliberately — that is Data Room surgery affecting retrieval for every question, and `DAT-11`'s enforcement semantics are John's call. Generalisable lesson: *"residue to delete" earned by inference is not the same as residue verified by reading the rows* — the read reversed the remedy.

## 2026-07-29 — S-AGT-37-design / S-AGT-37 (v6.3.214, worktree `agt37-citation-ids`, data-only) — **QA FAILED; the finding is worth more than the fix**

`AGT-37`'s premise was that Elena Cho — The Reasoner lifts truncated chunk references out of Priya Nair — Forecast/Theory/Performance Expert's prose, and that constraining her own Skill would stop it. The Skill edit shipped (one `skill_profiles` row, surgical, siblings byte-identical) and **the fix does not work.**

**The coding session's 3/3 green was vacuous, and it said so itself** — a good catch worth crediting: `--only upgrade-cycles` ran clean three times, but `durable_hops` held no `reasoner-intent` rows, because Elena chose `no_action` each time. A hop only exists on `consolidate`, so the amended sentence — which governs only that branch — was never exercised. A passing run proved nothing.

**Design-session QA therefore forced the branch directly** (three controlled calls to `memory-consolidation`/`reasoner-intent` through the deployed API, reversal-shaped content so `consolidate` is the correct choice):

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| **B** — prose carries a real full UUID | `consolidate`, `ids=["0cecd001-097d-4e92-b46d-519d9e8f96fe"]`, write **OK** |
| **C** — prose carries no id-like text | `consolidate`, `ids=[]`, write **OK** |
| **A** — prose carries truncated `(id: 0cecd001)` | **DENIED** `denied-source-chunk-cross-room-or-missing`, reproduced twice |

So the amended instruction is correct, harmless, and did **not** silence consolidation (C disproves the obvious worry that added caution would push her to `no_action`) — it simply fails on the one input it was written for. Faced with an id-shaped decoy, the model copies it regardless of an explicit, emphatic prohibition.

**This is the second occurrence of the same class, and that is the real finding.** `DAT-7` mitigated Nadia Rahman — Data Analyst's `chunk_id` echo by instruction as well, and it also lost — `chunk_id="H1"` on four completed hops in the 0/24 run. Two different agents, two different Skills, two instruction-only guards, defeated by the same shape of input at temperature 0. **Generalization to carry forward: an id-shaped decoy defeats instruction-level guards. Do not attempt a third wording.** The fix has to be structural — either write-side sanitation that strips non-UUID entries (so a malformed id degrades to the honest empty array instead of killing the hop, while a fabricated *full* UUID is still refused by the existing guard), or the durable answer of handing Elena real citations as structured data so she never parses prose at all. John picks; `AGT-37` stays open and is **not** archived.

**Process note:** the Skill edit was deliberately left in place rather than reverted — B and C show it is strictly better guidance and does no harm — but the row is marked 🔴 so nobody reads a shipped version number as a working fix.

## 2026-07-29 — S-HAR-21-design (v6.3.222, worktree `design-agt-37`, docs-only) — **the structural fix for `AGT-37`, and the finding that made it cheap**

Picked up `AGT-37` the morning after its instruction-only fix failed QA, with an explicit constraint from John: no third wording, walk through the structural options, get a pick before writing.

**The finding that re-scoped the whole item.** The prior session's row scoped the durable fix as "code, screen + driver + assembly" — a build. It isn't. The correct full-UUID citations already exist on the screen at the moment of the commit click, and are already handed to Nadia Farouk — Data Expert one line below the Elena call. `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx:4198` destructures `citations` alongside `flaggedAnswer`; `:4204` passes `citations[0]` to Nadia as `disputed_chunk_id`; Elena Cho — The Reasoner's `task_context` at `:4212` receives prose only. Priya Nair — Forecast/Theory/Performance Expert's theory-test sections are `{text, citations}` objects (`CHI-65`) and `:4205` joins only the `.text` halves, discarding three further citation arrays. Live confirmation of the shape from `ai_activity_log`: `ci-answer-intent` → `citations: ["6bef824b-c56e-487b-a976-cccdefe567c4"]`. **We were asking a model to reconstruct from prose a value already held, correctly, in a variable on the same line.**

Two negative checks that mattered as much as the positive one. `formatLibraryEntry` (`lib/librarian.js:60`) renders `[id: ${m.id}]` — the **full** UUID — so the truncation is genuinely the model's own behaviour, not a harness artifact upstream. And Elena's `memory-consolidation` rows carry **no** `retrieved_chunk_ids`: she is handed text, she does not retrieve, so the id cannot be recovered from already-captured §19i facts. There was no free version of the fix; the value has to travel.

**Two of John's calls shaped the design.**

*Both write paths, not one.* Supabase shows `traits->>'handler' = 'reasoning-write'` returns **two** Skills — `reasoner-intent` and `data-patch-execute-intent` — contradicting `reasoning-write.js:7`'s comment claiming only the latter. So the rule had to be written generically. Nadia Farouk — Data Expert's path has the same retype step one degree milder (she is *handed* `chunk_id` structurally, then asked to type it back out), and it manufactures the decoy too: a stored `pending_confirmations.proposed_action` from this same day contains, in her own prose, "Three independent consolidated Data Room entries, with IDs 2479db72, 9e3c8eb8, and 27044da3" — with `chunk_id: null` on the row. Filed as `AGT-39`. John's reasoning for covering both was decisive: restricting the rule to Elena would take *more* code, and the exclusion would have to name an agent.

*A service, not an agent action.* The root cause is a model put in charge of an id, twice. The work contains no judgment, and structurally a capability here would start a capability execution inside `runLoop()`'s terminal step. Recorded as the principle **if the correct value is already known, no model touches it**, and as `utilizes_model: false` on the new `platform_services` row.

**Why a new service at all — reversing a prior deliberate choice.** `AA-189` inlined its own `UUID_RE` rather than extracting a helper and `DAT-6` re-affirmed that explicitly as a flagged Tier 2 decision. Sound at two copies; not at five — `search-harness.js:100` plus `librarian.js` 249/355/385/418, alongside two write handlers carrying byte-identical denial logic under a "Category M — both write handlers must stay in sync" comment. Writing this session's rule inline would have been copy number six. The change in facts, not a change of opinion, is what justified extracting. Collapse of the other five filed as `HAR-22`.

**The split, which fell out of the service decision rather than being imposed.** Building it as a service produced two sessions that each fit the three-file cap with no exception needed — where the original inline plan needed four files and John's sign-off to break the rule. `HAR-21` (v6.3.222) ships `lib/claim-resolver.js` plus its first consumer, and **alone unblocks Store as Forecast**: a malformed id degrades to an honest `[]` instead of a 422 that takes down the whole commit sequence. `AGT-37` remains open for the envelope threading that makes the link *correct* rather than merely honest, and its gate is explicit — it closes when a stored `the_reasoning` row carries the right chunk id, never when the click stops erroring.

**Also filed:** `HAR-23` (`reasoning-write.js`/`library-write.js` absent from `platform_services` while their siblings in the same folder are registered), `AGT-40` (provenance recovery when no id exists anywhere — the legitimately agent-shaped remainder), `SES-53` (this file records her as "Nadia Rahman — Data Analyst"; `agents.js:211` says Nadia Farouk — Data Expert — a sweep, since one wrong name propagates into every session that quotes the entry). `AGT-37`'s row exceeded the 2000-char cap and its history was moved — not deleted — to `docs/harvests/AGT-37.md`.

### `S-HAR-21` shipped the same day (v6.3.222, `b4445f8`) — QA 7/7 PASS

Coding agent (Opus 5) built it to spec: 3 files, nothing outside them, `search-harness.js`/`execute.js`/`request-receivable.js`/`src/` byte-identical to `origin/dev` (verified independently by diff, not taken from the report). Regression suite 16/16, `npm run build` clean, `platform_services` 31 → 32.

**The fix proven on the exact input that failed.** Deploy gate confirmed the preview was serving `b4445f8` before any live call. Three controlled `memory-consolidation`/`reasoner-intent` calls, consolidate branch forced directly:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| truncated `(id: 0cecd001)` in prose | HTTP 200, row `d7647f40`, `source_chunk_ids: []` — **was a 422 denial the day before** |
| real full UUID in prose | HTTP 200, row `87974f65`, `source_chunk_ids: ["0cecd001-097d-4e92-b46d-519d9e8f96fe"]` — not a blanket stripper |
| fabricated full UUID in prose | HTTP 200, row `1fb7901d`, `source_chunk_ids: []` — **vacuous, see below** |

**QA caught its own vacuous pass, which is the finding worth carrying.** The third call was written to prove the AA-189 guard still refuses a well-formed but nonexistent id. It returned success — and `ai_activity_log` showed why: `self_reported_claims: null`. **Elena Cho — The Reasoner silently declined to cite the fabricated id at all**, so nothing ever reached the guard. A green result proving nothing, the identical shape that made v6.3.214's run look successful. Re-run through the *other* Skill on this handler — Nadia Farouk — Data Expert's `data-patch-execute-intent`, which is told to echo a supplied `chunk_id` — the guard fired correctly: **HTTP 422 `denied-source-chunk-cross-room-or-missing`**. Same call with a real chunk id wrote row `8364c28c` carrying it, confirming her path is unbroken and now benefits from the same rule. **Generalization: with this class of bug an agent's *refusal* to emit is indistinguishable from a fix working — always read `self_reported_claims` before believing a pass.**

**Drop visibility confirmed:** the truncated-id call emitted its own `ai_type: 'deterministic'`, `feature: 'claim-resolver'` row carrying `dropped_reference_ids: ["0cecd001"]`. The malformed id is recorded, not silently swallowed.

**QA item 3 (the Store as Forecast click) was verified by controlled capability calls rather than a browser run, deliberately and on the record.** `HAR-21` touched no UI file, and the failing input depends on a model choosing to write a truncated id into prose — not something a UI run can be made to produce on demand. A browser pass would most likely have exercised an answer with no decoy at all, which is precisely the vacuous evidence this session already caught once. Five live scenarios through the real deployed pipeline is stronger evidence than one uncontrolled click, and `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` Step 5b's backend-only clause asks for a spot-check, not a full re-run.

**Two things the coding agent surfaced that changed close-out.** (1) `tracking_status: machinery` turned out to have a written definition in `ARCHITECTURE.md` §19m — "modules whose executions are attributed elsewhere … so nothing double-counts" — which Claim Resolver fits on the definition rather than by the inference the kickoff had to settle for. (2) Because the resolver logs **only** drops, populating its `match_keys` would render a call count that is really a drop count; `match_keys` was left `[]` and the residue recorded on `LOG-89` instead, per `.claude/rules/platform-services-directory.md`'s requirement that newly-detected unattributed activity have a backlog row. An honest gap beats a wrong number (§19l).

### `AGT-37`'s kickoff corrected post-commit — `task_context` is prompt material, not a delivery channel

Caught by John immediately after the kickoff was pushed, from a one-line comprehension check: *"this is simply allowing the envelope to carry the id and pass it on to the agent?"* The phrase "to the agent" was wrong for the design — the id is meant to travel *past* Elena Cho — The Reasoner — but checking why it was wrong exposed that the committed kickoff **would in fact have delivered it to her.**

`db-assembly.js` serializes every non-empty `task_context` key straight into the agent's prompt: `HAR-06` on the `.goal` branch (~L548) and `AI-44`'s TASK DETAILS fallback (~L572). Elena's `task_context` carries no `goal`, so it takes the AI-44 branch and every key lands in her prompt. Task 1 as written — "add them to `task_context` under the key `source_chunk_ids`" — would have rendered a real chunk id in front of the one agent this ticket exists to keep away from ids.

**It would still have passed its own QA.** She has no output slot for the field once it's removed from her contract, and the handler prefers the caller's value regardless, so the stored row would have carried the right id and the checklist would have gone green. The damage is one step downstream: `AGT-39` records that these agents write ids into their prose, and Nadia Farouk — Data Expert already demonstrably does it. Handing Elena a real id gives her material to write into her `content`, which becomes the *next* step's prose decoy — the fix quietly feeding the bug class it was built to end.

**Correction:** a sibling field, `handler_context`, passed only to `sendRequest` and never to `assemblePrompt()`/`enrichPrompt()`. Same two relay files, same one-line-each changes. The kickoff now carries a non-negotiable second QA assertion — the supplied id must appear nowhere in the assembled prompt — with an explicit note that a green first assertion plus a leaked prompt is a FAIL, not a partial pass. The accept path (`resolveAccept`, ~L1515) threads it too, so Nadia's id also stops round-tripping through her model.

**What this establishes beyond `AGT-37`:** the platform had no distinction between *agent-facing context* and *handler-facing facts* — `task_context` was silently both. That absence is precisely what made the wrong design look obvious. `handler_context` is a general harness capability any write handler can now use.

**Process note:** the near-miss came from assuming a parameter's purpose from its name and its position in the call chain, without reading what the assembly layer does with it. `task_context` was verified to *reach* the handler-dispatch boundary; it was never verified for what else it touches on the way. Verifying where a value travels is not the same as verifying who reads it.

Worth stating once: the driver runs **locally from the worktree**, so an engine-side fix (`SES-62`) is present by checkout while an app-side fix (`AGT-44`'s Skill data, `DAT-12`'s `retrieval_scope`) depends on deploy/Supabase — those are different currency questions and `check-deploy-current` only answers the second.

Verified live, before writing the kickoff: `.method` is `NULL` on this row (and on `data-patch-execute-intent`) and is not the field the model actually reads — `traits.analysis_instructions` is, confirmed against `api/prompt/db-assembly.js`'s intent branch, which concatenates `objective` + `method` + `analysis_instructions` in that order. Inserted one paragraph into `analysis_instructions`, in narrative sequence (not tacked onto the empty `method` field, which would have rendered as a disconnected fragment ahead of the real instruction). Both corrections were folded into the kickoff and its QA before any Supabase write, rather than discovered mid-session.

**Part 1's own closure gate still failed — a genuine scope conflict, not a QA miss.** The coding session's own report surfaced it: case 6 is hardcoded to the `edit` resolution (`CASE_RESOLUTIONS`, `chi-true-regression.mjs`), so the artifact the beta gate actually judges is the **edit-resolve** artifact — and that call built `user_reasoning` from the reviewer's edited text **alone**, discarding the theory-test figures before Nadia ever received them. The Skill fix was correct and proven; it simply had nothing to carry forward on the one path the gate measures. This is a fork the automated Design→Code→Verify loop's own rule anticipates ("still stop and ask John... when the coding agent's report surfaces a genuine scope conflict") — reported to John rather than silently expanded or silently left half-done.

**Part 2 — the edit-resolve path (`S-AGT-47b`, v6.3.235, 2 files: `MarketIntelligenceScreen.jsx` + `chi-true-regression.mjs`, no Layer 3/`api/` change).** Traced live, not assumed: `api/capabilities/execute.js`'s resolve branch (`:1613-1640`) is unconditional passthrough — `task_context: edited_task_context`, nothing to change there. The original theory-test text was already sitting unread in state: the screen stores it as `hypFlow.confirmation.user_reasoning` at the first call (`:4304`), and the edit-round-trip state update (`:4359-4362`) spreads `...prev.confirmation` rather than replacing it, so it survives repeated edits untouched — the bug was never losing the data, only never reading a field that was already there. Fix: destructure `user_reasoning` at the one call site that builds `edited_task_context` and join it with the reviewer's edit instead of discarding it (`[originalUserReasoning, editedText].filter(Boolean).join("\n")`); the driver's equivalent (`jointText`) was already in scope, same one-line-shape change. Deliberately **not** extracted into a shared helper between the two files — matches this repo's established "driver mirrors screen, independently" convention rather than introducing a new abstraction for a 1-line-shape fix.

**Concurrency, handled rather than missed:** a concurrent session (`DAT-16b`, v6.3.236, `4a45143`) wrote to `data-patch-intent.method` — the same row, a different column — partway through this session, for an unrelated reason (an honesty/sourcing instruction, "don't offer an adjacent real number as the asked-for value"). No collision: `jsonb_set` on `traits` and a plain `UPDATE` on `method` don't conflict, and `db-assembly.js` concatenates both. The coding session flagged it rather than assuming; the design session independently re-ran the regression against the post-`DAT-16b` live state before closing anything out.

**Independent verification, not accepted on the coding reports alone (`STANDARDS.md`/`feedback-manual-qa-gate` discipline):** re-ran `node scripts/chi-true-regression.mjs --only upgrade-cycles` directly from the design session, against current `dev` and current Supabase state, after both parts had shipped. Result: `case_pass: true`, `fail_causes: []`; both `theory_test` and `forecast_draft` verdicts `pass: true`, `failed_criteria: []` — every criterion (`named_entities_present`, `quantitative_content_present`, `actionable_guidance_present`, `platform_language_detected` clean, `asked_metric_present`) passing on real, quoted figures (Japan ~26mo, Mexico ~33%, US 3.84yr, spread narrowing 2020→2025). `check-deploy-current.js` confirmed the serving preview contains the final commit.

**Not this row's problem, flagged rather than fixed or ignored:** the coding session also found `vitrine-tech` (case 9) failing live, under `DAT-16`'s honest-gap reclassification (a real corpus figure exists, the agent correctly reports it, and the honest-gap rubric — which requires the asked figure to be *absent* — fails a correct answer on the wrong bar). Proven structurally out of this diff's reach, not just pattern-matched: `RESOLUTIONS` doesn't include `vitrine-tech`, so it runs `expected_journey: "direct"` and never calls the function either changed file touches. Left for `DAT-16`'s own owner.

**Process note — two rounds of "no blind fixes" in one session.** Both real corrections this session (the `.method`→`traits.analysis_instructions` field catch, and the edit-resolve gap) came from verifying live before committing to a claim, not from trusting the design harvest's own prior-session prose or the coding session's first completion report. Neither would have been caught by re-reading source; both needed a real query or a real run.

## 2026-07-30 — `design-arch-beta-0729` round 3 (docs-only, no version bump) — **the score fell to 1/4 and it is the most useful result yet: three failures, one root cause, and the platform is being punished for telling the truth**

**John's ask:** *"i have finished the 3 tickets. do you pre-test again?"* — `AGT-47`, `SES-65`, `DAT-16`.

**Result: 1 PASS / 3 FAIL in 29 min** (round 2: 2 PASS / 2 FAIL in 16 min). Per-case table and deploy reasoning: `docs/BETA-TRIAGE.md` §3 bucket 1.

**Both in-scope fixes are confirmed working.** `AGT-47` took case 6 `upgrade-cycles` — the longest journey in the set — from FAIL to a clean PASS on both artifacts. `DAT-16` Part 1 is confirmed: case 9's `answer` artifact now passes. That is real, measured progress on the two hardest items of the morning.

**⚠️ Amended within the same session, before any other session acted on it — the paragraph immediately below is wrong in its diagnosis, and the correction makes the remaining work far smaller. Kept rather than deleted because the wrong inference is the instructive part.** Two things were checked in Supabase after writing it. (1) **`platform-language-guardrail`'s clause 3 already permits honest disclosure** — *"When something is missing, say what is missing in business terms and what would resolve it — describe the absent information itself, never where you looked for it."* So the two standards were never in conflict; the permitted phrasing was there from the start, and **no ruling, carve-out, or loosening is needed.** (2) **Case 12's flip is not caused by the Guardrails Skill.** It was attached `2026-07-29 23:48:20 UTC`; round 2 ran `02:03 UTC` on 07-30 and case 12 **passed with it already attached**, round 3 failed on identical data. Guardrail present for both — so that is Owen Marsh — The Proofreader's own judgment varying, exactly as `AGT-50` originally framed it. **The real cause of case 24 is coverage, not conflict:** the guardrail is attached to only `hypothesis-evaluation` (Priya Nair) and `data-analysis` (Nadia Farouk) — **not** `channel-intelligence` (Marcus Webb, who emits the `answer` on every direct question), `quality-gate` (Owen Marsh), or `project-manager` (Michelle Manning). `AGT-44`'s close-out claimed "every artifact-producing agent" and covered **2 of 5**. Case 24 was failed for breaking a rule Marcus was never given. **Minimal fix: ONE `capability_skill_profiles` row (`channel-intelligence`), no code, no re-wording — "two rows" was written here first and corrected the same session; `quality-gate` and `project-manager` are deliberate exclusions (capability-wide attachment would reach Owen's judging intents; the drawer's routing reasoning is mechanics-as-content).** **The generalisable lesson — and the reason this went undetected through three rounds and two sessions:** no agent can see the attachment table, so no agent could notice the standard it is judged against was never delivered to the agent being judged. The gap is *coverage visibility*, not instruction quality, and it belongs to mechanical enforcement (`SE-02`/`SES-28` class — assert every capability emitting user-facing text carries the guardrail) rather than to any prompt.

**The three failures share one root cause, and it is not a bug in any one agent: the platform is now penalised for honest disclosure.** `AGT-44`'s Guardrails Skill forbids narrating platform mechanics; the `honest-gap` class *requires* an agent to say the Data Room lacks the asked-for fact. Saying so **is** narrating platform mechanics. An honest answer therefore fails `platform_language_detected` and a concealing one fails for fabricating — as the two standards are currently written there is no satisfying answer.
- **Case 24** — Marcus Webb — GEO CSO Expert disclosed *"MacRumors headline only, no access to full article"* and was failed for it, Owen Marsh — The Proofreader conceding the trap in his own critique: *"The content itself is strong—specific geographies, real numbers, clear next steps—but the framing reads as platform narration of the agent's constraints."*
- **Case 12** — Priya Nair — Forecast/Theory/Performance Expert's `theory_test` failed for *"back-office vocabulary (data pull, retrieval gap, visibility problem, measurement problem)"* while honestly explaining a real corpus gap.
- **Case 9** — the mirror image: under `honest-gap`, supplying the asked figure is the failure, and both remaining artifacts supply one (Vitrine's own 40% completion rate presented **as** the gap).

**`AGT-53` was claimed and immediately retired into `AGT-50`.** `design-dat-16` had filed `AGT-50` hours earlier over the same scope; this session claimed an ID before checking. Caught and unwound within the session rather than left to close under two numbers — **the identical pattern John had to unwind that morning when `AGT-45` turned out to be `AGT-36`'s unfinished scope under a second ID.** The round-3 evidence was folded into `AGT-50`, including the fact that changes its diagnosis: **case 12 passed this criterion in rounds 1 and 2 and fails in round 3**, i.e. after the Guardrails Skill reached every artifact-producing agent. `AGT-50` was framed as an inconsistent judge; that before/after points at the standard itself, and the two diagnoses imply different fixes — re-wording Owen's criteria treats a symptom if the conflict is structural.

**Two open rows settled by observation rather than argument.** `SES-64`'s predicted false-FAIL on #24 **did** occur — green in round 2, red in round 3, same code and the same degraded-article condition, so the rounds bracket it and the behaviour is confirmed unpredictable in both directions. And `DAT-16`'s QA, which its own row listed as pending, is a **FAIL**: Part 2 set `data-patch-intent.method` for Nadia Farouk — Data Expert only, while the failing `theory_test` artifact is Priya's and was never in scope.

**Consequence worth carrying: fixing `SES-64` alone will not make case 24 pass.** Reclassifying it to `honest-gap` leaves the identical Guardrails penalty on the identical disclosure. `SES-64` and `AGT-50` have to land together.

**`CHI-96` filed (Speed, bucket 2 — not 1).** Case 6 went **193 s → 828 s** between rounds, ~4.3×, and accounts for most of the set's 16→29 min increase. Suspected cause is `AGT-47`'s larger `user_reasoning` payload now carrying the original theory text alongside the edit. **Filed with an explicit instruction not to revert `AGT-47`** — it is the only case that improved this round; if the slowdown is real the fix is payload shape, not removal.

**A correction this session owes its own advice.** Round 2 recommended making `asked_metric_present` a hard gate on rich-answer artifacts. `S-SES-65` turned that down correctly: the criterion's Skill returns `false` whenever the question asks for **no quantity at all**, so gating it would fail correct answers — case 24 among them. The recommendation read `false` as "the asked figure is missing" without checking it also encodes "no figure was asked for", and runbook §5b had already locked it not-scored on that path under `AGT-36b`'s §8 approval. `SES-65` shipped the half that was real (a failure can no longer report an empty reason list) and verified scoring byte-unchanged across all 972 criterion/class/flag combinations. **Round 2's prediction of "1 PASS / 3 FAIL if the ruling lands" was therefore void** — the score did land there, for entirely unrelated reasons, which is exactly the coincidence that would have validated bad reasoning had nobody checked why.

**Standing caveat, stated once:** case 12's flip and `CHI-96`'s timing are each one run against two priors. Suggestive, not proof — a repeat run separates a regression from Owen's own judgment varying, and neither should be scoped as fact until then.

Case 12 has now failed four different ways in six rounds; it is the platform's canary, and its reds have never once been caused by the fix under test.

**Recommendation shipped with this entry: stop sampling, run the full 24-case regression.** The 4/4-green trigger was this session's own invention; John's approved bucket-1 strategy (2026-07-28) is regression-first — run, then schedule fixes for what actually fires. ## 2026-07-31 — `S-CHI-96-design` (docs-only) — `CHI-96` measured twice and closed: the "4.3× regression" was variance; ~6 min is the edit journey's construction cost

**Runs:** case 6 `upgrade-cycles` twice, dedicated, deploy gate PASSED (`fe8c5ce` serving, contains `8543596`): **455 s and 326 s, both full `case_pass: true`**, zero failed criteria. Sequence closed at 193 → 828 → 394 → 455 → 326.

**Root-cause accounting (the part worth keeping):** wall-clock alone couldn't separate variance from regression, so every second was attributed via `ai_activity_log`. Result: ~434 s of run 1's 455 s and ~314 s of run 2's 326 s are real model-call latency, zero idle. The edit journey runs Nadia Farouk — Data Expert's forecast-patch chain **twice** (draft, then edit re-draft; each ~80–100 s of Nadia → Michelle Manning — Project Manager → Nadia → Alex Reeves — Screen Controls Editor → Nadia) plus the accept-execute chain — ~15–18 sequential model calls. `AGT-47`'s payload is exonerated: edit-leg inputs 3–12K tokens, max single call 35 s (nowhere near `AA-139`'s 60 s hop budget). ±2 min run-to-run variance on a chain that long covers the 828 s reading.

**Wrinkle that became `SES-67` (Observability):** the two mid-journey patch chains ran under trace ids the driver's `REPORT_JSON` never captured (suspect: `call()`'s `job_id`/`continue` path) — the run first *looked* like a 200 s silent gap until a time-window query found the chains. Filed Beta-gate (bucket 1, §2b evidence class), `BETA.md` §2b item 10.

**Discharge of the row's own options:** measure 2–3 runs ✓; variance → downgrade/close ✓ (John's call, this session); do-not-revert `AGT-47` ✓ (untouched); payload-shape fix moot. `CHI-96` archived; `BETA.md` row 28 synced same commit. No kickoff doc, no version claimed, no code touched.
