## STANDARDS.md narrative moved 2026-08-01 (SES-68)

Moved verbatim out of `docs/STANDARDS.md` during its 45 KB → baseline trim. Every block below is
the "found live" history behind a rule that **still stands** in `STANDARDS.md` — the rule statement
itself was left in place there, with a one-clause `history: docs/SESSIONS.md` pointer back to this
appendix. Nothing here is itself a rule, a test category, or a checklist item; read it as evidence,
not as standing instruction.

### From Section 1 (Session Naming & Versioning) — version must strictly increment every session

This broke 2026-07-02: `S-ARCH-AGENT-LOOP-01`, `S-APPLE-02b`, `S-ARCH-PM-BROKER-01`, and `S-ARCH-LOOP-PATCH-01` all stamped `v6.0.0` into their version headers instead of incrementing session-over-session, because nothing in `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`'s kickoff-doc checklist explicitly said to bump it — the old checklist only said to "confirm current version," not increment past it.

### From Section 2 (Session Scope Rules), rule 5 — `run-all.js` is the gate

Before `SES-28`, a bare invocation exited 0 having tested nothing — `LOG-86`'s kickoff doc specced exactly that and would have shipped a red suite reporting green.

### From Section 2 (Session Scope Rules), rule 5 — run the suite against current dependencies

Found live: the installed tree was two weeks older than `package.json`, so `LOG-77-9` failed on a missing `@vercel/functions` that was never a code problem.

### From Section 5 (Always Required) — a Skill's instruction text and its output schema change together (`AGT-36b`)

Found live: `qg-content-context-intent` gained a fifth criterion in `method` while its schema still declared five keys, so Owen — Proofreader emitted nothing for it; the driver's explicit-`false` guard then failed *every* case in the class, i.e. the change silently accomplished the opposite of its purpose. The kickoff doc that specced it named only `method` — so this check belongs here, where a session looks before committing, not in any one kickoff.

### From Section 5 (Always Required) — every Manual QA item tests only the change under test (`S-SES-62`)

Found live: `SES-57`'s item 6 ("Marcus states the gap") tested its own payload plumbing, `CHI-91`'s Skill clause, **and** whether `api/fetch-article.js` ever reports a failure at all — the last of which is `CHI-95`. `SES-57` shipped correct and was held open for a day on an item that was never testing it.

Corollary narrative, same session (the surviving rule is "do not size a blocker from two samples"):

The claim that `CHI-95` made the honest-gap path unreachable came from two measured URLs; the first live run produced a real `401`, a populated reason, and the clause firing verbatim — so the "blocker" had been over-scoped and the moved criterion was already satisfied.

### From Section 6 (Browser Test Checklist) — "Why this is step 0 — the measured reality"

Across the 156 commits on `origin/dev` since 2026-07-28 12:00 CST, compared against every `dev` deployment Vercel actually produced:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Median lag from commit → first build containing it | 37 s |
| p90 lag | 852 s (14 min) |
| Max lag | 2,973 s (49.5 min) |
| Commits waiting > 5 min | 44 / 156 (28%) |
| Commits waiting > 10 min | 31 / 156 (20%) |

A ~46-minute window that evening produced no `dev` build at all, covering ~8 commits from six different sessions.

### From Section 7 (Manual QA Checklist Rules) — Status column vocabulary

This exists because free-texted status phrasing silently evaded the `session-hygiene` skill's Done-row archival check for weeks — the check only matched the literal string `✅ Done`, so any other completion phrasing never got flagged for archiving to `docs/FEATURES-ARCHIVE.md`. Found 2026-07-16; 12 backlogged rows recovered in one sweep once the check was broadened to match any Status cell starting with `✅` (see `.claude/skills/session-hygiene/SKILL.md` Section 3).

### From Section 10 (Change Log) — root-cause tails

The dated change statements stay in `STANDARDS.md` Section 10; only these root-cause narratives moved.

- **2026-06-15 (Architect Review mandatory + Category M added):** Root cause: AiBadge labels set from SVC design intent without verifying PATTERN_CATALOG active status — Reflection listed on Playbook badge while marked inactive in catalog.
- **2026-06-24 (Section 11 — agent build completeness):** Root cause: Victoria Chen shipped without standard fields; RosterScreen crashed on `trainableBy.toUpperCase()`.
- **2026-06-24 (Section 12 — canonical model ID + SERVICE_CATALOG roadmap):** Root cause: short-form model IDs in logAICall() call sites split model rows in AI Audit; services shipped without updating roadmap field left live services listed in Platform Roadmap.
- **2026-07-02 (Section 1 strengthened):** Root cause: 4 consecutive sessions (`S-ARCH-AGENT-LOOP-01`, `S-APPLE-02b`, `S-ARCH-PM-BROKER-01`, `S-ARCH-LOOP-PATCH-01`) all stamped `v6.0.0` because the kickoff-doc checklist only said to confirm the current version, not increment it. `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` Step 4 now has an explicit version-assignment step.
- **2026-07-02 (Category L scoping breadth):** Root cause: `S-ARCH-AGENT-LOOP-03` ran 4 full live tests (25 min, repeated 55s-timeout retries) for a 4-row data-only session where 3 rows re-exercised a mechanism already proven live twice by prior sessions — only 1 row (`qg-review-intent`'s `delegate_to_agent`-from-`task_context` path) was actually novel.
- **2026-07-07 (root cause protocol gains Step 1):** Root cause: John gets Claude status-page incident emails and had no standing step connecting them to QA-failure diagnosis — an upstream incident could otherwise get root-caused as a DeepBench code defect.
- **2026-07-08 (Category L loop-closure proof specificity):** Root cause: `AA-110`/`S-APPLE-05`'s "enablement" keyword check was satisfiable from pre-existing seeded content, not uniquely tied to the new write being tested.
- **2026-07-16 (Section 7 Status column vocabulary):** Root cause: free-texted completion phrasing (`✅ Fixed and verified`, `✅ Closed`, etc.) evaded the `session-hygiene` skill's literal `✅ Done` Done-row check for weeks; 12 rows recovered in a broadened sweep. `session-hygiene` SKILL.md Section 3 updated to match any `✅`-prefixed Status cell going forward.
- **2026-07-28 (Section 6 rewritten, `SES-015`, v6.3.209):** Root cause: the section assumed "after every Vercel deploy," but Vercel does not reliably build every push to `dev` — measured p90 lag 852 s, max 2,973 s, 20% of 156 commits waiting >10 min, plus a ~46-minute window that produced no `dev` build at all. Section now also carries the two-path sufficiency split (`api/` routes are never edge-cached, so the SHA gate alone suffices; frontend HTML *is* edge-cached and needs the bundle-grep second layer) and the 402 / poke-commit remedy. Supersedes `docs/BETA.md` §2b's bundle-grep-only prescription, which cannot cover the serverless regression path it was listed to protect.

## CLAUDE-DESIGN.md narrative moved 2026-08-01 (`SES-68`)

`CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` is read by every design session, so its incident retellings were costing tokens on every run. The rules themselves stayed in that file, each with its one-line "why" and a pointer here. Nothing below is a rule; each block is the full story behind one rule that still lives in `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md`.

### From Standing Rule — Backlog Capture, "criterion changes require an immediate full re-sweep" (added 2026-07-17)

Found live 2026-07-17: the criterion was broadened (more categories added) and, without an explicit ask to "redo the pass," the old classification would have silently stood — a re-sweep surfaced 14 rows in `FEATURES-NEXT.md`/`FEATURES-LATER.md` that fit the new criterion but hadn't been touched since the old one applied.

### From Standing Rule — Backlog Capture, "read full row text before any tier move" (added 2026-07-17)

Found live 2026-07-17: two rows (`AGT-005`, `SE-02`) looked like reasonable promotion candidates from a truncated view, but each carried its own explicit "stays here" rationale in the full text (one pointed to an already-promoted sibling row, the other was tied to a track John had already explicitly deferred) — a summary-only read would have moved both incorrectly, silently reversing a prior deliberate decision.

### From Standing Rule — Backlog Capture, "file same-investigation rows together for tier consistency" (added 2026-07-17)

Found live 2026-07-17: `S-ARCH-COMPETENCY-MODEL-design`'s ~11 output rows (`AGT-001` through `AGT-015`) ended up scattered inconsistently across all 3 tiers — some Now, some Next, one in Later — with no indication the split was deliberate, because each was filed in isolation at the moment it was found rather than cross-checked against its siblings.

### From Standing Rule — Backlog Capture, "the *number*, not just the prefix" (added 2026-07-28, `SES-18`)

Root cause this closes (found 2026-07-28): the claim step was documented *only* in the session-setup skill — a document read once at 8am while making a worktree — while this section, the one actually in front of a session at the moment it types an ID, described how to choose a prefix and said nothing about the number. Sessions that never re-read the setup skill at close-out had no instruction telling them to claim, and the single-ID claim shape made hand-counting the path of least resistance for the multi-row filings that are this repo's normal case (51 such commits in history, 7 in the two days before this was found). Three live collisions came out of that gap — `CHI-42` and `CHI-48` (two unrelated rows each), and `CHI-76`, where a session claimed *correctly* and still collided because another session had hand-minted 76 fifteen minutes earlier. `CHI-42`'s wrong ID reached shipped Supabase Skill content before anyone noticed.

### From Standing Rule — Backlog Capture, the `task_773e8b06` incident (added 2026-07-15, John's explicit call)

This is exactly what went wrong with `task_773e8b06`: never anchored to a durable ID at creation, so multiple sessions repeated "`task_773e8b06` is running separately, not blocking" as unverified fact for a full day, and the task's own session later failed to recognize a third-person mention of its own opaque ID as being about itself — see [[feedback-coordination-note-self-reference]]. A real ID at spawn time would have prevented both failure modes: sessions cite "blocked on `AA-191`," not "blocked on some session I have to go check on," and a session reading about its own backlog row doesn't have the same self-reference ambiguity a bare process ID does.

### From Step 4.6 Architect Review — "Re-run that grep against a fresh `origin/dev`" (added 2026-07-29, `SES-46`)

**Found live 2026-07-29 (`design-ses-33`):** that session measured the `SES-33` Vercel deploy stall, scoped a `scripts/check-deploy-freshness.js` gate, got John's approval, and wrote the full kickoff doc — then discovered on its pre-write rebase that `SES-015` had shipped `scripts/check-deploy-current.js` doing exactly that, already wired into `STANDARDS.md` §6 and the CHI runbook, in the ~2 hours between its scoping read and its kickoff write. The shipped version was also strictly better (ancestor test, not SHA equality — under concurrent sessions the deployed tip is normally *ahead* of the commit under test, so equality would fail constantly and the gate would be ignored within a day). Nothing was lost only because the rebase happened before the push; the whole session was wasted regardless.

### From Step 4.6 Architect Review — "Search by shape, not by name" (added 2026-07-21, `CHI-53`'s citation_missing fix)

This session first designed a fix for "Owen can't see the news article Marcus was given" by searching narrowly for content-propagation code (`task_context`, `delegate_to_agent`) — and missed that the same screen already had a fully-proven mechanism for tracking a related multi-call sequence and knowing when each stage completes: the Agent Routing drawer's own hop-numbering/event-building code (`buildHopEvent`/`onEvent`, `CHI-23`/`AA-164`), which the session had already read earlier in the same conversation for an unrelated reason and never connected back.

### From Step 4.6 Architect Review — "Multi-site bug pattern → shared-service check" (added 2026-07-16, `AA-192`)

**Concretely, this session first proposed changing a client-side helper's signature and reapplying that fix at 3 separate call sites (`DashboardScreen.jsx`, `PersonnelScreen.jsx`, `TeachScreen.jsx`) — all 3 shared one underlying route (`api/brief.js`) that was simply never migrated onto the shared `logActivity()` service everything else already uses.** Migrating the shared route once (root) collapsed 3 parallel per-site fixes into 1 route fix + trivial "delete the now-redundant client call" cleanups, and fixed a bigger co-located bug (wrong model logged, not just missing tokens) at the source instead of 3 times.

### From Step 4.6 Architect Review — "Secondary backlog IDs need a closure gate" (added 2026-07-28, `SES-32`)

**Found live 2026-07-28 (`design-log-60`):** `docs/kickoffs/v6.3.203-LOG-81-model-call-counting.md` said "also settles `LOG-60` (Observability)'s denominator question" in its Section 1 Feature line and nowhere else — no gate, no close-out step — while `LOG-60`'s own row, amended by that same design conversation, read "Close this row when `LOG-81`'s QA passes." Both halves of the hand-off existed in writing and neither pointed at an action, so `LOG-60` was on track to survive `LOG-81`'s close-out as a stale `❌ Missing` row describing already-shipped work. A gate was in fact available and unused — QA item 4 ("classified distinct + not yet classified = header Total Calls exactly") is literally `LOG-60`'s reconciliation question restated. It was caught only because John happened to open a session on `LOG-60` itself. Same close-out-leak family as `SES-27`, different mechanism: `SES-27` is one row's own scope outrunning its checkmark; this is a second row that no session's close-out owns.

### From Step 4.6 Architect Review — "Locked-section staleness check" (added 2026-07-02, `S-ARCH-AGENT-LOOP-02-design`)

Root cause this session: §19d's "Two delegation paths" paragraph (written by `S-ARCH-OWNERSHIP-02-design`) described a fast path as current and legitimate, but `CLAUDE-STATE.md`'s own session summary — already read at Step 1 of *this same session* — said that exact path was "eliminated entirely" by a later same-day session. The contradiction sat unreconciled until John caught the downstream mistake it caused.

The counter caught it cleanly; this worktree rebased onto that change before writing any kickoff doc, and every cited line number in all four kickoffs is post-rebase.

**a (v7.0.30, `f9bd2b0`, AgentNetwork.jsx):** Answer drawer capped `maxHeight={280} resizable` (was unbounded, grew past the canvas). Replaced LAV-5b's single-`litEdge` spotlight (exactly one edge lit/labeled at a time) with a pure per-edge fold (`edgeActivity()`) so every edge that carried real traffic this run stays solid + arrow-animated simultaneously in its own real meaning color while the run is live — John's own design, confirmed mid-session: "I want the lines to stay solid and arrow patterns going on all of them until the full loop is done — so the user sees 1 agent's loop requires all N amount of agents talking at once." Labels capped at the most-recent-2 (full opacity) + 3rd-most-recent (fading `.45`), older none. A delegation left genuinely unresolved at terminal now settles into its real Hand-off look immediately instead of sticking in the in-flight blue+arrow state forever (root cause: the settle effect only re-fired on new `runHops`, and a run's last hop is the last thing that ever arrives). **Coding session caught and fixed two real defects in this design's own kickoff spec, not scope creep:** (1) `pulsesForHop` emits a report-back as `target->dispatcher`, the reverse of the only key `sessionEdges` ever creates (`dispatcher>target`) — the kickoff's literal spec would have made `REPORT_COLOR` unreachable on any rendered line; fixed with a canonical (order-independent) pair key, `canonicalEdgeKey()`. (2) The settle effect's own `setVisuallyOpenKeys` state updater also writes `openSinceRef` as a side effect that React applies on the *next* render, after the settle loop already ran — so a key cleared on the terminal pass got silently re-added a moment later with nothing left to re-fire the effect. Fixed by gating the add-updater on `running`.

**b (v7.0.31, `5e736b1`, AgentNetwork.jsx):** `deriveNetwork()`'s delegation branch now pushes `secondaryAgentId` into `engaged` the instant a delegation names it, not only once the target produces its own credited hop — root cause of three related symptoms John reported as one item: a solid line pointing at a still-queued agent mid-run, a dashed line pointing at a still-queued agent post-run, and agents that never visibly "came forward." Deliberately diverges from `LiveAgentViewScreen.jsx`'s independent `agentsEngaged` meter, which stays scoped to "produced its own credited event" — John confirmed explicitly the two are allowed to disagree ("its ok with the split"): the canvas shows *addressed*, the counter shows *actually spoke*. Activity bubble (`net.bubbles[a.id]`) now gated on that agent's own pulsing state (`is-orch`/`is-assembly`/`is-active`) instead of the whole run merely being live — previously a finished agent's last line stayed visible for the rest of the run. Canvas spacing retuned as a first-pass numeric tuning (not a new control — confirmed with John, "just re-tune the spacing for now"): `ARC_RX`/`ARC_RY` 235/215 → 275/245, bench-stack step cap/span 52/468 → 58/520.

**Same-day patch (v7.0.33, `9398564`):** the LAV-9b coding session flagged, but deliberately did not silently fix, a real visual side effect of its own change: `done` was computed as `[...engaged, ...finished].filter(...)`, and since `engaged` now includes not-yet-spoken targets, a freshly-addressed agent fell into `done` and wore the finished-look moss border while still waiting its turn. Root-caused and patched same session: `deriveNetwork()` now tracks `selfEngaged` (the pre-LAV-9b narrower meaning — "has a hop really credited to its own id") separately from the now-broader `engaged`, and `done` tests `selfEngaged` instead. Verified live on the `upgrade-cycles` run below: Alex Reeves rendered on-canvas with no state class (plain resting card) rather than `is-done`.

**c (v7.0.32, `52d5521`, LiveAgentViewScreen.jsx):** removed the 3-second `setTimeout(() => setTerminal(null), 3000)` effect that silently reverted the mode badge from "Complete" to the same "Idle" look as a screen that had never run anything — `terminal` now only clears in `onRun()`, when the *next* question actually starts. Renamed `MODE_COPY.complete` from `"Complete"` to **`"Question Answered"`** (John's own wording, mid-session: "In this instance, i mean 'question completed'... perhaps the status is 'Question Answered'"), and widened the badge dot's `aiBlink` animation gate from `mode === "orch"` to `mode === "orch" || mode === "complete"` — John: "it pulses, so the user knows they can look at all the ending metrics all around the screen." Continuous pulse, not a one-time flourish, per John's explicit confirmation.

**QA — self-verified live on the deployed preview, `upgrade-cycles` and `south-korea-coop` runs, all 4 commits' builds clean, 4/4 Node suites passing (44 total assertions):**
- Answer drawer: confirmed `maxHeight: 280px`, `overflowY: auto`, real content `scrollHeight` (635px) exceeding `clientHeight` (280px) — genuinely scrollable.
- Mid-run: 3 edges observed simultaneously solid (no dash), each with a `<polygon>` arrow whose fill matched its own line color (2× `#5a7538` moss "Report back" at label opacities 1 and 0.45, 1× `#2d6fb5` blue in-flight Delegate with no label) — confirms the "all active, own color, recency-fading labels" mechanism directly in the DOM, not inferred.
- Bubble gating: `Eleanor Voss`/`Marcus Webb`/`Owen Marsh` all showed `bubbleShow: false` once `is-done`, while the currently-`is-active`/`is-orch` agent showed `bubbleShow: true`.
- Post-run (upgrade-cycles run, which itself hit the pre-existing `LOO-29` bug and errored — unrelated to this session, confirmed the Error badge renders red/non-pulsing, unchanged): 7 edges all settled — 4 green solid (no stuck blue, no lingering arrows), 3 dashed grey resting — and `Alex Reeves` rendered with no state class, confirming the same-day patch live.
- Status badge (south-korea-coop run, completed cleanly): "Question Answered" observed with `animationName: aiBlink`, color `rgb(90,117,56)` (`T.moss`), and **still present unchanged after 8+ seconds** — past the old 3-second bug window, with no reversion.
- Known limitation, documented rather than skipped: the in-app browser pane runs with `document.hidden = true`, so `requestAnimationFrame` (which drives the actual smooth motion of `Pulse`/`LoopingArrow`/the choreography tick loop) does not fire there — smooth-motion playback itself could not be watched frame-by-frame. Verification instead used DOM-state snapshots (computed styles, attribute values, class membership) at multiple points during and after live runs, which is sufficient to prove the underlying mechanism (color/label/class/animation-gate correctness) without depending on rAF. Canvas spacing (item 8) verified via code diff + the coding session's own report only — a full visual screenshot check was not possible in this environment; flagged as a first-pass tuning per the kickoff's own allowance, not a blocking gap.

**Open, not part of this round:** `LAV-10` (Post-beta, ❌ Missing) — orchestration-mode showcase visual (radial-burst offshoot cluster + one-time particle/glow trigger, John's "jackpot" framing), split out mid-session because it needs its own motion/timing design pass, not a kickoff-doc-ready fix. Full detail `docs/harvests/LAV-9.md`.

## S-LAV-10-design/S-LAV-10 (v7.0.35, 2026-08-01, design-lav-10-0801)
LAV-10 (UI, Post-beta): closes the item split out of `LAV-9` — an "orchestration mode" showcase moment, John's own "jackpot" framing. Settled quickly in a short follow-on design conversation (one question, one answer, "go") rather than a long back-and-forth, because the prior session's harvest note had already narrowed it to a concept in principle.

**Design decisions, in order:** John's first framing was a spatial "offshoot" — the orchestrator + delegates pulling into their own cluster away from the rest of the roster. The design session proposed that OR a louder in-place treatment and asked which; John chose in-place, then reframed the effect himself: "perhaps the canvas flashes as soon as orchestration is known and all the contributors have a flash until their own." The design session proposed the concrete mechanism from that framing — a rising-edge trigger (not level, not a fixed per-hop event), a canvas-wide flash immediately, then a staggered per-contributor cascade ~150ms later reusing the SAME meaning-color `is-orch` already carries (`ACTION_TEXT_COLORS_FETCH.CLICK`) rather than inventing a new one — and John confirmed with "I like it" before the kickoff was written.

**What shipped, `AgentNetwork.jsx` only, 2 tasks:**
1. Rising-edge detection on `deriveNetwork()`'s existing `orchestrators` set: a `knownOrchestratorsRef` tracks every id already seen orchestrating this run; anyone newly present fires the burst, anyone still present (continuing to orchestrate) does not. Resets on the same runHops-length-shrink signal every other run-scoped ledger in this file already uses for "a new question started." Contributors = the new orchestrator + whichever currently-`engaged` agents aren't it — reusing `computeTargets()`'s own "everyone engaged except the lead is one arc" notion rather than inventing a parallel grouping concept.
2. Two CSS layers: `.lav-orch-flash` (a radial-gradient wash across just the canvas, clipped to `.lav-inner` so it never covers the Answer drawer/legend/toggle sitting outside it) and `.lav-node.is-orch-burst .lav-ring` (a brighter/faster one-shot ripple than `is-active`'s continuous `lavRipple`), with each contributor's own `animationDelay` computed from its cascade index (`150 + idx×100`ms) — additive to whatever other state class (`is-active`/`is-orch`/`is-assembly`) that card already carries.

**Coding-session-caught defect in the design's own kickoff spec (not a coding mistake):** Task 2a's exact-code diff included a CSS comment, inside `NET_CSS` (a JS template literal), that used backticks — which terminate a JS template string mid-file and would have broken the build if pasted verbatim. The coding session caught this before committing, rewrote the comment backtick-free, and flagged it explicitly in its report rather than silently patching around it. Root cause: writing "exact code spec" prose inside a kickoff doc's own markdown code fence doesn't syntax-check against the file it's destined for — worth a beat of caution the next time a kickoff spec touches a template-literal CSS block specifically.

**QA — self-verified live, not inferred from code, using the same rAF-blind-spot workaround `LAV-9` established:** since `requestAnimationFrame`-driven motion can't be watched frame-by-frame in this environment (`document.hidden` in the browser pane), a `MutationObserver` was installed on `.lav-inner` before running a real `upgrade-cycles` question, watching for `.lav-orch-flash` add/remove and `is-orch-burst` class add/remove with each `.lav-ring`'s own `animationDelay`. Captured 3 genuine orchestration transitions across one run:
- Owen Marsh → contributors [Owen 150ms, Eleanor Voss 250ms, Marcus Webb 350ms, Michelle Manning 450ms]
- Marcus Webb (a former contributor, now newly the orchestrator) → [Marcus 150ms, Eleanor 250ms, Owen 350ms, Michelle 450ms]
- Michelle Manning → [Michelle 150ms, Eleanor 250ms, Marcus 350ms, Owen 450ms, **Alex Reeves 550ms** — a newly-arrived 5th agent correctly picked up mid-run]

Every delay matched the `150 + index×100` formula exactly, every time; the canvas flash's add/remove events landed in the same tick as each cascade's start/end; and critically, no burst fired for an orchestrator that was merely continuing to hold its delegation (only genuinely NEW ones). One observed artifact, not a defect: total on-screen duration ran longer than the JS constants alone predict (~1.5s observed vs. ~1.05s calculated for a 4-contributor burst) — consistent with `setTimeout` throttling in a backgrounded/hidden browser tab, the same class of environment limitation as the rAF gap, not a bug in the delay arithmetic itself (which is computed synchronously and was independently confirmed correct).

## S-LAV-12-design/S-LAV-12 (v7.0.40, 2026-08-01, design-lav-canvas-0801)
LAV-12 (UI, Post-beta): 4-item follow-up from John's live review of the deployed canvas (a pasted screenshot showing agent cards rendering under the prompt box/legend and a dotted line reaching into the queue), worked one item at a time.

**Item 1 — chrome collision.** Root-caused by reading the actual layout code: the legend/toggle (`right:12,top:12`) and the prompt box (`right:314,bottom:8`) are both positioned in real screen pixels, entirely outside `AgentNetwork.jsx`'s own 1200×640 coordinate space — and the bench/queue column is *also* anchored to that space's right edge, so all three collide by construction. John asked directly whether the fix would shrink the canvas; the honest answer (given before he committed) was no, the canvas stays the same size, but the *usable area for card centers* shrinks and trades against `LAV-9b`'s own spacing work — he accepted that explicitly ("go with it"). Fix: a static reserved vertical band (`TOP_SAFE_Y`/`BOTTOM_SAFE_Y`), not runtime DOM measurement — confirmed as the simpler, non-drifting choice over precisely tracking the chrome's actual rect. `ARC_RY` narrowed `245`→`215` (the arc's real vertical swing had reached `y=60`, inside the legend's band); bench-stack span `520`→`430` (had reached `y=565`, inside the prompt box's band); `homeLayout()`'s own grid already fit unchanged (~102-538), verified and stated in a comment rather than left for a future session to re-derive.

**Item 2 — remove the agent code.** Simple in the kickoff; the coding session found the kickoff's own scope had missed a third render site (`MOB-4b`'s mobile Bench view, mobile's *default* view, `.lav-mcode`) and fixed it live against the kickoff's own QA item rather than shipping a fix that would have failed its own acceptance test.

**Item 3 — always-label an active line.** John: "I still noticed a lot of the trace lines not showing their legend name — can we just make sure everytime a line is active it shows its name?" Root cause: `LAV-9a` made every active-this-run edge animate simultaneously but still capped LABELS to a recency-ranked top-3 — so once a busy run had 4+ real edges, most of the visibly-moving lines went silent. One-line fix: `labelOpacity = running ? 1 : labelOpacityForRank(rank)` — the recency fade still governs the settled view after a run ends (nothing to prioritize by once nothing's "active"), it just no longer throttles the live view.

**Item 4 — edges persisting across questions, read as "agents hiding in the queue."** John's original report matched a screenshot of a run only 7 seconds in — too early for cross-question staleness to be a live explanation, so this was investigated for real rather than assumed: a `MutationObserver`-based check on a single fresh run (82 samples over 2+ minutes, matching every rendered line's actual screen endpoint against every card's actual screen position via `getScreenCTM()`) found zero within-a-run violations, proving `LAV-9b`'s promotion mechanism was never the bug. Reading `LiveAgentViewScreen.jsx` directly then found the real mechanism: `hops` (fed to `sessionEdges()`, "edges persist across runs" per `AgentNetwork.jsx`'s own JSDoc, a `LAV-1b`/`1c`-era deliberate choice) is the whole-session ledger, only reset when the harness hook's own event stream goes empty — while `runHops` (everything else: nodes, bubbles, pulses, the `LAV-10` burst) is correctly reset at every `question_boundary`. A line from question A survives into question B's render even though question B's own node/queue state has already moved on. John confirmed: reset edges too, since every other run-scoped mechanism already does. Fix is a caller-side prop change only, both `<AgentNetwork>` call sites now pass `hops={canvasRunHops}` instead of the whole-session `canvasHops` — `sessionEdges()`/`deriveNetwork()` untouched.

**Coding session's own deviation, caught and fixed rather than shipped as-is:** the kickoff's Section 8 test draft hardcoded the safe-zone bound values (`215`/`430`) as literals in its own assertions — a vacuous test that would pass identically whether or not the real source was ever touched. The shipped test instead extracts the real constants/expressions from the source text and adds negative controls proving the OLD (pre-fix) values genuinely violate the band; run against the pre-fix file it failed 3 real assertions, confirming the test discriminates.

**QA.** Self-verified live on the deployed preview immediately after the coding session's report: confirmed 0 `.lav-code`/`.lav-mcode` elements anywhere on a live run (item 2); confirmed active-edge labels at `opacity:1` while running, for edges the pre-`LAV-12` code would have faded/hidden (item 3, matches the source diff exactly); re-ran the same `MutationObserver` line-to-benched-card check from the original diagnosis and found zero violations again post-fix (item 4's within-run half). **One check not completed:** the live cross-question re-verification (question A's line vanishing once question B starts) — three separate attempts across two tabs all hit unusually long-running demo questions (`south-korea-coop`'s own guardrail-retry behavior, `CHI-98`, plausibly compounding; `training-turnover-benchmark` also ran far past its normal duration in the same window) and none reached a second question within this session's testing budget. Not treated as a silent pass: the mechanism itself is a simple caller-side substitution onto a variable (`runHops`/`canvasRunHops`) that is *already* proven correctly scoped per question by every other piece of this canvas, and the Node test's case E exercises the exact reset scenario (a real `question_boundary`, a stale edge from before it, a real edge after it) end to end. Accepted on that combined evidence — code diff + a discriminating Node test + live confirmation of the within-run mechanism the fix reuses — documented explicitly as the one item not re-observed live, per STANDARDS.md Section 5b's "accept on indirect evidence only where genuinely unreachable, documented explicitly."

## S-LAV-14-design/S-LAV-14 (v7.0.47, 2026-08-02, design-lav-console-0802)
LAV-14 (UI, Post-beta): small, single-item rename request — nav label "Live Agent View" → "Live Agent Console" (desktop Work dropdown + mobile `NAV_GROUPS`, both call sites), and the screen's own `PAGE_TITLE` constant from "Live Multi-Agent Routing" → "Live Multi-Agent Console".

**Factual check before scoping, not after.** John's original ask described the current screen title as "Live Multi-Agent View" — a fresh grep found the real current value is "Live Multi-Agent Routing." Rather than silently "correct" his wording or blindly implement a string that doesn't exist, this was surfaced directly and confirmed: he'd conflated the nav label's old wording ("View") with the screen's actual middle word ("Routing"), and confirmed the intended change is "Routing" → "Console." Same discipline as `LAV-9`'s "is that the right merge?" checks — cheap to ask, expensive to guess wrong on a string that becomes canonical.

**Scope discipline:** grepped the full repo for every occurrence of both old strings before writing the kickoff — exactly three live-UI occurrences (two nav `label:` call sites in `AppShell.jsx`, one `PAGE_TITLE` in `LiveAgentViewScreen.jsx`), no `<title>`/document-title reference, and two historical mock/doc HTML files correctly left out of scope. `AppShell.jsx`'s own comment already documented that the nav label and screen title were deliberately kept as two different strings by an earlier John call ("dual naming... do not unify") — this rename preserves that duality (both strings change, they still don't match each other), not undoes it. Kickoff explicitly listed every internal identifier (`FOCUS_AREA_STATUS.liveAgentView`, `isLAV`, the `/live-agent-view` route, file names) that must NOT be touched, to head off an unrequested identifier-rename refactor.

**Coding session (Sonnet 5, mechanical tier per the model-naming rule) caught a real bug in the kickoff's own Section 8 test:** the draft's negative-check asserted the old label string was gone from the *entire file*, which false-fails against `AppShell.jsx`'s own line-1 header comment (which legitimately still says "Live Agent View" — it's the mechanism's historical name, explicitly in the kickoff's own do-not-touch list). Narrowed the assertion to the actual `label:` call sites instead of the whole file, and separately updated one adjacent doc comment that quoted the now-stale old screen title as documentation for the dual-naming point — a genuine drift-prevention catch, not scope creep.

**QA.** Screen title confirmed live verbatim ("Live Multi-Agent Console (Beta)"). The nav dropdown itself could not be visually confirmed this session: the browser pane kept rendering the mobile LAV composition (Canvas/Answer tabs, Single/Bench toggle) regardless of the desktop viewport preset requested, and one direct check read `window.innerWidth` back as `0` — a pane-level compositing quirk consistent with earlier-documented limitations in this environment (the `document.hidden`/rAF gap from `LAV-9`/`LAV-10`), not a sign of a real bug. Accepted on the source diff (`git show` confirmed both `label:` call sites read "Live Agent Console" verbatim, byte-identical otherwise) plus the coding session's corrected, non-vacuous test — documented explicitly as the one item not re-observed live rather than silently marked done.

## 2026-08-02 — S-LAV-15-design / S-LAV-15 (v7.0.49) — `Run Tasks` drawer on the Agent Console

**Worktree:** `design-lav-15-0802` (design branch, switched to `session/lav-15-run-tasks-coding` for the code step). **Commits:** `2fe10ec` (path correction), `a0867d1` (build), close-out following.

### The session had no design work to do

John opened with "design lav-15." The kickoff doc already existed and had been respecced by him earlier the same day (`8c5a576`). Rather than re-designing, the session verified that premise fresh and said so: all six kickoff-referenced files present, `origin/dev` unmoved, no `RunTasks` anywhere in `src/` on `origin/dev`, and `dev_version_counter` sitting at `7.0.49` claimed by `design-scaling-arch-0731` — the very session that wrote the doc, so no collision. John's answer was "build it."

**Process note worth keeping:** "build it" reversed a decision recorded *in the kickoff itself* — that doc said "John runs this session himself … the manual path applies." Two lines (the CONTEXT paragraph and the Manual QA Checklist heading) would have told the spawned coding agent that a human owned its QA. Both were corrected to the automated-loop path *before* spawning, and the `FEATURES.md` session cell with them. A stale process instruction inside a kickoff doc is read by the agent as authoritative; correcting it is part of flipping the path, not bookkeeping to do afterward.

### Transient API failure mid-build — resumed, not restarted

The first `Agent` spawn died after ~6 minutes and 16 tool uses with `ENOTFOUND` — a network failure, not a task failure. Before deciding, the session checked disk rather than assuming: clean working tree, zero commits ahead of `origin/dev`, no `RunTasks.jsx`. Nothing had persisted, so `SendMessage` resumed the same agent from its transcript, preserving ~118K tokens of orientation reads instead of paying for them twice. The resumed run completed normally. Worth repeating: **check the worktree before choosing resume-vs-restart** — the two look identical from the notification alone, and a resume onto half-written files would be the bad case.

### QA — all 5 items PASS, verified live

Deploy gate confirmed dev serving `a0867d1` before anything was trusted (`scripts/check-deploy-current.js`, per the standing Vercel-quota hazard). Screenshots were unavailable — the browser pane never composites frames (`document.hidden` is permanently true) — so verification ran on DOM text and computed geometry, which is the sharper instrument anyway. The `LAV-14` viewport quirk did **not** recur: `window.innerWidth` read a true 1600.

- **Placement/geometry:** `.lav-leftstack` at left 12, width 280, bottom **822**; trace console (`.lavc`) top **828** — the 6px stage-floor gap, confirming the drawer expands to the trace console top as specced. Title is literally `Run Tasks` in the DOM with CSS `text-transform: uppercase`, the identical treatment `Answer` gets.
- **Live run** (`training-turnover-benchmark`): 18 entries, contiguously numbered 18→1 newest-first, Asked/Did/Content on three lines, time signatures in the `arrived M:SS into the run · took Ns` form, **no summary entry**, feed persisted after the run button re-enabled.
- **Guardrail demo** (`south-korea-coop`): feed reset 18→4 on the new run, gate entry carried the blocked-verdict wording, and `LAV-11`'s `Answer: Agent guardrail catch` drawer title was unaffected.
- **Facts cross-checked, not trusted:** `eleanor · the_library · 10 chunks`, `michelle · roster · 22 chunks`, `michelle · knowledge · 4 chunks` and both delegation strings all appear verbatim in the raw trace console for the same run; all five agent name/role pairs (Michelle Manning — Project Manager, Marcus Webb — GEO CSO Expert, Owen Marsh — The Proofreader, Eleanor Voss — The Librarian, Alex Reeves — Screen Controls Editor) match `src/data/agents.js` exactly. No invented numbers or names.

### The finding that mattered: a completion report's own enumeration was wrong

The kickoff asked the coding session to enumerate missing stream fields so an enrichment ticket could be filed. It produced 8, each presented as freshly verified against named source lines. Live QA **disproved 3 of them**: delegation `reasoning` renders (Michelle's pick rationale appears in full on entry 16), PM-brokered hand-offs *do* carry a rich `task_description` (entry 12), and `assembly_work_complete` is emphatically not inert — it fires live and drives 8 of the 18 entries. Three others (gate per-criterion scores, `qa_answer` headline, citation source) were confirmed real and are what `LAV-17` actually scopes.

Nothing shipped wrong — the feature is *better* than its own report claimed. The lesson is narrower and worth stating: **a completion report's negative claims ("field X is absent") are exactly the ones live QA is positioned to falsify, and scoping a follow-up ticket off an unverified list would have sent a future session hunting for gaps that don't exist.** `LAV-17` therefore carries an explicit caution to re-measure. Same family as `feedback-interrogate-the-metric` — a correct-looking report supporting a wrong conclusion.

### Follow-ups filed

## 2026-08-02 — S-LAV-16-design / S-LAV-16 (v7.0.50) — Console Boot Dial

**Worktree:** `design-lav-boot-dial-0802` (design branch, switched to `session/lav-16-boot-dial-coding` for the code step). **Commits:** `9700306` (build), `1574a25` (exit-fade patch), close-out following.

### Discovery corrected the premise before any code was written

John's opening ask assumed a "first agent node appears" event existed and asked discovery to confirm which one. Reading `AgentNetwork.jsx` directly disproved the premise: every roster agent renders a `.lav-node` card unconditionally from first paint — there is no event that creates a node. What actually happens is a real, already-named mechanism: **"Choreographed" mode** (a toggle, default on) holds unengaged agents in a **bench queue** and promotes the first engaged agent to the **`LEAD`** choreography slot the instant `net.engaged` gets its first entry (`deriveNetwork()`, `AgentNetwork.jsx:303-313`/`:477-479`) — set by the first `runHops` entry carrying *any* `agentId`, not specifically a `delegation`-typed one. When John was later asked to resolve the one open design call, his own phrasing — "as soon as an agent's avatar appears on the choreograph screen from the queue" — matched this exact mechanism verbatim, confirming the corrected trigger rather than requiring a re-explanation.

Also found live: this is not a new problem. `LiveAgentViewScreen.jsx:1-3` records `LAV-13` (v7.0.41) shipping a pulsing status badge as a stopgap for the identical dead-window complaint John had already hit once before.

### Kickoff scope, verified rather than assumed

The screen already exposed everything the fix needed — `canvasRunHops`, `running`, `awaiting` — so the kickoff specified a single pure derivation (`deriveBooting()`) with an explicit hard rule against any new state/ref/effect. Before finalizing scope, checked the mobile-only rendering branch (`AgentNetwork.jsx` ~L1355) that discovery had initially flagged as unverified: it shares the exact same `.lav-stagewrap` wrapper class as the desktop branch, so one mount point works unmodified on both layouts — turning what could have been a separate `MOB`-prefixed follow-up into a zero-cost inclusion in the same session.

### Build caught a real spec gap; patched same session rather than shipping it broken

The coding session's own completion report flagged, unprompted, that the kickoff's literal `{booting && <ConsoleBootDial/>}` mount expression (John's own requested seam — "one boolean, no new state machine") gives React no exit transition: a conditionally-rendered child is removed from the DOM instantly, with no chance for the approved "~250ms fade out" to play. Rather than accept a silently-broken piece of an already-approved behavior spec, this was fixed as an immediate same-session follow-up: `useLingeringMount(booting, 250)` keeps the dial mounted ~250ms past `booting` going false, with a `leaving` prop driving a CSS opacity transition (no new keyframe, consistent with the "no new global keyframes" constraint even at the patch level).

### QA — all 5 items PASS, verified live

Deploy gate confirmed dev serving `1574a25` before anything was trusted. This session's browser pane runs `document.hidden: true` (confirmed directly), so the rAF-driven numeral and the CSS `fadeIn` opacity both read frozen at their initial values throughout — the same documented `reference-chi-live-qa-input` limitation, not a regression; verified by checking `document.hidden` directly rather than assuming from the frozen readouts alone. React's `<select>` also silently ignored `form_input`'s native value-set (DOM value changed, React's internal `onChange` never fired) until the same value-tracker-reset + dispatched `change` event technique that memo already documents for chat inputs was applied — worth folding into that reference for future `<select>`-driven QA.

Given animation playback was unobservable in this environment, the mount/unmount *timing* was verified independently of it — through DOM presence, not visual animation — via a single atomic in-page JS polling script (avoiding the round-trip latency that made naive step-by-step `javascript_tool` calls miss the boot window entirely on the first two attempts):

- **Mount:** `.lav-bootdial` present at the first 100ms poll tick (~117ms after the click), `position:absolute`, `inset:0`, `z-index:40`, parented inside `.lav-stagewrap` — above the node range (2-9) and `.lav-orch-flash` (10) as specced.
- **Unmount trigger:** the dial's `leaving` class began at the *exact same* 100ms sample as the first `.lav-node.is-active`/`.is-orch`/`.is-assembly` appearing (both at t=1000ms in one captured run) — direct proof the dismissal fires on the corrected trigger, not a delegation-only subset of it.
- **Lingering-exit timing:** the dial actually left the DOM ~230ms after `leaving` began (target 250ms; the gap is explained by the poll's own 100ms granularity, not a timing defect).
- **Caption:** showed the run's real live status text (`"Marcus is thinking…"`, sourced from `useHarnessStream`'s own `writeStatus` call) rather than invented copy, on both desktop and mobile.
- **Mobile (375×812):** identical mount point, z-index, and caption behavior confirmed on both the Single and Bench views — no separate code path needed, matching the desktop/mobile parity finding above.
- **Reduced motion:** the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule (`animation-duration:14s` on the sweep, `animation:none` on the breathing scale) confirmed present in the deployed component's own `<style>` tag — accepted as indirect evidence since a live OS-level toggle wasn't reachable from this environment, same allowance the kickoff's own checklist named in advance.

No follow-up backlog rows filed — everything discovery corrected or QA found was resolved inside this same session, not deferred.

## 2026-08-02 — S-LAV-20/MOB-11-design / S-LAV-20/MOB-11 (v7.0.52) — 3-chip legend, post-run trace settle, always-named lines, mobile bench pulse

**Worktree:** `design-lav-postrun-edges-0802` (design branch, switched to `session/lav-20-legend-trace-coding` for the code step). **Commits:** `2be2318` (kickoff), `8a449c7` (build), close-out following.

### The walkthrough that produced the decisions

John opened with two post-run canvas observations: lines keep their last solid colours after "Question Answered" (he expected settled dashed communication-trace lines), and some solid lines — especially blue ones — carry no legend name. Diagnosis against source showed **both were `LAV-9`-done's deliberate design**, not bugs: "the colours stay, because what those lines carried is still true after the run," plus the words-are-scarcer-than-lines rank rule (2 full labels, 3rd fading, older invisible — and since delegations happen early in a run, blue lines almost always ranked past the cutoff, which is exactly why "especially the blue ones").

A first proposed settled view (dashed + meaning colour + all names) got a flat "no," which led to the productive step: **walking through all six legend elements' actual trigger conditions.** That walkthrough surfaced the real state of the vocabulary — **Link has been effectively dead since `LAV-12`-done** made edges run-scoped (a line now only exists because a delegation crossed it this run, so it is born wearing a meaning colour and the at-rest dashed style has nothing to attach to); Hand-off needs a delegation unreturned at terminal (nearly extinct in healthy runs); Iterate (né Re-dispatch) needs a repeated pair; Assembly is a card ring, not a line. That explained John's "all I ever see is two," and his calls followed directly: **3-chip legend (Delegate / Result / Iterate — his renames), every solid line named while running, and the dashed tan trace at terminal** — which is precisely the dead Link style getting its job back.

### Build

One file (`AgentNetwork.jsx`, +173/−105), Opus 5, clean run. Notable implementation choices from the coding session, all accepted: the desktop legend row now *iterates* `EDGE_MEANING_LABEL` instead of hand-listing chips (legend and line words agree by construction); both render paths share a new pure `edgeRenderStyle()` instead of two hand-parallel expression blocks; `sessionEdges()` dropped its now-meaningless `runHops`/`running` params; `HANDOFF_COLOR`, `ASSEMBLY_LEGEND_LABEL`, `labelOpacityForRank`/`LABEL_*_COUNT` and the `.sw-ring` rules deleted rather than left as dead exports. `MOB-11`: three component-scoped `lavMobBreath*` keyframes animate the existing `.lav-mava` glow (no new DOM, nothing in `tokens.js`), 1.1s active/assembly matching `lavRipple`'s own cadence, 2.4s orch; static glows kept as baseline; `prefers-reduced-motion` disables all three. Node test 46 assertions with the negative control **pinned to the pre-push dev tip** (`3454657`) — an unpinned control would have passed both ways once dev contained the change; against that base it fails 22.

### QA — all items PASS, verified live (deploy gate `8a449c7`)

- **Legend:** exactly `Delegate / Result / Iterate` on desktop; mobile legend showed the renamed words and never the removed chips.
- **During-run words:** a real `training-turnover-benchmark` run showed "Delegate" and "Result" on solid lines; zero genuinely-unlabeled solid edges (entries my sampler first flagged all had `stroke: none` — pulse-dot paths over-matched by the selector, not lines). "Iterate" did not occur live (no repeat pair that run) — accepted on the Node test's fixture, per the kickoff's own allowance.
- **Settle:** at "Question Answered," all 5 desktop edges and both mobile Bench edges read `stroke #c8bb9a` (verified = `T.line`), dash `2 7`, width 1.6, no words, no arrows.
- **Mobile pulse:** at 375×812, `getComputedStyle().animationName` (the computed value this pane reads reliably) returned `lavMobBreathActive`/`lavMobBreathAssembly`/`lavMobBreathOrch` on the three live states and `none` on done/resting; no live node remained post-run.
- **Environment artifacts, not defects:** frozen pulse dots during scripted QA (`Pulse` completes via rAF, which never fires in the hidden pane; a real user's pulses complete in 900ms, and a backgrounded tab's jump straight to done on return); the hidden pane also throttled my first `setInterval` sampler to ~1/30s — direct state queries after terminal were the reliable instrument.

### Residue and adjacent closures

- **`MOB-12` (UI, Post-beta) filed:** the mobile Single view's two-card connector keeps its last meaning colour/word after the run (observed live: green "Result") — deliberately out of this kickoff's scope (it is `activeHandoff`'s spotlight composition, not a `sessionEdges` line). Whether it should adopt the trace treatment is John's UI call.
- **`MOB-5` (Tech Debt) structurally closed:** its premise was 6 possible legend meanings against a 402px row that fits 3. The vocabulary is now exactly 3 by construction, so the wrap is impossible. Honoured the original row's "don't close by truncating/scrolling" — the vocabulary shrank for John's own legend reasons.
- `STYLE-GUIDE.md` §41's routing-line bullet rewritten (it still described the pre-`LAV-9` single-lit-line model — two generations stale); §42's known-limitation updated; `BETA-TRIAGE.md`'s `MOB-5` row annotated.

## S-HAR-33-design + S-HAR-33a (v7.0.76) + S-HAR-33b (v7.0.77) — 2026-08-08 — IP Access Gate

**`HAR-33` (Feature, Beta-gate live-URL protection) ✅ Done + archived.** John's ask, verbatim goal: the site is live on `main`, the URL is about to circulate, API credits auto-reload — stop abuse ("block a US IP after $5, block all foreign IPs, popup with a friendly message"). Design settled conversationally: everything keys off the existing `ip_org_cache` table (John's call, adopted over a separate whitelist table — one row per IP, `country` already present); `permission` blocked/trial/unlimited (John named the set — trial scales to multi-tenant later); cap crossing WRITES the block; `user_label` for multi-IP users; spend computed, never stored.

**Mechanism.** `middleware.js` (Vercel Edge Middleware, matcher `/api/:path*`, NOT one of the 12 serverless functions): OPTIONS + `GET agent-configs`/`load-entries` pass ungated (browse stays open while blocked, John's vision); `x-db-gate-bypass` = `GATE_BYPASS_SECRET` env exempts QA tooling; IP derived byte-identically to `lib/request-context.js` so gate and log agree; unlimited→pass, blocked→403 (stored `spend_cap` re-fetches stats per PATCH-1 so the popup always has its tiles — fail-CLOSED if that RPC breaks), trial→geo check (non-US → write `blocked/geo`) then `get_ip_stats()` vs `spend_limit_usd` (≥ → write `blocked/spend_cap`, refuse with stats). Infra errors on the un-decided path fail OPEN (cost protection must never be an outage). Refusal contract: 403 `{deepbench_gate, reason, ip, stats?}` → `src/lib/gate-intercept.js` (idempotent fetch wrapper, original Response untouched) → `AccessGateModal.jsx` (Treasury tokens, superuser/private-beta variants, ✕+"Keep browsing"+Esc, NO email anywhere — John: true users know how to reach him). Data: migration `har_33_ip_access_gate` (6 `ip_org_cache` columns, `model_pricing` seeded from `COST_PER_1K_*`, `get_ip_stats()` with cache-token multipliers 1.25×/0.10×, `ip_spend_report` view, partial index on `ai_activity_log(caller_ip)`; every new object denied to anon — verified both directions).

**QA.** Backend 33/33 live incl. an A/B proof (31/33 against the pre-PATCH-1 deploy, only the new assertions failing). Design-session QA: real agent run on the dev preview from this machine's genuinely-over-cap IP (trial, $6.28 real spend) → gate refused before any model call (0 hops, $0), real popup with real stats (804 calls / 5,165,854 tokens / $6.28 / IP chip), dismiss→browse→re-fire all pass, row written `blocked/spend_cap` then restored; separate unlimited-row pass proven with a real logged embedding call (path-taken: row in `ai_activity_log` with this IP). Anon-key probes: PATCH/DELETE/rpc/view/pricing all denied, legit projections + client-logging INSERT still work.

**`DAT-18` (Data, Beta-gate) — found live, OPEN.** The anon key (in every visitor's bundle) held table-level INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on ALL 32 public tables, RLS off everywhere — remote wipe/rewrite of `skill_profiles`, `agents`, `the_library`, counters, all of it. Locked down this session (migration `har_33_gate_table_write_lockdown`): `ip_org_cache` all writes revoked; `ai_activity_log` append-only (client INSERT kept, non-negative-token check closes forged-negative-row spend deflation). Full pre-lockdown snapshot: `deepbench-backups/2026-08-08-1110` (56,393 rows, 0 failures). Remaining 30 tables need survey-then-revoke — a blind mass-revoke could break legitimate browser writes.

**Runbook impact:** any live-QA/regression call from a non-`unlimited` IP without the `x-db-gate-bypass` header now 403s. Get the secret via `vercel env pull` (set on production/preview/development 2026-08-08). Bucket-1 runs: add the header to the driver or ensure John's IP row is `unlimited` first.

**Filed:** `HAR-34` (Observability, Post-beta — push alerting on new blocks; no email service exists in the stack), `HAR-35` (Tech Debt, Post-beta — `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on `/api/*`, mitigated by the gate), `HAR-36` (Architecture, Post-beta — cookie-carried per-user permission; visitor_id is spoofable-by-design + anon-readable, so it must not unlock spend without its own auth design).

## 2026-08-08 — design-dat-18 / S-DAT-18 (v7.0.78) — Anon-key write-grant lockdown (28 tables)

**`DAT-18` (Data, Beta-gate live-URL protection) ✅ Done + archived.** Closes the platform-wide half of the exposure `S-HAR-33-design` found: the anon key (in every visitor's bundle) held full table-level write privileges on 29 of 32 tables, RLS off.

**Survey (the ticket's own open question, answered live in code + `information_schema`):** the browser legitimately writes exactly two tables — `tasks` (INSERT `CreateWorkOrderScreen` ~L533; UPDATE `AnalyzerContext` ~L302 + `TaskInstructionsScreen` ~L404/480/717) and `ai_activity_log` (logging INSERT, locked prior session). `pending_confirmations` — the row's named suspect — is server-side only. One non-browser surprise: `scripts/platform-stats.js` (Vercel `prebuild`, every build) PATCHed `platform_stats` with the **anon** key; in `--soft` mode a 403 would have silently killed stats refresh with zero build failure.

**Shipped (1 code file + migration `dat18_anon_write_revoke`):** all writes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER) revoked from `anon`+`authenticated` on 28 tables; `tasks` reduced to INSERT+UPDATE; `platform-stats.js` prefers `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY` (anon fallback kept for keyless soft runs); `alter default privileges for role postgres … revoke … on tables` closes the auto-grant hole for future tables (fail closed — a new browser-written table must carry its grant in its own migration; rule updated in `.claude/rules/supabase-column-grants.md`). Untouched by design: every SELECT grant, `ai_activity_log`, `ip_org_cache`, `model_pricing`, sequences, RPCs, RLS.

**QA (self-verified, deploy gate `d668f46` LIVE):** grant matrix asserted as a computed diff (0 mismatches, both roles, 32/32 tables); denials are real permission checks (401/`42501` on `skill_profiles` INSERT, `the_library` DELETE, `agents` UPDATE); kept paths proven with the real anon key (tasks INSERT 201 → UPDATE 204 → service-key cleanup 204); reads intact (`select=*` + `ai_activity_log` column-list); CHI renders with full data, console clean; `/api/load-entries` 200 (service-key route path); Vercel prebuild's service-key write proven on the real post-push build (`platform_stats.updated_at` 18:23:06 UTC, inside the `d668f46` build window, after the coding session's last local write). Snapshot first: `deepbench-backups/2026-08-08-1318` (32 tables, 56,556 rows).

**Coding-session findings (Opus 5, automated loop — all three verified by the design session):**
1. **Kickoff test-fixture bug:** `tasks.id` is `integer`, not uuid — the spec'd nonexistent-UUID DELETE probe 400'd (`22P02`) before the permission check, a non-discriminating assert (`feedback-qa-assertion-must-discriminate` class). Coding swapped to `id=eq.-1`, which genuinely reaches the grant check. Design-session lesson: type-check probe fixtures against the actual column, same as any other schema fact.
2. **PG17 `MAINTAIN` residue** → `DAT-20` (also covers the unalterable `supabase_admin` default ACL). Invisible to `role_table_grants` — the complete grant surface needs `pg_class.relacl`/`pg_default_acl`.
3. **Backup tooling's schema capture silently broken since ~2026-08-08** (`_backup_schema_ddl` 404, no `schema.sql`/`migrations.sql`, fails soft; grants captured in no form) → `DAT-21`. The only record of the pre-migration grant state is the coding session's baseline matrix in its transcript.

**Process note:** worktree `design-dat-18`, branches `session/design-dat-18` → `session/dat-18-coding`. Kickoff push hit two concurrent-dev races (SH-24's close-out + coding push) — both resolved by the standard keep-both-bullets rebase + one retry. ID claims: `DAT` block of 1 (`DAT-19`), then block of 2 (`DAT-20`/`DAT-21`). Backlog sweep: DAT-18 archived; DAT-19/20/21 filed (all Post-beta); `DAT-9`'s row updated (write half closed, read-policy scope remains); §19t and the grants rule file updated to the shipped posture.

## 2026-08-10 — audit-pattern-coverage-0810 / S-LOG-137 (v7.0.89) — Function Calling enumeration put to Susan; she declined to widen

**Origin:** John asked a measurement question — would Susan recognize more patterns if the vocabulary were updated, or does recent activity already reduce to known patterns? Answering it required scoping the question correctly first, and two of the three candidate answers dissolved on inspection.

**The measurement (14 days, live):** 16,424 rows → **13,808 AI calls** (name a model) → 6,793 classified (49.2%) / 7,015 unclassified. The raw 758 distinct unclassified signatures is **not** 758 patterns — signatures carry `retrieved_chunk_ids`/`assembled_skill_slugs`, so cardinality explodes. Collapsed to structural shape, the unclassified half is four buckets: **3,561** embedding calls (`similarity`/`librarian`/`librarian-write`), **1,868** `guardrails-check` rows, **1,407** function-calling-shaped agent turns, **179** fact-capture residue + misc. Every classified call is an `agent-turn` row; **zero** service rows classify.

**Two of those buckets are not vocabulary gaps, and finding that out is most of the value:**
- The **1,868 `guardrails-check`** rows are the duplicate half of an AI-51 pair — exactly 1,868 `agent-turn` rows carry `gated_subroutine_fired` and already match `output-guardrails`. Equal counts on both sides was the tell; confirmed by grouping on `ai_type`. A logging artifact, not a missing pattern.
- The **3,561 embedding** calls are a **settled decision, not a discovery.** Susan ruled on this 2026-07-22 (candidate `087368e3`, decision `merge`): *"Converting text to dense vectors for similarity search is a foundational technical operation, not a distinct system-design pattern… already explicitly covered as part of RAG."* `LOG-73` records John's acceptance of the consequence. **The design session had already proposed filing an embedding candidate and John had approved it** — checking `FEATURES.md`/`pattern_candidates` before writing caught that it would have re-litigated Susan's judgment and contradicted John's own call. That check is the reason nothing was written.

**What was real:** `LOG-136` (v7.0.87, migration `20260810181025`, 18:10 UTC) had activated Susan's Function Calling criteria hours earlier. That exposed the gap underneath — her criteria enumerates two literal tool names while her Round-1 reasoning names a general test (*"tool_calls must name the schema tool, not just delegate"*). Applying her own test generically — `traits.schema: true` AND `tool_calls` contains the row's own `intent` — found **1,492 unclassified agent turns across 17 intents**, including `qg-review-intent` (the quality gate), `reasoner-intent`, and Susan's own `pattern-vocabulary-review-intent`. Her enumeration also carried a dead value: `channel-intelligence:ci-answer-intent` matches 0 rows platform-wide.

**Susan's decision — `amend`, re-affirming the narrow scope unchanged.** She weighed a `GRAMMAR-LIMIT` discard against widening and chose neither, verbatim: *"Rather than GRAMMAR-LIMIT-discard a real pattern, I'm amending with the narrow ci-answer-intent scope you originally wrote, understanding this as a deliberate choice to keep Function Calling scoped to the CHI answer capability specifically—leaving other schema-emission turns unpattern'd or subject to future intent-specific patterns."* The gold row was verified **byte-identical** to its pre-session snapshot — a real decision that happens to write identical values, which is why the QA assertion was equality against the snapshot rather than "did the write succeed."

**Task 1 — the stale candidate, and why ordering mattered:** `d6527773` (S-LOG-135 Round 2) sat `pending` asserting her criteria *"matches ZERO rows platform-wide."* True for 13 minutes; `LOG-136` falsified it. Worse, its proposed remedy (`{"traits":{"schema":true}}`) is rejected by `validateCriteria()` — bare `traits` is not in `SIGNATURE_FIELDS`. Because `buildReviewContext()` passes every other pending candidate into the next review as `otherPendingCandidates`, leaving it would have injected a false premise into Task 2's own context. Resolved first, by appending a clearly-marked Round-3 correction (original text preserved verbatim, confirmed at QA) and letting Susan `discard` it on the corrected facts rather than stamping her name on a decision she did not make.

**QA (parent session, independent):** both candidates resolved with non-null reasoning and `reviewed_by: susan`; both calls logged (`ai_activity_log` 37868/37869, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `pattern-vocabulary-review:pattern-vocabulary-review-intent:depth0`); `function-calling` blast radius 594 unchanged; 28 gold rows / 11 with criteria unchanged; unclassified emission baseline 1,492→1,494, the delta being this session's own two governance calls. QA item 6 (live console run) accepted on direct DB evidence — the panel reads the same view the matcher re-run already exercised, and Susan's decline makes a blank `qg-review-intent` hop the expected state.

**Residue filed:** `LOG-139` (bucket-5 "if appropriate" call — 1,494 calls stay unclassified by decision; John's call, not more analysis) and `HAR-38` (John's home IP at $9.8669 of a $10.00 cap, sibling IP already `blocked` on `spend_cap`; `GATE_BYPASS_SECRET` unretrievable through any tool path).

**Process notes:** an audit session, not design or coding — worktree `audit-pattern-coverage-0810` on `session/audit-pattern-coverage-0810`, which does not match `session/design-*`, so no branch switch was needed before the automated spawn (Sonnet 5, per the kickoff's model line). The session's own lesson is the one above: **twice, a proposed action dissolved once the existing record was checked** — the embedding candidate (Susan had ruled) and the "stale-candidate blocker" (already fixed by `LOG-136`, residue not blocker). Both were caught by reading `FEATURES.md` and `pattern_candidates` before writing, which is `CLAUDE-DESIGN.md` Step 4.1's check doing exactly its job.

## 2026-08-11 — design-log-139-0811 / S-LOG-139 (v7.0.91) — 17 unnamed schema-emission shapes governed; the family cleared

**Origin:** John resolved `LOG-137`'s fork: the ~1,500 unnamed schema-emission calls were not accepted as pattern-less; Susan Smith — Trainer Agent's own pointer — intent-specific patterns — became the work. One candidate per intent, evidence-only (mechanism grounding via `parseModelTurn()`, fresh counts, sibling table, her `LOG-137` resolution quoted as provenance), names/criteria/maturity authored by nobody but her.

**What shipped (`ca598c7`, harvest doc only):** 17 candidates batch-filed after the Node gate passed, then reviewed sequentially oldest-first through her live `pattern-vocabulary-review` capability. **Rulings: 5 promote, 1 amend, 5 merge, 6 discard — 17/17 resolved, no-retry rule never triggered on a candidate.** One §19o checkpoint/resume `in_progress` on `ws-news-search-intent` completed via the documented `action: continue` path (zero altered content — not a retry). New gold rows: `structured-output-for-ui-rendering` (**14,076** rows platform-wide — the de facto classifier: criteria `traits.schema` + `generative` covers most of the schema-declaring population), `explicit-evidence-grounding-citation` (2,825), `output-quality-gate-evaluation` (1,937), `structured-decision-record` (274; widened 18 s later by the batch's own `amend` — the amend targeted the batch's own new row, so the 28 pre-session gold rows stayed byte-identical), `failure-driven-escalation-triage` (0 — dead).

**Closure gate, verified independently at QA:** the pinned family query returns **0 rows** — every one of the 17 shapes now classifies or carries a governed discard. The newest real `qg-review-intent` hop (row 37914) renders "Structured Output for UI Rendering" via `ai_call_patterns` — the exact view the Agent Patterns panel reads (browser check skipped on documented grounds: zero code changed this session; the view mechanism was live-console-proven in `S-LOG-133`/`S-LOG-136`). Platform unclassified: 25,580 → 19,419. Spend: $10.00 → $11.35 of $20.00, `trial` throughout, no block (`HAR-38`'s overnight cap raise held).

**The honest findings (filed as `LOG-140`, Post-beta):** 3 of the 5 promotes don't match their own founding evidence — one dead (`failure-driven-escalation-triage`, blast radius 0: its `gated_subroutine_fired` conjunct never co-occurs with `intake-failure-intent`), two live-but-misaimed (`output-quality-gate-evaluation` 1,937 rows none of them founders; `explicit-evidence-grounding-citation` 2,825 likewise). The harvest's §3.4 root-cause is directional, not incidental: **criteria built from fields the family query guarantees present landed safely both times; criteria reaching for fact-half signals Susan cannot verify (her authoring constraint forbids inspecting real log rows — deliberate, §19k's "the log must not shape the criteria") silently promote unmatchable.** Adjacent coherence residue: two candidates merged INTO `function-calling` whose narrow criteria excludes them (her own `LOG-137` narrowing), and one merged into an "umbrella" (`reasoner-intent`) that was itself discarded 21 s later — recorded, not smoothed over, per the `S-LOG-133` honesty precedent. Latent, not live-wrong: every founding hop renders ≥1 pattern via the broad row (verified), a dead row renders nothing, and the misaimed rows' labels are semantically arguable on the rows they DO match — hence Post-beta.

**QA (parent session, all independent):** 17/17 non-pending with `reviewed_by: susan` + non-null reasoning; per-pattern blast radii re-measured (matched the harvest); founding-row matches tested per promote (the 2-safe/3-misaimed split confirmed); amend's founder matches (row 33452); gold-row diff clean; spend after-state clean. The coding agent's chat summary transposed the discard/merge counts (said 5 discard/6 merge; DB says 6/5 — the harvest's own table is correct, DB authoritative).

**Bucket-5 consequence:** the "every agent displays ≥1 pattern in its hop — if appropriate" bar is now answerable per-hop from governance records, and currently every hop in the family renders at least one line. The bonus counter (re-classify below 10K) moved 25,580 → 19,419 — still above 10K, big step.

**Process notes:** worktree `design-log-139-0811` on `session/design-log-139-0811` (design-named branch was fine — the only repo write is `docs/`, which `SES-010`'s hook doesn't match; stated explicitly in the spawn prompt so the agent wouldn't switch).
